507685|2026-09.headline: Wipro Q2 FY27 IT services revenue flat QoQ at $2.61B; Q3 guided -1.5% to +0.5% CC sequential amid furloughs.
507685|2026-09.overview: IT services revenue was $2.61B, flat sequentially and up 0.6% YoY in constant currency, with operating margin at 16.5%, up 0.5% QoQ on operational improvements and rupee depreciation. TCV fell to $2.6B with nine large deals; management said two large deals slipped on paperwork and are expected to be signed in Q3. Net income declined 5% QoQ to INR32 billion as other income fell 68% after the June 2026 buyback completed, while EPS rose 0.9% QoQ to INR3.23. Q3 guidance is seasonally weak with furloughs and fewer working days.

-68% QoQ due to lower investable surplus after June 2026 buyback

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 IT services revenue guided to $2.571B to $2.625B, i.e. -1.5% to +0.5% sequential in constant currency.
Q3 impacted by seasonal furloughs; furlough impact expected broadly in line with last year and built into guidance.
Management expects Q4 revenue to benefit from closing the two slipped large deals; no full-year guidance, only quarterly.
Margin: management aims to keep improving margins but gave no timeline to return to the 17-17.5% target band; continued investment in AI Native Unit.
Salary hike effective 1 March 2026 has been rolled out; no further salary increase under consideration.
capex_capacity: AI Native Unit launched April 2026 with over 2,000 engineers, including forward deployed engineers, to drive outcome-based deals.
Five AI growth themes receiving accelerated investment: AI data centers, AI foundry services, physical AI, AI devices and design-to-manufacturing.
Headcount flat YoY; no campus hiring in H1, with campus hiring planned for H2 given volume growth; AI projects driving productivity.
Recent acquisitions HARMAN DTS (engineering, design-to-manufacture) and Mindsprint (food and agri, via Olam deal) cited as contributing capabilities.
demand_pricing: Demand environment described as largely unchanged; clients focused on efficiency while accelerating AI adoption.
Cost optimisation and vendor consolidation remain key drivers; BFSI and Tech named as likely growth leaders.
Deflation: management says contracts average 2 to 2.5 years and the renewal cycle of the last 1.5 to 2 years suggests an inflection in a few quarters.
Nine large deals closed in Q2 with a consulting-led AI transformation win at a global financial institution; mid-market consumer products win for an AI capability centre in India.
Health: first-time outsourcers emerging on cost pressure; US payer policy changes weighed on demand.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q2 TCV fall QoQ, and were numbers as expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two deals could not be signed on time in Q2 due to paperwork and will be signed in Q3; Q3 pipeline described as very robust.

qa_highlights.question: Will Wipro use its cash balance for large acquisitions as in the cloud wave?
qa_highlights.answer: Inorganic strategy is consulting-led and AI-powered in priority sectors; acquisitions will continue to be opportunistic, citing HARMAN DTS and Mindsprint as examples.

qa_highlights.question: Is Wipro not benefiting from BFSI recovery seen at peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a delayed mega-deal ramp now starting, a European BFSI client reversing captive insourcing, and Capco growth; BFSI and Tech named as likely growth leaders.

qa_highlights.question: Is the client-specific issue behind us and how much did the Alpha Net tuck-in and Mindsprint contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said client issues are largely behind, with most resolved in Q3. Mindsprint contributed one month of revenue via Olam deal; Alpha Net impact was not material and not quantified. Organic growth figure not separately disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to the 17-17.5% band by Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the goal is to improve margins quickly, with operational improvements offsetting investments in AI Native Unit, but no timeline was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q4 be a positive growth quarter and what drove the Q2 headcount reduction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 visibility improves if deals close early in Q3. Headcount was flattish YoY; the QoQ reduction reflects no H1 campus hiring, with H2 campus hiring planned.

risks_watch: Conversion of the two slipped large deals in Q3; failure would weaken Q4 revenue visibility.

Americas 1 continued decline and Americas 2 down 4.7% YoY; regional recovery not yet broad.

507717|2026-03.headline: Dhanuka Q4 FY26 revenue rose 9% to Rs 483.34 crore and PAT rose 30% to Rs 97.77 crore, helped by a one-off GST refund; FY27 guidance is low double-digit growth.
507717|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 483.34 crore vs Rs 442.02 crore (about 9% growth), with EBITDA of Rs 124.89 crore vs Rs 109.75 crore and PAT of Rs 97.77 crore vs Rs 75.50 crore. Management attributed the record EBITDA margin largely to a sharp rise in GST refund income in Q4 (Rs 14.5 crore of the Rs 29 crore full-year refund), and said Q4 value and volume growth were roughly equal. Management guided FY27 to low double-digit growth, with the Bayer-acquired molecules (India plus rest of world) and biostimulant recovery as the main offsets to the loss of GST refund and biostimulant disruption. Input costs rose 3-5% at basket level in March-April, with pass-through expected to be gradual and largely complete by Q2.

507717|2026-06.headline: Dhanuka Q1 FY27 revenue fell 12.56% YoY to Rs 461.93 crore; EBITDA Rs 55.01 crore and PAT Rs 36.30 crore, with FY27 growth guided to small single digits.
507717|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations declined about 12.56% YoY to Rs 461.93 crore from Rs 528.29 crore, with volume down about 12.7% and value down 12.56%, per management. Management attributed the quarter to delayed monsoon onset, a June rainfall deficit of about 40% (narrowing to 15% by end-July), weak herbicide demand in soybean and cotton states, and price erosion after a short-lived price hike. Management now expects a small single-digit growth in FY27 crop protection, versus the earlier guidance that was cut in the presentation. Biologicals, Bayer-acquired molecules and the Nagpur formulation plant (Rs 200 crore outlay, 23,000 MT) are the main forward-looking items.

qa_highlights.question: Why such a steep guidance cut, especially on top-line?

507717|2026-09.headline: Dhanuka Q2 FY27 revenue rose 9.91% to INR657.51 crore, but management reiterated only a low-single-digit full-year growth and ~100 bps gross margin loss.
507717|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew about 9.9% YoY to INR657.51 crore, with EBITDA of INR152.97 crore and PAT of INR109.22 crore, both up YoY. Growth was driven by insecticides (47% of revenue), which management attributed to El Niño-led product focus and channel agility rather than market share gains. Management said Q2 growth is not a run-rate: it expects low single-digit revenue growth for the full year, with Q3 and Q4 subdued and gross margin down about 100 bps. Analysts probed channel inventory, margin drivers, Dahej plant ramp-up and the new-product index, and management was specific on most points but declined product-level revenue figures.

segments.name: Zones (share of Q2 turnover)
segments.commentary: North 31%, East 12%, West 28%, South 29%. Analyst noted North grew about 22% in Q2 and about 12% in H1; management attributed North strength to irrigated markets.

segments.name: Product categories (share of Q2 revenue)
segments.commentary: Insecticides 47%, fungicides 25%, herbicides 8%, others 20%. Herbicides were hit by dry weather; insecticides grew strongly.

segments.name: Dahej (Harsh Dhanuka)
segments.commentary: Plant at about 70% utilisation per analyst; H1 sales about INR55 crore and H1 EBITDA loss about INR1.79 crore. Two new fungicide products planned in the existing plant, taking the portfolio from 2 to 4 products in FY28; capex amount not disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 revenue growth now guided at low single digit (management clarified this after earlier single-digit guidance; a Q2 growth of about 10% is not a run-rate for Q3 and Q4).
Gross margin expected to fall about 100 bps for the year, with EBITDA decline similar or slightly larger; management said margin expansion will not happen this year.
Q3 and Q4 described as subdued; management does not expect a high sales season in Q3.
Rabi season initial movement described as promising in certain regions; South and East zones are the key for Rabi.
Management said the GST refund effect on gross margin recurs every quarter; excluding it, gross margin is flat.
Biostimulant Dhanzyme Gold liquid formulation approved, launch planned for December 2026.
Dahej capacity expansion approved; new fungicides to be added in FY28. Capex quantum to be clarified in a later round.
Two plant growth regulator and growth influencer launches planned in Q3.
capex_capacity: Dahej plant at about 70% utilisation; capacity expansion of existing products approved along with 2 new fungicide products in the existing plant (FY28).
Capex quantum not disclosed; management said clarity will come in a later round but the company is 'absolutely committed' to capex.
Two R&D centres with NABL-accredited labs; partnerships with 10 multinational agrochemical innovators from Japan, Europe and the US.
Distribution footprint: over 10 million farmers reached via 6,500 distributors, 80,000-plus retailers and 40-plus warehouses.
demand_pricing: Q2 growth attributed to insecticides (LaNevo, Miyako, Mortar, Decis), plant growth regulators and nutritional products; management said this was product-specific, not market share gain.
Chilli in South and cotton (repeat insecticide sprays) and vegetables in East supported demand; fungicide demand was weak.

Generic crop pricing under severe pressure; management said tepid demand prevents full pass-through of raw material cost increases. Some raw materials fell in Q2 and others rose; increases passed on selectively.

Channel inventory described as optimal; company said it cleans channel monthly and did not front-load in Q1. Analyst asked about receivables jump; management said debtors are not aggressively placed and material is taken back quickly.

Farmer purchasing power constrained: commodity prices high but rainfall-dependent farmers reduced, per management; fertiliser e-Token and enforcement cited as reducing fertiliser-linked tagging of crop protection sales.
Polin (paddy fungicide from Nippon Soda, Japan) priced above market acceptance; not expected to scale near term.
Brazil and European subsidiaries are for registration only; customers appointed in about 14 countries, purchase orders in hand from 5.

qa_highlights.question: What drove about 10% growth in Q2 and was there regional share gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was product-specific insecticide growth from El Niño-driven re-planning, plus focus on water-available areas and no Q1 channel front-loading. Q2 growth is not an indicator for the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10% growth a run-rate, and will growth moderate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management maintained single-digit growth guidance for the year, saying Q2 growth reflects the weak base of last year's same quarter and is not indicative of Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is the strong North performance (about 22% in Q2) market share gain or industry-driven?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said North irrigated markets (Punjab, Haryana, Western UP) were industry's favourite; it would not confirm share gain.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin held despite lowest ITI and high-margin mix moderation: what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said gross margin was slightly lower YoY due to GST refund effects; EBITDA margin improved mainly from tighter other expenses. Value growth (10%) exceeded volume growth (6%).

qa_highlights.question: Full-year guidance: high single digit or double digit?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Dhanuka said the company will grow by a single low digit for the year, with gross margin down about 100 bps and EBITDA down similarly or slightly more.

qa_highlights.question: Will product-level revenue such as LaNevo be disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to share product-specific revenue, though it said LaNevo was a leading growth driver in Q2.

risks_watch: Full-year guidance cut to low single-digit growth; Q3 and Q4 subdued, with weak demand in the Western and Central regions where rain opportunity has ended.
Gross margin pressure of about 100 bps; competitors' high-cost inventory could pressure generic pricing in H2.
Dahej remains loss-making; capex quantum and timelines for the two new fungicides not yet disclosed.
Enforcement against unregistered and spurious products; industry-wide concern flagged, with FICCI involvement.
Rabi season performance in South and East zones is the key swing factor.
New-product index (ITI) moderation; Polin unlikely to scale near term, pipeline depends on Q3 PGR launches and Dhanzyme Gold December launch.
507717|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on Q2 execution and insecticide-led resilience, but cautious and explicit about H2: management repeatedly tempered the Q2 print and lowered full-year expectations. Evasive on product-level revenues and capex amounts.
key_quotes: This indeed is a product-specific growth from the domain of insecticides.
So this 10% growth is not an indication of what we can expect in other two quarters.
So about 100 bps less in gross margin.
I think so the position is that we'll be growing by a single low digit, and that is where we are.

507779|2026-03.headline: Kanpur Plastipack Q4 FY26 standalone PAT rose ~14% YoY to INR14.53 crore, but a INR3.65 crore DFIA income reversal cut other operating income to negative INR2.9 crore.
507779|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone total income was INR183.1 crore (up ~6.16% YoY), with EBITDA of INR25.06 crore (13.69% margin) and PAT of INR14.53 crore. FY26 total income rose 26.26% to INR726.67 crore, EBITDA reached INR74.75 crore (10.29% margin) and PAT was INR38.19 crore (up ~68%). Management attributed the Q4 hit to government suspension of import duty on polypropylene until 30 June, which removed the value of DFIA licences. Management guided to 10% top-line growth in FY27 with margins similar to current levels, and flagged a softer order book in the near term from customer inventory correction.

financial_highlights.value: INR3.65 crore; other operating income negative INR2.9 crore
INR112 crore (short-term borrowing INR78 crore, GECL loans INR23.8 crore, long-term loans INR9.01 crore)

segments.commentary: Commercial production targeted from September 2026 (machine 1) and December 2026 (machine 2). FY27 revenue guided at INR20-25 crore; FY28 at INR100-120 crore (one reference said INR100-125 crore) with 15-16% EBITDA margin. FY28 volume about 8,000-9,000 tonnes.

Non-woven: FY27 revenue INR20-25 crore with no loss expected; FY28 revenue INR100-120 crore at 15-16% EBITDA at steady state.

Raw material 'new normal' expected at USD1,200-1,350 per tonne versus USD1,000 earlier; DFIA income expected to resume once import duty suspension (till 30 June) ends, at about INR3-3.5 crore per quarter on average.

qa_highlights.answer: Unit 3 produced 100 tonnes in March 2026 at a 1,200 tpa run-rate; about 1,800 tonnes expected in FY27, exiting at 2,400 tpa. Full 6,000 tpa is worth about INR130 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 11% Q4 margin sustainable and what is FY27 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will sustain and gave 10-15% growth, later narrowed to about 10% top-line growth.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company have a price pass-through clause for Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, pass-through is per kg rather than percentage, so a rise in raw material cost lifts the percentage of RM in selling price (e.g. 50% rising to about 60% in the example).

qa_highlights.question: What is the DFIA reversal and its run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: The reversal covered income up to 31 December 2025, because the duty suspension wiped out licence value. DFIA averages about INR3-3.5 crore per quarter once it resumes.

qa_highlights.question: How much did ESSEKAN and non-woven contribute, and what are the margins?
qa_highlights.answer: ESSEKAN sales INR20-25 crore with Kanpur at a 20% markdown; both marketing JV and manufacturing expected at about 15% EBITDA. Non-woven FY28 target INR100-120 crore at 15-16% EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Asia's contribution low, and is Japan on the back burner?
qa_highlights.answer: Asia is price-competitive with local makers and shorter lead times; Japan is still a focus, with Tokyo Pack exhibition in Sept-Oct 2026, though China and Vietnam currently have cheaper PP.

qa_highlights.question: What is FIBC utilisation given sales of 14,352 tonnes?
qa_highlights.answer: Production was about 15,000 tonnes against 18,000 tpa installed, about 83% utilisation; management said real capacity is stitching-time based.

Order book softness in Q1-Q2 FY27 as customers buy smaller and more often; lead times down to 3-4 weeks.
Non-woven ramp-up: first revenue only from September 2026; 35% effective time availability in FY27 and 70% utilisation assumed; no OEM approvals yet, only trial and sampling orders.
Europe concentration at 56.5% of exports; North America share fell to 16%.
Labour skill and stitching-capacity constraints for the expanded FIBC capacity; Valex Ventures (UK) B2C business yet to show success; Japan entry delayed by Chinese PP pricing.

507779|2026-06.headline: Kanpur Plastipack Q1 FY27 standalone total income Rs 207.49 cr (first time above Rs 200 cr) and PAT up 112% YoY to Rs 12.14 cr, with EBITDA margin at 10.69%.
507779|2026-06.overview: Standalone total income crossed Rs 200 crore for the first time, up Rs 13.86 crore YoY, while EBITDA rose 58.98% to Rs 22.19 crore and margin widened to 10.69% from 7.66%. Average selling price rose 31% QoQ against an 18% rise in raw material prices, though management said employee cost increases of about Rs 3-3.5 crore per quarter absorbed part of the gain. FIBC volume fell to about 3,000 tonnes from 3,500 tonnes a year earlier, due to polymer and labour disruptions. The premium polypropylene Taslan yarn JV with Essegomma (Italy) started commercial production and sales, with volume ramp guided from Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Shubhi Gupta (Trinetra Asset Managers): How is raw material volatility from the West Asia conflict progressing, and can raw material moves be passed to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Polymer volatility has eased from about plus/minus 25% in March to plus/minus 10% now. Raw material changes are generally passed through with a lag of two weeks to one quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Shubhi Gupta: What is the marginal differential and expected EBITDA from the B2C-linked premium segments, and what total EBITDA margin should be expected for the company?
qa_highlights.answer: ESSEKAN is expected to add about Rs 10 crore revenue in FY27 at 20-25% EBITDA; non-woven B2C is guided to mid-double-digit EBITDA. Management would not give an exact company-wide margin guide but expects to sustain current levels.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor (Kapoor & Co): What is ESSEKAN's peak revenue on current capacity and when would more capacity be added?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity can reach about Rs 30 crore revenue. More capacity will be added once utilisation hits 50-60%, as the capex is not high.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: Why did margins not expand more despite the 31% ASP rise versus 18% raw material rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Manufacturing EBITDA margin was 12.6%. Employee cost rose about Rs 3-3.5 crore QoQ, FIBC manufactured volume fell due to supply chain and labour disruptions, and there were packing, oil, freight and one-time disruption costs. Energy costs were not a significant increase.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: What are the factors ahead for the rest of the year, and what are the FIBC capacity and mix plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Two risks: ocean freight rising from about $2,000 to $5,000 per container could dent demand, and partial sharing of costs with customers could hit margins. Target is 5,000 tonnes per quarter by Q1 FY28; management declined to give a product mix percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: What was the FIBC utilisation and is 3,000 tonnes the base for the year?
qa_highlights.answer: Volumes were 3,800 tonnes in Q3 FY26, 3,500 in Q4 FY26 and 3,000 in Q1 FY27, with working-day seasonality. Management called 3,000 a damaged number that will build from here.

qa_highlights.question: Chaitrika (individual investor): What is the long-term revenue aspiration and what are the milestones?
qa_highlights.answer: Current projects and installed capacity can take revenue to about Rs 900-950 crore in FY27-28 and Rs 1,000-1,050 crore in FY29, assuming current trading and polymer prices. Management will decide on deploying balance-sheet cash for further capacity next year.

qa_highlights.question: Yash Parker (individual investor): What tangible benefits have the UK (Valex) and Italian JV delivered, and when will financials show?
qa_highlights.answer: ESSEKAN sampling is under way with significant commercialisation expected in Q3 and Q4 FY27, with guidance on it by Q4. Valex has delivered no significant tangible benefit so far beyond brand awareness; its turnover is manufacturing-transferred, so profit sits within Kanpur Plastipack.

qa_highlights.question: Yash Parker: What annual savings come from renewable power, and what is the FIBC capacity ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Renewable power is about 60% of energy and already at the planned level, saving about Rs 3-5 crore a year. Battery storage is a couple of years away. FIBC adds about 1,200 tonnes a year, so 4-5 years to reach the full 6,000 tonnes.

qa_highlights.question: Yash Parker: What IRR and ROCE hurdles apply, and what working capital is needed as the business ramps?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-woven targets 15-20% IRR and ROCE above 20%; ESSEKAN returns are far higher given low capex. Working capital stays at similar levels for FIBC and raffia, while non-woven adds 30-40 days of working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Deeya Jain (Sapphire Capital): What are the realisation trends, and the ESSEKAN revenue targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Realisations track raw material and freight costs and should hold while raw material costs are steady. ESSEKAN is about Rs 10 crore in FY27, with an ultimate aim of Rs 100 crore in four years.

qa_highlights.question: Saket Kapoor: What is the impairment, contract value and debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: The Rs 25 lakh provision relates to a Rs 15 crore government (FCI) coating tender supply, taken as a prudent provision. 507789|2026-03.headline: Jagsonpal Q4 FY26 revenue rose 10% YoY to INR64 crores and PAT 31% to ~INR9 crores; MAT growth 12.2% vs IPM ~7-8%.

FY26 revenue grew about 7% to INR287 crores, while profit from operations grew 19% to about INR45 crores before the one-time labour code charge taken in Q3. The board announced a INR40 crore buyback at INR250 per share (no promoter participation) and a 200% dividend including a 75% special, together returning over INR66 crores. Management reiterated a target of 1.5x IPM growth, which it translates to 12-15% currently.

segments.name: Dermatology

Expects growth to get better over the next two quarters on Pharmarack-reflected numbers.

Dividend of 200% (INR4/share incl. 75% special), total cash outgo ~INR26 crores, subject to AGM approval.
Management said it can raise over INR200 crores of fresh debt and has balance-sheet capacity for acquisitions up to ~INR400 crores; an acquisition announcement is not yet made.
capex_capacity: MR headcount unchanged; no new MRs added in the last quarter. Growth to come from productivity of existing field force and geographies.
Asset-light model using CMOs; management says cost pressure is mainly packaging material and insurance costs, passed on over time under longer-term CMO agreements.
Price increases are SKU-based and taken after 12 months; ~92% of portfolio is outside NLEM price control, allowing up to 9.9% increase per management.
Strategic initiatives on field-force retention, internal promotions and MR upskilling are in progress.
demand_pricing: Pharmarack MAT (FY26) Jagsonpal growth 12.2% vs IPM ~8.5-9% (volume ~1-2%, new products ~3%, price ~5-7%); Q4 Jagsonpal 14.2% vs industry 10.5%. Management noted reported Pharmarack figure is 7% vs 12% on its mirrored basis, attributed to lead-lag.
Top 10 brands ~58-60% of sales; nine of them rank in top five in their categories. Growth of top 10 brands said to be in line with the rest of portfolio.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin and other expense trends in Q4?

qa_highlights.question: Will the 1.5x IPM target stand after the outperformance?

qa_highlights.question: Breakup of growth into price, volume and new products?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 industry: volume ~1%, new products ~3.1%, price ~4.8%. Jagsonpal: volume ~2%, new products ~3.2%, price 6-7%.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Q4 numbers a one-off and how is the portfolio diversifying?

507815|2026-03.headline: Gillette India FY26 sales rose 8% to ₹3,100 crore and PAT rose 23% to about ₹650 crore, with the company citing a ~300bps structural margin gain.
507815|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 (year ended March 31, 2026) sales of about ₹3,100 crore, up 8%, and PAT of about ₹650 crore, up 23%, attributed to productivity across cost buckets. Management said the topline slowdown was largely due to one-time export impacts from affiliate distribution changes, including the Bangladesh distribution agreement closure, and that domestic sales were growing quarter on quarter. The call focused on new launches (Gillette Guard 3in1, Gillette trimmers, Oral-B Sensitive), Venus growth, productivity, and raw material inflation linked to the West Asia conflict. Management gave no numerical FY27 guidance.

segments.name: Male grooming (Blades and Razors)
segments.commentary: Management says the category grows about 12% and Gillette remains market leader; male grooming offtake grew 8% in P6M and 12% in P12M. Gillette Guard grew double digit and premium razors grew in early teens.

segments.name: Female grooming (Venus)
segments.commentary: Venus contributes double digits to grooming and is growing upwards of 20%; female grooming overall is growing upwards of 20%. The focus is new-user growth in in-home hair removal.

segments.name: Manual oral care (Oral-B)
segments.commentary: Growing high single digits, driven by the Oral-B Sensitive range, which is growing double digit and is among the fastest growing segments in the category.

segments.name: Power oral care (Oral-B)
segments.commentary: Growing at roughly 1.5x this year and at double digits steadily; business has doubled in the last 3 years.

segments.name: Trimmers and appliances
segments.commentary: Four new Gillette trimmers launched about 2 months before the call; management expects the trimmers category to grow at early double digits.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 sales or margin guidance was given; management said it expects some challenges to continue in the near term.
Management aims to grow ahead of the male grooming category and keep balancing topline and bottom-line growth.
A multi-year savings and productivity plan is in place by business unit to support margins and offset input-cost inflation.
Management said it cannot comment on future margins but expects productivity to fund investment and provide cover against macro volatility.
Management expects growth may fluctuate in the mid-term; it sees India growing at 6.5% for the year.
capex_capacity: About 85% of products are manufactured domestically; finished goods are exported to more than 10 countries.
Bhiwadi manufacturing plant issue was resolved within a few days with zero supply-related shortfall, per management.
Management is constantly assessing the locally manufactured vs imported supply chain mix.
Supply 3.0 advance ordering now covers half of the business; over 2 million automated on-shelf availability checks are run daily.
demand_pricing: Gillette Guard 3in1 (launched about 2 months earlier): about 1 million razors sold in the launch month, distribution reached over 6 lakh stores, and a new copy reached 20 crore viewers in month 1.
Numeric distribution rose by a couple of points in FY26 for priority SKUs; premium Mach3 and Fusion distribution grew at mid-single digits for 3 years.
Gillette Guard added 20 million new users over the last 3 years.
Management said raw material costs were hit by crude up ~50% and resins up ~50%, with availability challenged; the company said it did not go out of stock.
Management said rural consumption remains higher than urban, but rural is softening because of inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Why was revenue growth subdued and volatile in FY26 and the March quarter, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one-time export impacts from affiliate-company decisions, including the Bangladesh distribution agreement closure, weigh on the base. Excluding them, growth would roughly double, and domestic sales are growing quarter on quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Are FY26 margin gains sustainable, and what about FY27 margins and raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said structural margins improved upwards of 300 bps through premium innovation and productivity. It would not comment on FY27 but said a multi-year savings plan is in place and it will keep mitigating inflation and freight overcharges.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth plan over the next 3 to 5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will double down on its five-vector integrated strategy: daily-use portfolio, superiority, productivity, constructive disruption and an enabled organisation. No numeric target was given.

qa_highlights.question: What are the growth drivers in Venus and female grooming?
qa_highlights.answer: Venus is double digit in grooming and growing upwards of 20%; the focus is new-user growth in in-home hair removal through influencers and myth-busting content. No Venus salience figure was disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the trimmers and appliances opportunity, and what share is targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Four trimmers were launched about 2 months before the call; the category is expected to grow at early double digits. Management aims to grow faster than the category but gave no share target.

qa_highlights.question: Was the Bhiwadi plant issue fully resolved, and were there supply challenges?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the issue was resolved within a few days, with zero supply-related challenges, and the stock exchange was alerted.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation: crude and resin up about 50%, with tight availability tied to West Asia conflict; the margin impact was not quantified.
Export revenue volatility from affiliate distribution changes, including the Bangladesh agreement closure.
Softening rural consumption and inflation-driven pressure on consumer spending.
Competition in men's shaving, which management acknowledged in Q&A without giving share data.
Next quarter: whether domestic growth and margin gains hold, and the early traction of Guard 3in1 and trimmers.

It deflected several quantitative questions (FY27 margins, share targets, Venus salience, the innovation pipeline) and said some information would be withheld as price sensitive.

rows.why: The Bangladesh distribution agreement closure is a one-time export drag on the base; management said excluding it growth would roughly double, but the closure itself is not reversing.

rows.label: Supply 3.0 advance ordering
rows.why: Supply 3.0 advance ordering now covers half the business and over 2 million automated on-shelf checks run daily, supporting availability through the input shortage.

508814|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 consolidated sales rose 37% to Rs 1,021 crore and EBITDA rose 53% to Rs 130 crore, with net debt cut to Rs 1,159 crore.
508814|2026-03.overview: Cosmo First reported Q4 FY26 consolidated sales of Rs 1,021 crore (up 37% YoY on 41% volume growth) and EBITDA of Rs 130 crore (up 53% from Rs 85 crore), helped by new BOPP/CPP capacity, specialty volumes and a Rs 7 crore EBITDA rise at the specialty chemical subsidiary. PAT growth was moderate due to higher depreciation and interest, a Rs 7.2 crore exceptional provision at a Netherlands subsidiary and a Rs 5.3 crore deferred tax asset reversal in South Korea. For FY26, revenue rose 26% and EBITDA rose 32% to Rs 479 crore. Management said the capex cycle is largely complete, net debt fell Rs 75 crore over six months to Rs 1,159 crore, and it expects double-digit topline growth in FY27.

segments.name: BOPP/BOPET films
segments.commentary: BOPP margin about Rs 20/kg in Q4 vs Rs 13/kg in Dec-25 quarter; BOPET about Rs 18/kg vs Rs 12/kg in Dec-25 quarter. Films are about 90% BOPP-CPP and about 10% BOPET; specialty films are about 60% of films in Q4 (56-57% for full year).

segments.name: Specialty chemicals (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 sales Rs 54 crore with 25%+ EBITDA; FY26 sales Rs 204 crore. Value growth was about 10% because raw-material-linked pricing was lower, though volume grew about 20%.

segments.name: Cosmo Plastech (rigid packaging)
segments.commentary: Q4 topline up over 70% YoY; reached EBITDA breakeven in Q4 with a small PBT loss likely. FY26 turnover about Rs 92 crore. Management targets high single-digit EBITDA in FY27 and mid-to-high teens in FY28.

segments.name: Zigly (petcare)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 topline up 54% YoY; annualised run rate about Rs 90 crore. Plan to move it into a separate subsidiary in FY27, with possible external capital.

segments.name: Cosmo Consumer (window films, PPF, ceramic coatings)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs 23 crore; exit annualised run rate about Rs 38 crore. Gross margin expected at 35-40%; still loss-making due to brand marketing. Management says at least two years to profitability and targets Rs 100 crore revenue first.

guidance_outlook: FY27 topline to grow in double digits, driven by utilisation of BOPP/CPP capacity added in FY26 and new businesses.
No EBITDA guidance given; management cited industry-cycle uncertainty but expects decent margins from new businesses, specialty growth and the US subsidiary.
Film volume growth potential of 15-20% from existing capacity; chemicals potential about Rs 100 crore more revenue; Plastech potential 30%; Cosmo Consumer at about 20% utilisation.
Capex for FY27 expected below Rs 100 crore; investment in Plastech, Consumer and Zigly about Rs 50-75 crore over next year and the year after.
Net debt to fall further; target to bring debt below 2x EBITDA within 12-18 months (currently 2.4x).
US tariff refund of more than Rs 60 crore expected over 6-12 months, partly payable back to customers; flows to both P&L and cash flow. Management expects Q1 FY27 to be better than Q4 FY26.
Operating cost (employee and other) expected to hold at Q4 run-rate plus inflation in FY27.
Dividend of Rs 4 per share recommended for FY26, subject to shareholder approval.
risks_watch: BOPP/BOPET spreads remain volatile as 7-8 new Indian BOPP lines arrive over three years; possible short-term core-film oversupply.
Speciality pricing lag (one to three months) can compress margins during raw material price swings.
Cosmo Consumer and Plastech still loss-making at PBT level; Cosmo Consumer will keep losing money in FY27 as marketing continues.
Net debt of Rs 1,159 crore (2.4x EBITDA) and potential interest-rate pressure from inflation; deleveraging target below 2x within 12-18 months.
Timing and size of US tariff refund (above Rs 60 crore, partly payable to customers) remains uncertain.
Management gave no quantitative EBITDA guidance and called the outlook highly uncertain.

Rs 5.3 crore, South Korea subsidiary reorganisation

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 33 crore FY25; sales Rs 204 crore, 25%+ EBITDA margin
Down Rs 75 crore in last 6 months

qa_highlights.question: What is the industry outlook for BOPP and BOPET prices and spreads in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins may stay volatile as new capacity comes, though it sees a macro demand-supply balance. It said the company controls mix and cost, specialty films are 60% of films, and it is the lowest-cost producer in India.

qa_highlights.question: Is the employee and other cost base likely to keep rising after FY26 (employee expenses Rs 250 crore in FY25 vs Rs 336 crore in FY26)?
qa_highlights.answer: Costs should be held at the Q4 FY26 run rate plus normal inflation, and should fall as a percentage of sales as volumes grow.

qa_highlights.question: How much is the Plastech and Cosmo Consumer losses and when do they reach PBT break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Plastech reached EBITDA breakeven in Q4 with a possible small PBT loss; targets high single-digit EBITDA in FY27 and high-to-mid teens in FY28. Cosmo Consumer will keep losing money in FY27 due to marketing and needs at least two years to profitability.

qa_highlights.question: Why did specialty chemical growth slow to about 9-10% in FY26 against about 20% in prior years?
qa_highlights.answer: Value growth was about 10% because raw-material-linked prices were lower, while volume grew about 20%. EBITDA rose from Rs 33 crore to Rs 53 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 capacity utilisation across lines?
qa_highlights.answer: Full-year utilisation is 80-85%, with 15-20% volume headroom in films, about Rs 100 crore revenue headroom in chemicals, 30% in Plastech and about 20% utilisation in Cosmo Consumer.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt outlook and interest cost guidance amid possible rate hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt is expected to fall further, with FY27 capex below Rs 100 crore. Management aims to bring net debt/EBITDA below 2x within 12-18 months from 2.4x. It gave no interest-cost guidance.

508814|2026-06.headline: Cosmo First Q1 FY27 consolidated sales rose 46% to Rs 1,166 crore and EBITDA 26% to Rs 147 crore, though margin fell to 12.6%.
508814|2026-06.overview: Revenue growth was driven mainly by raw material pass-through after the West Asia conflict, with volume up only 9%. EBITDA rose 26% to Rs 147 crore, helped by better per-kg contribution across base, semi-specialty and specialty films, and management says all B2B businesses are now profitable. Export volumes fell 13% due to port congestion and a line maintenance outage, and BOPET margins compressed sharply sequentially. Net debt was flat at Rs 1,166 crore (2.3x EBITDA), and management targets below 2x within 12 months.

segments.name: BOPP films (base, semi-specialty, specialty)
segments.commentary: Specialty sales volume up 12% YoY; specialty mix at 61%, highest in five quarters, with target of 70%. Gross margin Rs 30/kg including non-repeating stock gain; management said base BOPP margin ex-stock gain was broadly flat.

segments.name: BOPET films
segments.commentary: Gross margin fell to Rs 9/kg from Rs 18/kg in Q4 FY26. Capacity is 30,000 tonnes against 277,000 tonnes of BOPP. Management expects margins to recover after recently levied anti-dumping duty.

segments.name: US film business
segments.commentary: Export volumes down 13% due to port congestion and in-transit shipments. US subsidiary received about USD 7 million duty refund in July 2026, not yet appropriated. Management expects US revenue to grow 25-30% in FY27.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue up 34% YoY with 25% EBITDA margin, improved 2 percentage points QoQ. About 80% of business is backward integration into group films. FY27 growth guided at about 50%; Rs 400-500 crore FY30 target may be reached by FY29.

segments.name: Cosmo Plastech (rigid packaging)
segments.commentary: Revenue up over 58% YoY and turned EBITDA positive. FY26 revenue about Rs 100 crore; FY27 guided Rs 150-160 crore and Rs 200+ crore next year, with capacity up 50% at minimal capex over next two quarters.

segments.commentary: Monthly GMV run rate about Rs 100 crore (annualised Rs 100 crore, per the call). Gross margin 47%, services 64% of sales mix, private label revenue up 105% YoY, 47 centres, 29,000 customers in the quarter. Management estimates breakeven at about Rs 250 crore revenue, a couple of years away.

segments.commentary: Near EBITDA breakeven in Q1. Revenue grew 4.5x last year and management expects more than 3x this year. Margin about 25% (EBIT per management, up from 15-17% at launch); gross margin target 35-40%. TV advertising began July 2026; 150 dealers in 100+ cities.

segments.name: Publication (state boards)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue of INR719 crore, stable. Management expects a curriculum change in Maharashtra and Gujarat over FY27-FY29 and about 15% growth in a single year; FY27 publication EBIT margin guided at least 200 bps above FY26.

segments.name: Domestic stationery (YOUVA brand)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR366 crore, +4% value on +6% volume. Management guides about 15% growth in FY27 and a normalised EBITDA margin of about 9% in FY27 (post brand spend), against about 13% historically.

segments.name: Export stationery
segments.commentary: Revenue down 10% in FY26 on US tariffs; divisional EBITDA margin down about 3 pp; a 4% favourable FX cushion was passed through as price cuts. Management guides single-digit to higher single-digit growth (8-9%) for FY27 and says no cancellations have been received.

segments.name: Indiannica (CBSE subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Sales fell to INR42 crore from INR55 crore with a INR16 crore PAT loss, due to stopped new category creation and higher returns. Merger into Navneet is pending regulatory approval.

guidance_outlook: FY27 domestic stationery revenue growth about 15%; subsequent year higher.
FY27 export stationery growth guided at 8-9%, conservative; long-term export growth about 15% possible in normal conditions.
Publication revenue growth of about 15% in a single year during the FY27-FY29 curriculum change; FY27 publication margin at least 200 bps above FY26.
Stationery EBITDA margin about 9% in FY27 post brand spend, and 9.5-10% in the following year, versus about 13% normally. Full-year margin impact from export price cuts expected to be under 100 bps.
Brand spend of about INR30 crore in FY27 and about INR40 crore in FY28; no price premium expected to offset it.

Capex: UAE manufacturing project on hold, so limited spend; India capex about INR25-30 crore in FY27. Southern Gujarat plant cost INR65 crore including land; asset turn 1x in year one, at least 2x in year two, about 2.5x thereafter.
capex_capacity: Southern Gujarat plant: INR65 crore invested including land; mainly plastic-based products for domestic and export markets; plastic export products currently outsourced will move in-house.
Paper capacity utilisation about 80% annually (three months of very low volume due to seasonality); outsourcing used heavily.
Non-paper categories to be initially outsourced under the brand and packaging, with capex deferred category by category.
UAE manufacturing project placed on hold due to geopolitical tensions; very limited investment made so far; may resume depending on the situation.
India capex in FY27 expected at only about INR25-30 crore, with no major land, building or machinery plans.
demand_pricing: Export orders: management says there are no cancellations; back-to-school volumes were finalised Nov-Feb. Price cuts given during the tariff period are being reversed.
Domestic: 6% volume growth achieved despite falling paper prices and price competition from unorganised regional players, which forced price cuts.
Paper prices rose about 8% from the lowest level in the last year; management doubts mills can raise prices for at least the next 3-4 months.

Publication: no curriculum change in Maharashtra/Gujarat since FY18 explained flat revenue; shift of customers to central board and lower per-customer spend also cited. Secondhand book market and trade inventory disappear with curriculum change.
Inflation in developed markets, including the US, is a risk to export buyers; management is haircutting growth by 5-7% for conservatism.

qa_highlights.question: Are export customers cancelling or cutting volumes, and will margins return to last year's levels?
qa_highlights.answer: No cancellations; volumes intact. Price cuts are reversed; only the first two months were affected, so full-year margin impact is under 100 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Why the shift to aggressive domestic branding, and what is the spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-paper categories need brand awareness to scale quickly. About INR30 crore in year one and about INR40 crore in year two, under the YOUVA brand; no price premium expected.

qa_highlights.question: What are the South Gujarat plant economics?
qa_highlights.answer: INR65 crore invested including land. Asset turn 1x in year one, 2x in year two, about 2.5x thereafter; beyond that, more machinery is needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did publication margin fall in H2 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Seasonal buying shifts between halves, inflation with no revenue growth, and a leave-encashment provision under the new labour code. Paper prices were favourable in H1 and not in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Indiannica revenue decline, and is it being merged?
qa_highlights.answer: Stopped creating new categories and higher returns reduced sales to INR42 crore. Merger into Navneet is planned to cut duplicate costs and share distribution; awaiting approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Are there plans for a demerger or buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: No demerger plans, since the stationery numbers are not large enough. On buyback, management said about three buybacks have been done in the last five years and they may revisit at the right time.

Indiannica merger approvals, integration and losses; CBSE penetration is still an open question for analysts.

508989|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue fell slightly to Rs 785 crore as curriculum-led Publication offtake slipped into Q2; FY27 Publication growth guided to ~10%.
508989|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue was Rs 785 crore, slightly lower YoY, with Publication down 3% to Rs 405 crore and Stationery up 2% to Rs 380 crore. Late release of state textbooks in Maharashtra and Gujarat pushed Publication sales into July (Q2), so management argues the shortfall is timing rather than loss. Export Stationery fell about 9% in the quarter and full-year export guidance was cut to around -5%, while Domestic Stationery grew 26%. Management guided Publication growth to about 10% for FY27, below the earlier ~15% expectation, and Stationery margin to about 8-10% amid brand investments and under-utilisation of a new polymer plant.

segments.name: Publication
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs 405 crore (-3%) due to late state textbook release in Maharashtra and Gujarat; FY27 growth guided ~10% (earlier ~15%); margin guided 26-27% (later cited ~10% for year). Management said no MRP increase in FY27, so growth is all volume.

segments.name: Domestic Stationery
segments.commentary: Grew 26% in Q1 on brand association, new cover designs, and e-commerce and quick commerce; FY27 growth guided 15-17%. Brand spend and senior hiring for non-paper vertical pressured short-term profitability.

segments.name: Export Stationery
segments.commentary: Down about 9% in Q1 on US demand weakness, supply-chain and geopolitical disruption, and missed back-to-school orders; FY27 guidance cut to about -5% from high single-digit growth guided in May. New polymer plant ran at ~30% utilisation (Rs 65 crore investment), causing under-absorption.

segments.name: Indiannica
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue Rs 3 crore and PAT of Rs (-7) crore; seasonal business.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs 30-35 crore would have been earned in Q1 without curriculum change; this shifts to Q2 plus curriculum-driven growth. Q2 Publication expected at Rs 130+ crore vs Rs 91 crore in Q2 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 Publication growth outlook and does competition from coaching and EdTech content threaten it?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance ~10% for FY27 given Q1 uncertainty; management said more than 10% possible. Competition seen mainly in higher grades and is not comparable on price; primary-level changes limit that threat.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Export Stationery guidance move from high single-digit growth to about -5%?

qa_highlights.answer: Growth driven by paper stationery, brand association, packaging and e-commerce/quick commerce; non-paper product refresh done, new categories by year-end, target 10-15% share in 3 years. Price/volume split not disclosed.

509079|2026-03.headline: Gufic Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 23% YoY to INR252 crore with EBITDA margin at 17.7%, while FY26 PAT fell to INR63.2 crore.
509079|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter in company history, with revenue of about INR252 crore (vs INR205 crore in Q4 FY25), EBITDA of INR44.7 crore (17.73% margin vs 13.17%) and PAT of INR20.5 crore (vs INR8 crore). Full-year revenue rose to INR940.5 crore (from INR820 crore), but EBITDA margin eased to 16.26% and PAT fell to INR63.2 crore from INR69.9 crore, reflecting Indore fixed costs, a domestic critical-care working-capital reset worth about INR22 crore of revenue, and higher overheads. Indore reached EBITDA breakeven in Q4 at about 30% capacity utilisation, as committed. Management guided to about 15% revenue growth in FY27, around 18% EBITDA margin for FY27, and gross debt held at about INR400 crore.

segments.name: Indore (CMO / complex injectables)
segments.commentary: Reached 30% capacity utilisation by year-end as targeted and EBITDA breakeven in Q4. 40 tech transfers complete, 27 under development; 200-plus state FDA approvals; more than 20 Indian pharma companies use it as CMO base. Management expects Indore margin of about 31-32% at full utilisation, with overall Indore margin around 20%.

segments.name: Navsari (existing plant)
segments.commentary: Management said Navsari margin was about 20% and expects it to settle at 18-18.5% as costs rise. Navsari is building cartridge and pen GLP-1 capabilities.

segments.name: Domestic / Critical Care
segments.commentary: About 48-50% of revenue. Hospital direct-billing receivables of 140-150+ days were reset to CFA/stockist distribution, costing about INR22 crore of revenue across Q2-Q4 FY26; collections now essentially complete. Critical care growth guided at 6-8%, maximum 9%, before new launches.

segments.name: Women's health (fertility and gynaecology)
segments.commentary: Strongest year ever. Gonadotropin flagship hit its highest annual sales; a hormone launched two years ago beat its annual target and was ranked among top new launches by IQVIA. IVF expected to grow at a decent rate, with recombinant launches planned over the next two years.

segments.name: Aesthetics (botulinum toxin and fillers)
segments.commentary: Claimed the number 2 botulinum toxin brand in India at about 23% share. Toxin is about 3.5% of revenue. A Canadian in-licensed filler is targeted for launch in Q3 or Q4 FY27, India only.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Record FY26 international business. Shifting from distributor-led model to holding marketing authorisations (Gufic Ireland for EU), with direct supply, out-licensing and tech transfer income. Exports about 20-22% of revenue. Approvals in Myanmar, Philippines, South Africa, Colombia, Germany, Ecuador in Q4; dossiers filed in 18 countries.

segments.name: CMO
segments.commentary: About 18-19% of revenue, boosted this year by GLP-1 contract work. Management guides to about 15-18% at peak. GLP-1 revenue not quantified.

segments.name: Nutraceutical and Ayurveda
segments.commentary: Focus on pain, arthritis and GI chronic therapies; a first-in-India formulation launched in heritage orthopaedic brand in Q4. No financials disclosed.

qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed gross margin gains to domestic and international reset, new launches and moving to more profitable geographies, guiding 0.5-1% YoY improvement.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GLP-1 work a confirmed contract and how big could it be?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a CMO role with partners, too premature to quantify, and not in prior projections.

qa_highlights.question: Why was INR6.5 crore invested in a cooperative bank?
qa_highlights.answer: Saraswat Bank relationship of over 15 years; investment earns about 15% dividend vs about 8% borrowing cost. Total exposure about INR250 crore across fund-based, non-fund-based and term loans. Shares can be sold back at face value.

qa_highlights.question: Is Gufic participating in GLP-1 (semaglutide) under its own brand, and has third-party CMO revenue started?

qa_highlights.question: How does the shift in international model (distributor-led to own-registration, field-force led) change economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is moving to own field force in Africa, Southeast Asia and South Asia once registrations and scale allow, aiming to lift margins from 40-50% under distributor models by 15-20% or more. A regional team was recruited in Q1 (one person in Mexico, one in the Philippines, two in Mumbai); the company also says it is building IP and trademarks in these markets.

qa_highlights.question: When will Indore get EU certification and does margin expansion follow, and is 18% the new normal margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Navsari already holds EU certification. The Indore EU certificate is awaited, with feedback expected in about one to two months; a US partner has also filed from the site. Indore utilisation was 18-22% last year, 20-25% the year before, and close to 30-35% this year, targeted at 40-45% by year-end. Management said the 18% margin is the start of an improvement trend rather than a new normal, and that the earlier 18% period had Indore costs, depreciation and interest capitalised.

qa_highlights.answer: The Indian filler market is estimated at about INR200 crore. Launch is expected around December-January, after registration in Q2 or mid-Q3. Management gave no first-year revenue number and aims to move from number 2 to number 1 in toxin plus fillers within 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is 15-20% growth conservative, and can growth go beyond 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15-20% year-on-year company growth is a bare minimum, with efforts aimed at growing beyond it. Some low-yielding product mix is being squeezed out, and it was not conservative in that guidance.

qa_highlights.answer: Roonghta first put FY27 expected revenue at about INR1,100 crore, with 15% annual growth taking it to about INR1,600 crore on existing facilities. Pranav Choksi said Navsari is capped at about INR800 crore, with toxin and penem not saturated, and Indore could add INR800-1,200 crore on about INR300 crore capex. The combined no-capex figure was cited as INR1,600-1,800 crore, and the total maximum as INR1,600-2,000 crore. The INR2,700 crore figure was not confirmed.

qa_highlights.answer: Most additions are at Indore, with about 50-60 people for domestic expansion, while international headcount is capped at 20-25. Employee cost growth is in line with the company's overall growth.

509152|2026-03.headline: GRP Q4 FY26 EBITDA fell to INR 94 million (7% margin) from INR 331 million as EPR income, exports and raw-material costs weighed.
509152|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income declined 10% YoY to INR 1,450 million, with the prior-year base inflated by INR 305 million of EPR gains versus INR 66 million this quarter. FY26 total income fell about 3% to INR 5,380 million and EBITDA dropped to INR 429 million from INR 694 million, with adjusted PAT of INR 46 million after a INR 14 million Labour Code charge. Export volumes fell about 15% while domestic volumes grew nearly 10%, and raw-material inflation reached 43% in certain SKUs. Management said the Pyrova (pyrolysis) and rCB platforms are still stabilising, and that the revised pricing from April 2026 passes through the full raw-material impact.

qa_highlights.question: Did pyrolysis oil realisations improve with high crude prices, and will this continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Some benefit in March; Q1 FY27 realisations are marginally above Oct 2025-Feb 2026, but road-construction demand is weaker, so volumes are affected.

qa_highlights.question: What is the recovery trend in exports and order inflows, and have RM costs stabilised?
qa_highlights.answer: North American direct volumes are largely recovered and the order book is stronger than most of FY26. Revised pricing from April 2026 captures the full raw-material cost increase.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY26 capex breakup, and what is the feedback on TPO and the new reclaim technology?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about 50% Pyrova, 30-35% RR and about 15% other. TPO is in validation for industrial furnaces, with petchem approvals longer. A second new-technology RR line will be added by end Q1 FY27, taking capacity to about 700 t/month from about 350 t/month.

qa_highlights.answer: Pyrolysis EPR accrual awaits PCB approvals, expected within weeks, with retrospective accrual in Q1 or Q2 FY27. Credits accrue at about 0.8 weightage with about 1.5x conversion; the mix of crumb, char and TPO is not yet disclosed.

qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated close to 20%+ revenue growth for FY27, driven by Pyrova Energy, Reclaim capacity and order book, and plastics scaling. It said the Q1 margin is not one-time and should keep improving, but it did not give a separate gross margin number.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rCB project status, including customer trials, expected revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: The first pyrolysis phase was commissioned in October 2025 and stabilised by March 2026. The rCB plant starts commissioning in August 2026 and is targeted for October 2026. Meaningful contribution is expected from Q4 FY27. Pyrova can reach 18-20% EBITDA margin once rCB is mature, subject to customer approvals; FY28 is seen as the maturity year.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 27% growth in engineering plastics volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was mainly automotive OE demand for nylon, with early appliance approvals from Q4 FY26 contributing some commercial volume. Polyolefin revenue grew but volumes were flat because customer selection was tightened, with a push into specialty polyolefin sectors.

qa_highlights.question: How much has rubber inflation risen over the past year, and when will prices stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to predict how long rubber inflation will last. Revenue grew about 30% against 12% volume growth, so the balance is price, largely passed to customers with a lag because contracts reset quarterly, half-yearly or annually. Prices are not expected to reverse soon given El Nino and oil-linked synthetic rubber.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 and FY28 capex plans, and what is the deleveraging plan?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is INR90-100 crore, covering two more pyrolysis lines to reach 45 KTA, the rCB plant and reclaim debottlenecking. FY28 capex will be decided in 2H FY27. About INR100 crore of the INR250 crore plan remains. Deleveraging timing is not in management's control, and there are no firm plans, though it would be needed to accelerate the Gujarat expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Are customers shifting toward sustainability-led material solutions rather than buying on price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a combination of value and sustainability. Reclaim is increasingly considered an alternative to virgin rubber given synthetic rubber and carbon black supply-demand mismatches. In plastics, regulation drives conversion and cost drives adoption.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the recovery is demand normalisation versus share gains, and is the export order book back to pre-tariff levels? What is the sustainable EBITDA margin, and when does Pyrova become EBITDA positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports rose 20%, mostly North America, with early Europe contribution. Domestic market share is up about 1% YoY, and export share is flat overall but higher in focus geographies. Pyrova crossed a 25-day monthly continuous run with a 4-day shutdown in July 2026. Management did not give a date for EBITDA breakeven. Stand-alone EBITDA margin targets are Reclaim 10-14%, Pyrova 15-20% and plastics 12-15%.

509675|2026-03.headline: BirlaNu Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 9% YoY to Rs 1,010 crore; standalone EBITDA margin up ~380 bps, but Parador impairment of Rs 74 crore hit standalone books.
509675|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a transition year, with subdued demand, pricing pressure and Middle East-driven volatility. Q4 improved: consolidated revenue grew 9% YoY to Rs 1,010 crore and standalone EBITDA margin expanded about 380 bps, helped by a Rs 5 crore Clean Coats dividend and resin price spikes in March. Full-year consolidated revenue was Rs 3,730 crore (+3%), while standalone EBITDA rose 39% to Rs 146 crore, aided by Rs 22 crore Clean Coats dividend and Rs 7 crore asset-sale profit. A Rs 74 crore diminution provision on the BirlaNu International GmbH (Parador) investment was booked as an exceptional item in standalone accounts, and Parador posted a Rs 35 crore operating loss in Q4 including a Rs 19 crore severance provision. Total debt was Rs 851 crore at year-end, down from Rs 929 crore in December.

509820|2026-03.headline: Huhtamaki India Q1 FY26 EBITDA up 24.8% YoY on mix and efficiency; sales up only ~10 bps, EBIT hit by INR 88 mn prior-period depreciation charge.
509820|2026-03.overview: Management reported sales broadly flat (up about 10 bps YoY) with EBITDA up 24.8% YoY, attributed to higher-value sales mix and operational efficiency. Reported EBIT was about INR 386 mn after a one-off INR 88 mn depreciation charge for prior two years (WDV instead of SLM error), with EBIT margin ex-charge at about 8% (27.8% EBIT margin ex-charge is stated in the call and appears to be an inconsistent figure relative to the 8% quoted). Reported PAT of about INR 256 crore was roughly 2% lower YoY; management said it rose about 23.1% excluding the prior-year charge. Raw material costs rose sharply from end-March on the Middle East conflict; management said most of the increase was passed through to customers, with low-to-medium double-digit RM impact.

capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation not disclosed; management said capacity is not a constraint and there is 'a lot of room to grow'.
Solar captive electricity project at Khopoli plant under execution, expected to go live within months.

Zero liquid discharge status at Khopoli, Rudrapur and Silvassa; plans to extend to other plants.
Property in Daman put up for sale after curtailing operations there.
demand_pricing: Raw material costs (films, paper) rose from end-March 2026 with volatility; management estimated low-to-medium double-digit RM impact on products overall, and said availability is not an issue.
Pricing: India was among the first regions to pass through costs; by end-March almost all future orders were locked at new prices, with contracts allowing pass-through.
Customers came with panic-driven volume requests during the conflict; management said demand has since stabilised with no significant change.
Competition: large multinational customers grow slowly; smaller regional Indian players grow faster. Management said it is not chasing low-value volume.
Analyst cited annual report reference to Indian flexible packaging growing 10-12%; management said the comparison is not like-for-like because the definition includes paper.

qa_highlights.question: What is the raw material cost impact post-war and is availability an issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Prices rose from end-March and are volatile; low-to-medium double-digit RM impact overall. Availability is not an issue given global procurement, though shipments from overseas can be delayed. Most costs passed to customers.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments are seeing demand post-war and how is cost affecting demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers initially over-ordered in panic, then volumes stabilised. No significant demand change; large FMCG customers grow 2-5%, regional customers faster.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company losing share given the 10-12% market growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the market includes multinationals and smaller regional Indian players growing faster; the company is selective and focused on innovation and premium customers, so growth is in line with its value proposition. Amit Gupta said the market definition includes paper and is not comparable.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the jump in other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest on an income tax refund (about INR 6.5 crore), higher FD interest, and FX gains on exports from rupee weakness. Management said several one-offs offset this.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the rise in other expenses from INR 95 crore to INR 106 crore QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the increase is not substantial, expense ratios are declining as a percentage of sales, and the one-offs include provision reversals and the INR 88 mn depreciation charge plus a property charge.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the INR 100 crore ECB repayment to the parent extended from Feb 2026 to June 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: The ECB loan from the parent follows RBI tenure guidelines; part has been repaid and the balance is payable by June 2027. Servicing cost is linked to FD returns, so no negative impact, per management.

509820|2026-06.headline: Huhtamaki India Q2 CY26 net sales rose 23.1% to INR723 crore and EBITDA margin widened to 10.5% from 8.3%, with PBT up 77%.
509820|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q2 net sales of INR723 crore, up about 23% YoY, with growth split roughly evenly across price, volume and product mix and broad-based across exports and domestic. EBITDA margin expanded to 10.5% from 8.3%, and PBT rose 77% to INR559 crore, with EPS up about 77%. H1 sales grew close to 12% and H1 EBIT margin was hit by a one-time INR8.8 crore prior-period depreciation charge; excluding it, EBIT margin was 7.6%. Management attributed the quarter to pricing pass-through of Middle East-driven raw material inflation, a healthy portfolio mix and productivity, plus some customer inventory build-up that it said would partly reverse.

Home care and liquid categories growing faster than food and beverage in India; late monsoon boosted beverage season.

509820|2026-09.headline: Huhtamaki India Q3 net sales rose about 24% to INR748 crore with volume up about 7%, while reported PAT fell 19% to INR30 crore on a one-time Baddi charge.
509820|2026-09.overview: Net sales reached about INR748 crore, up roughly 24% YoY and the highest quarterly sales in the last couple of years, with growth split across pricing pass-through, mix and volume. Reported EBIT was flat YoY because the prior-year quarter had one-time retirement-related gains; management says like-for-like EBIT margin is about 8% and EBITDA improved about 18% on a comparable basis. PAT fell 19% to about INR30 crore (from INR37 crore) after a INR96 million charge for closing the Baddi labels plant, with volumes moved to Ambernath and Bangalore. Nine-month sales grew about 16%, EBITDA about 25% to INR204 crore (margin about 10% vs 9.2%), and PAT about 13%.

segments.name: Flexible packaging
segments.commentary: Growth attributed to pricing pass-through of raw material inflation, mix shift to higher-value products and about 7% volume growth in Q3. Management says roughly one-third each from price, mix and volume, though exact split not given.

segments.name: Labels (pressure-sensitive)
segments.commentary: Baddi labels plant closed (about two months' notice, closing around the call date); volumes moved to Ambernath and Bangalore plants. Management says Baddi was the smallest plant by output and headcount and was not profitable.

guidance_outlook: No formal margin or full-year forecast given; management says it does not disclose forecasts.
Management aspires to grow every quarter and year and to keep improving margins, contingent on market conditions.
Sees no major capex needed for the next 2-3 years to meet demand, as productivity gains free up capacity.
Q3 EBITDA margin dip attributed to raw material cost spike in late September not passed through in the same month; expected to be recovered in following months.
capex_capacity: Baddi labels plant closed in Q3 with a INR96 million one-time charge; volumes shifted to Ambernath and Bangalore, which management says have spare capacity.
Solar captive generation at Khopoli started in August (Q3), lifting renewable electricity share to 23%.
Daman land is held for sale; bids being evaluated, no price disclosed, and sale to be disclosed to the market when concluded.
Management says no significant investment needed for next 2-3 years to meet demand; capacity utilisation figure not disclosed.
demand_pricing: Pricing is linked to raw material inflation through contractual pass-through, with lags of days to weeks; September RM spike was not fully passed through in the quarter.
Power and fuel cost inflation linked to Middle East prices is being pushed into pricing; other expenses rose to INR112 crore from INR96 crore YoY, partly due to prior-year one-time reversals.
Management claims volume growth while some customers report flat or declining volumes, implying market share gains; company holds less than double-digit share in a fragmented market.
Segment focus on higher-value products; weaker in commoditised single-layer segments such as biscuits, with pharma cited as a growth opportunity.
Regulatory PCR (recycled plastic content) mandates exist: about 30-40% for simple mono-material laminates, about 10% for complex multi-material laminates, rising annually.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin moderation is from inventory costs, are margins sustainable, and how is the INR150-170 crore top-line increase split between volume and price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said price, mix and volume contributed roughly equal shares, about one-third each. Like-for-like EBIT margin is about 8%; Q3 dip was timing of RM pass-through, expected to reverse next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: At what utilisation are plants running, and how much extra revenue could full utilisation add?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a utilisation figure or revenue capacity estimate; said there is enough capacity for the next 2-3 years without major investment, with productivity gains creating headroom.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any Baddi-style restructuring planned at other plants, and how will Baddi customers be served?
qa_highlights.answer: Baddi customers were moved to Ambernath and Bangalore and the supply chain is running smoothly. No similar restructuring planned at other plants currently; actions will be taken as demand requires.

511147|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 26% to about INR111 crore and PAT rose 77% to INR6.14 crore, while Q4 growth slowed on macro and war-related travel weakness.
511147|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a record year, with revenue crossing about INR111 crore for the first time, PBT of INR8.03 crore and PAT of INR6.14 crore, and the company stated it remains debt-free. Q4 was hit by macro volatility, especially in March, from the US-Israel-Iran conflict and lower US student travel, though management said Q4 revenue still grew 22% and GTO grew 16%. Management highlighted the FEMA 401/2026 RBI circular, which expands AD-II scope to trade remittances and family maintenance and allows Forex Correspondent (FXC) appointments, and said it has recommended a 15% dividend. Management also acknowledged that rupee credit cards with zero cross-currency markup have taken share from forex cards in leisure travel, and that leisure market volumes contracted about 25% from March.

segments.name: Student
segments.commentary: Largest growth driver per management; overall market contracted about 20% in the year while the company gained share. Loan-funded students growing while own-funds students contracted after TCS was cut to 2%.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Over 900 corporates served; management cited a 95.62% CAGR. Named clients include Accenture, Siemens, EY, Zoho, Tech Mahindra and, recently, Adani.

segments.name: Retail / leisure
segments.commentary: Card business declined in FY26 on lower US student traffic and competition from rupee credit cards; leisure market down about 25% since March. Management described this as a calibrated, value-led push with a minimum margin per transaction.

segments.name: Prepaid cards
segments.commentary: Four products (three plastics and one digital-only, Uni-Z launched last month). Switch Card supports 30 currencies; Xplorer Metal card is by invitation. Samsung Pay and Google Pay tokenisation planned this year.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q1 FY27 to be a challenging, linear quarter with leisure travel down roughly 25% from March, and expects the next one to two months to remain tough.
Trade remittances expected to become a material business in 12 to 18 months; family maintenance (about $3 billion market) to be a growth area.
FXC network expected to expand through the model over the next 12 to 15 months, with Spice Money group network and NBFC/retail partners as possible distribution.
Trade remittance margins expected 20-30 bps, below current blended levels, as competition rises.
Target to raise digital/automated share of transactions from about 60% to 80% this year.
Management did not give numerical FY27 targets for cards or revenue; it said Q2 to Q4 are peak months and FY27 mix will change materially.
capex_capacity: Network kept lean at 21+ branches (down from 35 when the CEO took over, 16 in COVID); expansion planned mainly through FXC appointments rather than owned branches.
Company is evaluating whether to apply for a PA-CB licence.
Working on multiple payment rails for faster, holiday-enabled remittances and a student fee-remittance platform.
Smart Agent Platform, FPaaS, Smart Corporate Platform and consumer app run on a unified payments stack.
demand_pricing: Q4 traffic hit in March by the US-Israel-Iran conflict; leisure market contracted about 25% from March to May 2026 per management.
Rupee credit cards with zero cross-currency markup and lounge perks have taken a large share of international spend (management estimate about 60%), with credit card spend outside LRS and TCS.
Management says it will not price at a loss; pricing uses interbank rates with a small card fulfilment fee on the Switch card.
B2B and corporate make up about 80-85% of business; partner commissions and referral fees are a larger share of costs.
Retail customer lifetime value is quoted at about INR1,000 of annual income per traveller versus high digital CAC.
Management expects more competition after the RBI circular, with margin pressure; trade remittances may run at 20-30 bps margin.

qa_highlights.question: How will the new RBI circular affect volumes, revenue and margins over the next one to two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said scope has expanded to trade and non-trade current account transactions, with no negative impact from the circular itself, but competition will pressure margins. Trade remittance margins are expected at 20-30 bps; current net margin is 0.6-0.8%.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments will be most affected by the new regulations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not split out the impact by segment. It said the new trade and family maintenance categories open new growth areas, and that retail/leisure faces the most pressure from credit cards.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company compete with low-priced small players on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will stay competitive but will not work at a loss per transaction, citing a minimum margin policy and a digital platform for each segment. It acknowledged its retail pricing may not be the lowest.

qa_highlights.question: Segment-wise FY26 revenue, volume, customer and new-product breakdown; agent commissions versus branch revenue; CAC; card KPIs and FY27 targets
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave only broad-based answers: B2B and corporate are 80-85% of business, partner commissions are higher as a B2B company, and digital CAC is high. It declined to give specific numbers and said detailed data would be shared through the company's written channel.

qa_highlights.question: How does Scapia (bank-sponsored card) compare, and how are rupee credit cards affecting forex cards?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said credit cards hold a regulatory arbitrage (no LRS or TCS), that around 60% of international spend has moved to credit cards, and that the association has represented to RBI for parity. Forex cards are positioned on rate certainty for multi-currency travel; corporate and student segments do not use credit cards.

qa_highlights.question: What is the TCS cut to 2% for education remittances doing to the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 2% TCS mainly hit own-fund students, while loan-funded students are growing; it called the change a relief and said zero TCS would be better for the priority-sector segment.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and payables increase?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Pooja Mishra said the rise in current assets and liabilities reflects card-program customer wallet balances on both sides of the balance sheet. Capital turnover improved to 4.4x from 3.8x, and short-term borrowings are fixed-deposit-backed working capital lines, not structural debt.

Rupee credit cards eroding forex card share in leisure; RBI parity representation is pending with no timeline.
Margin pressure from new AD-II entrants and FFMC-licensed competitors; trade remittance margins guided at 20-30 bps.
Execution risk on FXC network rollout and trade/family maintenance scope, which management said still has open clarifications.

Customer service complaint raised on a Delhi branch; management promised corrective action.

511147|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 turnover rose 41.2% YoY to INR2,914 crores, revenue up 30% to INR44.58 crores, PBT up 9.6% to INR5.33 crores.
511147|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 as a record quarter, with turnover of about INR2,914 crores (up 41.2% YoY) and revenue of INR44.58 crores (up 30% YoY). PBT rose 9.6% YoY to INR5.33 crores, and H1 PBT was INR5.91 crores, with Q2 contributing about 90% of it. Growth was driven by outward remittance (Q2 up 53.9% YoY) and student and B2B business, with commission payouts raised, which compressed margins. The expanded AD-II mandate (perpetual licence from July 30) opens forex correspondent (FXC) and trade remittance routes, both guided to go live in Q3 to Q4.

Management said higher payout reflects wallet-share strategy; no confirmation of figures

segments.commentary: Turnover up 12.3% YoY in Q2; management said corporate is at about 40-50% of pre-COVID levels. Active corporates stood at 944.
