Management expects FXC distribution to reduce yield (revenue sharing with partners) but save on fixed costs, enabling asset-light reach expansion; a few new branches may be added in the next 3-6 months.

Own tech team builds solutions; card development platform built in-house; CDP (card) platform and partner integrations ongoing.
demand_pricing: Management said the overall market dipped due to forex volatility, US visa uncertainty, Middle East conflict and weak discretionary travel; April was a big dip.
Two months in Q2 crossed INR1,000 crores monthly turnover.
Q2 is seasonally the strongest quarter; Q1 weakest; Q3 and Q4 taper but stay better than Q1.
Commission payouts raised to win wallet share; management said payouts depend on partner business potential rather than a flat rate.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said higher payout is the strategy to increase wallet share; payouts vary by partner, so there is no flat norm.

qa_highlights.question: Trade payments scope, and whether a PA-CB licence is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RBI asked the company to work with FEDAI; SOPs follow membership, expected in November. It will first operationalise AD-II and consider PA-CB later.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO said incremental business came from B2B channels with higher commission. Commission was about 88-89 bps of turnover in the prior-year quarter, which included a one-time visa incentive; the amount was to be provided by email.

qa_highlights.question: Will FXC and distribution lift profits from INR7 crores to INR20 crores in 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no numerical target; it said reach and trade could grow revenue without corresponding costs but yield would dip due to partner sharing.

qa_highlights.question: Treasury income and customer float on the balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the float reflects customer funds received before remittances and card settlements complete, and treasury income should rise with card volumes. No quantum was given.

511196|2026-03.headline: Can Fin Homes FY26 disbursements hit INR10,531 crore, just above guidance, with Q4 a record INR3,245 crore; FY27 disbursement target INR13,000 crore.
511196|2026-03.overview: FY26 disbursements of INR10,531 crore marginally beat the INR10,500 crore guidance, with each quarter setting a new peak and Q4 at INR3,245 crore. AUM growth was about 10.44% as rundown ran about INR600 crore above the INR6,000 crore assumption. Karnataka grew 7% in disbursements after e-khata issues, and Telangana ended roughly flat at INR1,147 crore versus INR1,198 crore. Q4 included two one-offs: INR46 crore additional DTA provision on standard assets and INR13.5 crore tax refund gain; management says underlying FY26 profit was INR1,027 crore, up 20% from INR857 crore. Around 85% of the book has moved to quarterly reset, with the 50 bps pass-through and a 15 bps cut in January leaving an opening yield near 9.8% and spread of about 2.8%.

after 50 bps quarterly-reset pass-through and 15 bps January cut

qa_highlights.question: Is the BT-out and rundown rate peaking after the April quarterly-reset shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q4 to be the peak; BT outs were about INR380-400 crore in Q3 and Q4, nearly flat, and FY27 rundown is modelled at INR7,000 crore versus about INR6,600 crore in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How will disbursements reach INR13,000 crore given branch growth of about 6-7%?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers are 28 new branches in H1 FY27, expanding the sales team from 80-90 to about 150, and recovery in Karnataka and Telangana; the company is also planning for elevated prepayments.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 state-wise disbursement run rates and opex split?
qa_highlights.answer: Current monthly run rates: Karnataka about INR275-290 crore, Tamil Nadu INR180-200 crore, North and West INR150-160 crore each, Telangana INR110-120 crore, East about INR100 crore. Employee cost is INR177 crore and other cost INR134 crore in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Are the West Asia situation or LAP delinquencies showing stress, and is any management overlay planned?
qa_highlights.answer: No stress seen in bounce rates or delinquencies through March and April; no additional management overlay planned, but PCR rose from 49% to 56%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for spreads and margins after the reset and NHB repricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Spread is expected at about 2.8%, with guidance kept at 2.75%; the only risk is a rate rise, which would affect the roughly 15% of the book still on annual reset.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company losing prepayments to LIC Housing and Bajaj?
qa_highlights.answer: LIC wins on price, offering rates such as 7.15% on new business; Bajaj wins on takeover-plus-top-up, where Can Fin is more conservative on LTV.

511196|2026-06.headline: Can Fin Homes Q1 FY27 disbursements rose 29% YoY to INR 2,609 crores, but rundown of INR 1,857 crores absorbed the AUM gain.
511196|2026-06.overview: Disbursements of INR 2,609 crores beat the INR 2,500 crore internal plan and grew 29% YoY across all six zones. Book rundown rose to INR 1,857 crores (from INR 1,730 crores in Q4), mainly from part-prepayments of INR 1,072 crores after the annual-to-quarterly reset, so net AUM growth was about 10.8% YoY. Yield held at 9.81% and cost of borrowing fell to 6.98%, lifting spread to 2.83% and NIM to 3.81%. Management reaffirmed 14% AUM growth and a 10 bps credit cost for FY27, while ROA slipped to 2.39% on higher opex and an IT project rollout is underway across 250 branches.

qa_highlights.answer: No demand slowdown across geographies; 60 APF projects added in Q1 (271 to 331 approved). Rates for new bank loans are 7.25-7.5% vs 6.95% last year. qa_highlights.question: Is the IT-sector hiring slowdown in Bangalore affecting home loan offtake or policy?
qa_highlights.answer: No major impact seen so far: Karnataka grew 18% YoY and Telangana slightly more (partly base effect). IT-sector customers are about 6% of the base, with top IT employers barely represented. Karnataka NPA was lower in absolute terms at March 2026 vs March 2025, with only a marginal June increase.

qa_highlights.question: Any opex surprises in FY27 and how far is APF exposure per project capped?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 40 crore of further IT-related cost to come, with AMCs and depreciation starting; salary, rent and other costs in line with last year. Cost-to-income about 19.5% for FY27, trending toward 18% in about three years. APF exposure capped at 10% of the book per project.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the book rundown elevated for four quarters, and is the 4% level the new normal? Also, how does the best-rate gap to banks affect pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: Part-prepayments of INR 1,072 crore (vs INR 976 crore) drove the rundown, as borrowers under change-in-tenure kept EMIs constant and paid down principal. BT-outs were INR 408 crore (vs INR 400 crore), and other closures INR 377 crore (vs INR 360 crore). Best rate gap widened from 55 bps to over 100 bps; management is exploring deposit conversion and bureau alerts for retention.

qa_highlights.question: Can ROA of about 2.4% and ROE of about 18% be achieved in FY27 given higher opex and the soft Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 ROA was 2.39% (2.53% last year) and ROE 18%+. Management said the cost impact is already visible and expects to manage ROA, with NIM and spread on track and credit cost not a concern. Q1 NPA rise was only INR 17-18 crore vs INR 45 crore last Q1 FY26.

risks_watch: Book rundown: part-prepayments of INR 1,857 crore in Q1 (INR 1,072 crore part-prepay) mean FY27 disbursements may need to exceed INR 13,000 crore to hold 14% AUM growth; Q2 target is INR 3,000 crore.

IT rollout: 245 remaining branches migrate in month-end tranches through September; update expected around September. Management noted 50-100 branches will need more handholding than the 5-branch pilot.
Cost of funds: new bank loans priced at 7.25-7.5% vs 6.95% last year; NIM guidance of 3.81%+ depends on incremental-only pass-through and yield mix shift.
Competitive pricing gap: best rate spread to banks/larger players widened to over 100 bps from 55 bps; LIC and Bajaj Housing (growing about 25-30% per analyst) are main rivals.
Asset quality: SENP current NPA about 1.45-1.5% vs about 0.6-0.63% for salaried; IT-sector and Karnataka exposure monitored with early-warning signals; credit cost guided at 10 bps.
Opex: cost-to-income moved from about 18% to 19%+ in Q1, FY27 guided near 19.5%; about INR 40 crore of further IT costs yet to come.
key_quotes: So against INR 2,500 crores, which was what was planned and what was projected, we have achieved INR2,609 crores.
So, we are confident that the NIM will be maintained at 3.81% plus and we should not have a problem in that.
And so the 10 bps that we have been talking about, definitely doesn't look to be a challenge this year.

The major challenge or the major portion from where our run down is happening is actually amortization and more importantly, part prepayment where customers are making more payments every month, and but the loans are still with us.
511196|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on disbursements, asset quality and the 14% AUM growth target, but cautious on the higher book rundown, the widened pricing gap to banks and the IT rollout's business impact. Management was candid about the rundown and competitive pressures, and it deferred on new product launches, saying the Board has not yet deliberated.

tone.note: Management was confident on disbursements, asset quality and the 14% AUM target and NIM at 3.81%+, but cautious on the higher book rundown, the widened pricing gap to banks and the IT rollout; analysts probed rundown, pricing gap, ROA and the IT rollout's business impact.

511196|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 disbursements fell to INR2,375 crore as Project Tejas IT migration hit branches; FY27 disbursement guidance of INR13,000 crore held.
511196|2026-09.overview: Can Fin Homes completed the full go-live of Project Tejas (IT transformation) across all branches, with the final ~93 old branches and new branches moving live from 1 October 2026. Disbursements for the quarter were INR2,375 crore, net of about INR29 crore of NHB-mandated cancellation netting, and management attributed the shortfall to one-time migration and process changes plus a Telangana Section 22 verification issue. Management held FY27 disbursement guidance of INR13,000 crore and AUM growth of 13-14%, and guided FY28 disbursement of INR16,000 crore with 15%+ AUM growth. Prepayments eased to INR1,795 crore from INR1,857 crore in Q1, and the company passed on a 10 bps housing rate hike effective 8 October 2026.

segments.name: Branches live on new system (Project Tejas)
segments.commentary: Rollout in phases: 11 branches in July (5 old, 6 new), 89 in August (75 old, 14 new), 77 old in September and 98 in October (93 old plus 5 new). Disbursements at branches during their go-live month dropped about 70-75%, recovering to 80-90% of prior run-rate the following month.

segments.name: Branches not yet migrated (93-branch cohort)
segments.commentary: Average monthly disbursement was INR435 crore in Q1 and rose to INR454, INR458, INR424 and INR481 crore in the months of July-September per management's slide 20 data (management's figures; not independently verified).

segments.name: Sales team channel
segments.commentary: Sales team headcount about 90 now, targeted at 150 by year-end and 250 in FY28; management expects INR1,500-1,600 crore from sales in FY27 versus INR560 crore in H1.

segments.name: Karnataka
segments.commentary: Disbursement has stabilised at INR230-250 crore per period, per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement guidance held at INR13,000 crore (20%+ growth over INR10,500 crore in FY26); Q3 target about INR3,500 crore with the shortfall to be recovered in Q4.
FY27 AUM growth guidance of 13-14%, closer to 14%; management said the 15% AUM growth figure for FY28 is a resultant of disbursement and rundown.
FY28 disbursement internal target INR16,000 crore (about 22% growth), implying 15%+ AUM growth, closer to 15.5%.

Spread and NIM guidance of 2.75% and 3.75% maintained; management said it will pass through rate hikes, with about 12-13 bps of liability cost increase on the full book from the 25 bps repo hike and 10 bps passed on so far.
FY27 credit cost guidance of 10 bps maintained; gross NPA expected to fall in H2.
Plans to draw NHB refinance earlier, from Q3 if sanctions are higher, to benefit from lower rates; exploring an additional refinance limit.
capex_capacity: Project Tejas fully live: LOS and LMS live across all branches as of 1 October 2026; modules including risk, ALM, borrowings (by September 2025 onward) and deposits/DMS (January) implemented per management.
25 of 28 branches planned for FY27 are already operational with staff; these are expected to contribute in Q3 and Q4.
Branch expansion: about 12 branches added in UP in the last year, per management.
About 129 staff who were deployed on the IT project are being redeployed to branches and departments, with some support retained for 1-2 months.
demand_pricing: Management said underlying demand is robust with no change, and attributed the Q2 shortfall to process changes (about 8-10 additional OTPs per borrower and co-borrower), a 5-day post-month data handover lag, and a new Telangana Section 22 sub-registrar verification requirement.
Housing loan rate raised by 10 bps effective 8 October 2026 (new customers from 12 October); about 87% of floating book is on quarterly reset, about 12-13% on annual reset.
Management expects a 25 bps repo hike to translate into about 12-13 bps on the book, with plans to pass on about 15 bps next time.

Prepayment rate was about 15.5-16% historically and about 17-17.5% recently; management said a 100 bps rise could narrow the rate gap by around 60 bps, reducing prepayment and rundown by about INR400 crore.
Higher-ticket (INR30 lakh+) loans have grown, and the company is also looking at AHF-linked INR15-25 lakh loans as NHB AHF share rises.
PMAY 2.0 uptake described as slow relative to CLSS-1, with limited presence in the high-need states (Odisha, Bengal, Bihar, UP).
Management said the sales team contributed INR560 crore in H1 FY27 and targets about 20% of disbursement from sales in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the liquidity coverage ratio rise well above the 100% regulatory minimum, and what is a steady level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to lower short-term borrowings, now about 12% of borrowings versus 26-27% in March 2023, plus smaller bulk borrowings. LCR range cited as 135% to 250%; HQLA held at roughly INR2,300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Does a rising rate cycle affect home loan demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a 25-50 bps move is a non-event for demand because EMI impact is limited on 15-year tenors. Rates of 7.15-8% are among the lowest seen, so customer behaviour is not expected to change much.

qa_highlights.question: Is there risk to FY27 disbursement target from the South monsoon or drought, and to asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is early to assess; drought has been declared in parts of Maharashtra and Karnataka, but the company lends mainly in Tier 1-2 areas. If industry slows, it could hit disbursement, and it may use LAP or construction top-ups as short-term levers.

qa_highlights.question: How will operational efficiency from Project Tejas play out in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited manual processes now automated, native AI features, auto form filling, and a digital sourcing channel expected to reach about 10% of business. Sales headcount to rise from about 90 to 150 this year without adding branch staff.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rate pass-through and prepayment outlook after the repo hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Housing rates rose 10 bps effective 8 October 2026 against a 25 bps repo hike, which translates to about 12-13 bps on the book. Management said a 100 bps rise could cut the rate gap by about 60 bps and reduce prepayment and rundown by about INR400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How reset timing works for bank borrowings and the loan book, and whether spread is at risk in a rising cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Repo-linked bank borrowings reprice from 1 November; T-bill-linked ones reset quarterly. About 87% of the floating book is on quarterly reset and 12-13% on annual, with roughly one-third repricing each on 1 November, 1 December and 1 January. Management said it will pass on hikes to protect spread and NIM.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management in the H2 disbursement ramp (about INR3,500 crore per quarter) and the FY28 AUM outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 was INR2,600 crore against a planned INR2,500 crore, so the INR100 crore buffer was used; Q3 target is INR3,500 crore with about INR400 crore shortfall recovered in Q4. FY28 disbursement target of INR16,000 crore implies AUM growth of about 15-15.5%, with 15% described as a resultant figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the productivity ramp for new branches and the pipeline status?
qa_highlights.answer: New branches take about 18 months (range 18-24) to reach 5 cases per staff per month. Management said sanctioned-but-not-disbursed rose about INR118 crore quarter on quarter, and that some pipeline was lost during the migration.

risks_watch: Q3 disbursement delivery against the INR3,500 crore target, and whether the INR400 crore shortfall is recovered in Q4 as guided.
Spread and NIM protection: liability cost rising about 12-13 bps on the full book against 10 bps passed on so far; management plans a next hike of about 15 bps.
Asset quality: SMA-0 uptick attributed to a daily versus month-end overdue computation change; gross NPA is expected to fall in H2 and credit cost is guided at 10 bps against about 9 bps in Q2.
Monsoon and drought risk to construction activity and demand in Maharashtra and Karnataka, plus Telangana Section 22 verification delays.
Sales channel ramp from about 90 to 150 staff (and 250 in FY28) to deliver INR1,500-1,600 crore in FY27 versus INR560 crore in H1, and the digital channel target of 10%.
Liability mix: NCD pricing around 8.3-8.35% versus bank term loans at about 7.65%, and special-rate T-bill-linked borrowings that reset at varying times.
Prepayment trend (INR1,795 crore in Q2 versus INR1,857 crore in Q1) after the housing rate hike, and the NHB refinance draw (INR1,350 crore sanctioned, expected at about 6.6-6.7%).
key_quotes: The month in which the implementation has happened, the disbursements, they have dropped in that particular branches by about 70% to 75%, and then the next month, again, it pushes back and it comes back to almost 80% -90% of the old disbursement.

Basically, in terms of the demand or in terms of the business per se, there has been no change, but for the impact of the IT transformation, which is mainly on account of the understanding, or rather the change in the flow, the additional processes that have been incorporated.
We will be looking at a 20% plus growth in terms of the disbursement, which consequently should become a 13%- 14% AUM growth this year and a 15% plus AUM growth in the next year.
Basically, our endeavor will be to ensure that our NIM and spread and NIM stays protected.
511196|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on the full-year guidance and long-term benefit of Project Tejas, while openly attributing the Q2 shortfall to one-time migration issues. Management was more hedged on the Telangana verification issue and monsoon risk ("it's a little early"), and it was evasive on the exact timing of the sales ramp and branch productivity.

511218|2026-03.headline: Shriram Finance Q4 FY26 PAT rose 40.86% YoY to INR3,013.57 crores; management guides 18% AUM growth for FY27 but will revisit after Q1.
511218|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered strong profitability, with PAT up 40.86% YoY to INR3,013.57 crores and NIM up to 8.61%, while AUM grew 14.85% YoY to INR3,02,273.75 crores. Gross Stage 3 edged up to 4.58% from 4.55% a year ago, and Stage 2 plus Stage 3 rose sequentially in CV, PV and MSME. MUFG Bank completed a preferential allotment on April 8, 2026, taking a 20% fully diluted stake, and the board recommended a final dividend of INR6 per share. Management budgets 18% AUM growth and 8.5% NIM for FY27, but said Q1 FY27 is hard to predict and it will revisit guidance after Q1, with credit cost unchanged for now.

segments.commentary: Management expects PV growth above 20% in FY27, against a Q4 slowdown in used PV financing that management attributed to focus on CV. Gross Stage 2 plus Stage 3 also rose in PV.

segments.commentary: New vehicles are about 15% of disbursements, and management expects this to rise by another 5 to 10 percentage points over the next two quarters; it is not expected to reach 30% to 35%.

qa_highlights.question: Is AUM growth of 18% for FY27 on AUM or disbursements, and what is the opex and credit cost guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: 18% refers to AUM growth; opex to stay around 26% to 27% cost-to-income; credit cost seen as manageable for now, to be revisited after Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 GS2 plus GS3 rise sequentially in CV, PV and MSME, and will credit cost rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said retail cash-flow fluctuations are normal and provisions are priced in; coverage was increased slightly; stress, if any, expected after November-December depending on fuel prices and monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: What is the budgeted NIM and how much of the cost-of-funds benefit goes to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: NIM budgeted at 8.5%; management aims to protect NIM and pass on benefit only if needed for growth; NIM will expand in practice, though the budget is conservative.

qa_highlights.question: Why did used PV financing slow in Q4, and what is the PV growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the slowdown to focus on CV and expects PV growth above 20% in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What share of disbursements is new vehicle financing and how will it scale?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15% of disbursements now; expected to rise by 5 to 10 percentage points over the next two quarters, not to 30% to 35%.

qa_highlights.question: Will MUFG increase its stake before the 24-month lock-in ends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment, saying nothing has been discussed and it is too early, less than one month after allotment.

511218|2026-06.headline: Shriram Finance Q1 FY27 PAT rose 59.79% YoY to INR3,444.56 crores, with NIM at 9.04% and disbursements up 19.51% YoY to INR49,974 crores.
511218|2026-06.overview: Shriram Finance reported strong Q1 FY27 numbers, with PAT of INR3,444.56 crores (up 59.79% YoY, up 14.3% QoQ) and NII up 33.67% YoY to INR8,055.70 crores. Growth was supported by fresh equity of about INR39,600 crores, which cut the leverage ratio to 2.14x from 3.82x in March and funded repayment of borrowings. Management reiterated the FY27 AUM growth guidance of 18% but said it will reassess after Q2, and guided credit cost around 2% and operational NIM around 8.5% in the medium term. Asset quality was broadly stable, with gross Stage 3 at 4.64% against 4.58% in Q4 FY26. Management said the company will now deploy surplus liquidity into growth and return to borrowing, including securitisation, towards the end of the quarter.

segments.name: Commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 CV disbursement INR19,556 crores, the largest product. Management said CV growth tracked the ~20% industry volume growth and new-vehicle share is rising.

segments.name: Passenger vehicles
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 PV disbursement INR11,018 crores. Management cited industry PV sales growth of 25.9%.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 MSME disbursement INR6,184 crores. Management targets MSME rising from about 15% to about 20% of the book, with growth expected to exceed the overall book.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Q1 FY27 gold disbursement INR5,153 crores; gold is about 2.5% of the book, targeted at about 5% in three years, with about 2,200 branches gold-ready.

segments.name: Personal loans, 2-wheelers, construction and farm equipment
segments.commentary: Personal loans INR2,773 crores, 2-wheelers INR3,548 crores, construction equipment INR792 crores (about INR1,000 crores for five quarters), farm equipment INR947 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth guidance of 18% is retained; management will reassess after Q2 FY27 and expects growth of more than 15% in Q2.
Operational NIM expected around 8.5% in the medium term (2-3 years); current NIM of about 9% expected to hold for the next two quarters as surplus liquidity is deployed.
Credit cost guided at around 2% in the near and medium term.
Cost-to-income ratio to remain stable; about 150 branches to be added in FY27 without a material rise in cost.
New vehicle share of disbursement (about 16-17%) expected to rise to about 20-25% over time, with new-vehicle book reaching about 30% plus of the book in the medium term.
Borrowing to resume around the end of Q2 (August to October), with securitisation likely; incremental borrowing cost about 7.77%, bank borrowing about 8%.
capex_capacity: About 150 new branches tentatively planned for FY27, with manpower to rise in line with volume.
About 2,200 branches made ready for gold loan activity; gold book targeted to double in three years.
Surplus liquidity of INR17,000-18,000 crores held as roughly three months of liability repayments; the balance of surplus is expected to be deployed into growth over about 1-1.5 months.
No liability repayments planned from here; borrowing programme to restart, with securitisation and direct assignment transactions not done in Q1.
demand_pricing: Industry: CV sales up 14.1% YoY to 2.65 lakh units; PV up 25.9%; 2-wheelers up 20.3%; 3-wheelers up 29.7%; tractors up 21.6%; construction equipment up 8.8%, per management.
Management said operators have absorbed fuel-cost increases without vehicle idling, and used-vehicle demand has stayed healthy.
Lower borrowing costs are being passed on to new-vehicle customers, and some customers who had left for other lenders are being won back by matching rates.
Management said the MSME slowdown in FY26 was due to US tariffs and policy uncertainty; the book is now expected to grow again from Q2.
Gold demand is driven by customers raising loans against existing jewellery, which management sees as a source of volume for NBFCs.

qa_highlights.question: Will the NIM hold at around 9%, given excess liquidity and a slow mix shift toward new vehicles?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current NIM should hold for the next two quarters, but will fall to about 8.5% in the medium term as new-vehicle mix rises. Management said the INR500 crore of NII from equity-funded surplus liquidity will gradually subside.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 18% FY27 growth guidance be raised?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management retained 18% for FY27, said it will reassess after Q2, and expects growth above 15% next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for asset quality in gold and MSME?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gold asset quality is not a concern, and MSME quality is improving after a cautious year. The Q1 Stage 3 rise was a seasonal impact, from 4.58% to 4.63%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of incremental borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bank borrowing would cost about 8%, and incremental capital-market borrowing about 7.77%; the company now borrows as a AA-rated entity, which lowers its cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why will the company borrow again if it holds surplus liquidity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the surplus will be used for growth over about 1-1.5 months, after which fresh borrowing will resume, including securitisation toward the end of the quarter.

risks_watch: Monsoon deficit: rainfall was 24% below normal from June 4 to July 16, and IMD forecasts 90% of normal rainfall for 2026, which could affect rural income and oilseed and pulse output.
West Asia conflict and fuel prices: management said pass-through has held so far, but a further rise in retail fuel prices could hit operator margins.
NIM trajectory: management guides NIM falling from 9.04% to about 8.5% in the medium term, and analysts questioned the pace.
MSME and gold: Stage 3 rose QoQ in gold and MSME; the MSME book must grow to about INR7,000 crores per quarter from Q3 to meet the target.
Borrowing restart: funding will move back toward market borrowings and securitisation after Q2, so the cost of funds and mix will be watched.
Construction equipment disbursement has stayed near INR1,000 crores for five quarters against about INR2,000 crores previously.
511218|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on growth, margins and asset quality, but cautious on the guidance path: management held the FY27 target, deferred any upgrade until after Q2, and repeatedly tied the outlook to monsoon and West Asia risk. Questions on the 8.5% medium-term NIM drew the most pushback from analysts.
key_quotes: But we are confident that we'll be able to grow more than 15% at least for next quarter.
So our long-term margins of 8.5%, we will be able to manage.
Gold, absolutely not. MSME, we have been cautious in the last 1 year. We are now pretty confident about the MSME quality -- asset quality.
Stable, I should say.

511218|2026-09.headline: Shriram Finance Q2 FY27 PAT rose 59.37% YoY to INR3,677.03 crores, with NIM at 9.52% and gross Stage 3 at 4.65%.
511218|2026-09.overview: Shriram Finance reported strong Q2 FY27 earnings, with disbursements up 25.71% YoY to INR54,079.02 crores and AUM up 16.96% YoY to INR3,29,021.72 crores. Net interest income rose to INR8,661.04 crores and NIM expanded to 9.52%, which management attributed partly to temporary capital-driven benefits. Asset quality weakened, with gross Stage 3 at 4.65% (4.64% in Q1) and credit cost at 2.03%, which management linked to weak monsoon and drought-prone geographies. Management trimmed AUM growth guidance to 15-17% from 18%, and said credit cost would be elevated by about 30-40 bps for one or two quarters.

financial_highlights.change: down 15 bps QoQ from 8.56%; down 18 bps since March

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: Disbursements rose to roughly INR10,000 crores per the analyst's figure, versus about INR6,000 crores in recent quarters, as lending expanded from the South and West to all-India. Unsecured share is 28% and secured 72%; MSME is a source of incremental Stage 2 and Stage 3 accretion.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold disbursements were INR5,443 crores in Q2 versus INR5,153 crores in Q1. AUM is about INR9,000 crores, and LTV is about 72-73%. Management attributes higher gold Stage 2/3 to the newly introduced EMI and interest-servicing products, where customers are used to bullet repayment.

segments.name: Construction equipment
segments.commentary: Disbursements have rebounded, but Stage 2 and Stage 3 ratios rose. Management said absolute gross Stage 3 fell to INR862 crores from INR874 crores QoQ, and gross Stage 2 is INR963 crores versus INR953 crores, so the rise is a denominator effect.

segments.name: Liabilities
segments.commentary: Liability mix is public deposits 31%, NCDs 15.71%, ECB and bonds 16.5%, bank and institutional borrowing 21%, and securitisation 14%, out of total liabilities of INR2,36,271 crores. Management said about INR27,000 crores was raised in the quarter, and liquidity was brought down to about 3 months of future liabilities.

guidance_outlook: AUM growth for FY27 is now expected at 15-17%, down from the earlier 18% guidance; Q1 growth was about 15% and Q2 about 17%.
Credit cost guidance is about 2% long term. Management said it may run 30-40 bps higher in select geographies and products for one or two quarters, and the full-year figure would be lower than 2.3%.
NIM is expected to stay near current levels for one or two quarters, then ease to around 9% in the medium term and about 8.5% in the long term.

Incremental cost of funds is expected to stay below 8%, potentially rising to about 8.35% if rates or capital market yields rise. Management does not expect the overall liability cost to rise from 8.4%.
Cost to income is guided to about 25% in the medium to long term, with technology spend likely to add to opex.
Gold loan target is unchanged: double the gold book in three years, from about 2.5% to about 5% of the book.

Insurance commission income of about INR350 crores in FY26 could fall by about INR100 crores if the draft IRDA distribution-income guidelines are adopted, which management called immaterial to the balance sheet.
capex_capacity: Liquidity has been drawn down to about 3 months of future liabilities, with cash plus investments falling from about INR38,000 crores to about INR31,000-32,000 crores. Future AUM growth will now largely need fresh borrowing rather than surplus liquidity.
Borrowing programme has resumed, with bonds and bank borrowing back to pre-March levels. Liquidity coverage ratio is 303%.
demand_pricing: Macro: Q1 FY27 GDP grew 7.8%, and the IMF raised its FY27 forecast to 7%. Retail CPI rose to 5.54% in September, and the RBI raised the repo rate by 25 bps to 5.5% with a calibrated tightening stance.

Rural and auto demand: the Q2 passenger vehicle sales growth was 30.7%, two-wheelers 15.2%, and commercial vehicles 28.7%. The monsoon was 87% of LPA, and 51.2% of India's area was abnormally dry or worse as of September 23.
Stress is concentrated in drought-prone states such as Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana. Management said it is cautious there but sees no widespread problem.
New versus used vehicle yield differential is 200-400 bps, depending on the segment.
Management said fresh loans can be repriced, but the existing fixed-rate book cannot be repriced.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the Stage 2 and Stage 3 increase across construction equipment, gold and MSME, and what credit cost is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to seasonal weakness and certain geographies with lower rainfall, and said it is not widespread. Credit cost guidance stays at about 2%, with a possible 30 bps temporary increase in select areas. Loan-book Stage 3 is about 2.3%, not 2.5%.

qa_highlights.question: How will NIM and cost of funds evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NIM is elevated temporarily from capital infusion and will stay near current levels for one or two quarters, then ease to about 9% medium term and about 8.5% long term. Incremental cost of funds is expected below 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the AUM growth guidance lower, and are credit filters being tightened?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth is guided to 15-17% because of the West Asia war and weak monsoon, and said credit filters are unchanged unless the economy slows. Rural demand was strong in the last two quarters, and caution has only been applied to drought-prone areas in the last month.

qa_highlights.question: Are gold loan stress levels a sign of industry-level problems?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rise is mainly from the new EMI and interest-servicing gold products, where customers used to bullet repayment are paying late, and it sees no industry-level challenge. The gold growth plan is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the draft IRDA distribution-income guidelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance commission was about INR350 crores in FY26, and the proposed guidelines could cut about INR100 crores. Management said this is not material to the balance sheet and expects IRDA to revise the rates.

qa_highlights.question: Why did opex growth stay benign, and what is the medium-term cost-to-income target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 included annual back-office bonuses, so Q2 staff costs normalised. The medium to long-term cost-to-income target is about 25%, with added technology spend as a risk.

risks_watch: Credit cost and Stage 3 could stay elevated for one or two quarters if the monsoon stays weak and in drought-prone areas such as Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana.
MSME is growing fast into new geographies and carries a high share of Stage 2 and Stage 3 accretion. Unsecured exposure is 28% of the MSME book.
Rising policy rates and capital market yields could push incremental borrowing costs above 8%, and the NIM could compress faster than the guided glide path.
Management did not quantify the share of slippages from drought-prone areas or the share of new vehicles in AUM, and it referred these to investor relations.
A reported unauthorised loan issue in Kerala was taken offline, with status and KYC controls not disclosed on the call.
Gold loan Stage 2 and Stage 3 are rising as customers move to EMI and interest-servicing products.

It was evasive on several specifics, including EBLR migration, the new versus used split, the drought-area share of slippages and Kerala, which it deferred to investor relations.

The net interest margin is because of th e capital infusion, there is a temporary increase in the NIM. It is likely to remain at this level maybe for another one quarter or two, then slowly coming down.
Growth, we have been cautious, even though our initial guidance was 18% growth.
No, it's basically because we had introduced EMI and interest servicing gold loans.

511243|2026-03.headline: Chola Q4 FY26 disbursements rose 25% YoY to INR32,913 crore, AUM up 21% to INR2,42,630 crore; FY27 credit cost guided to ~1.5% pre-overlay.
511243|2026-03.overview: Disbursements grew 25% YoY in Q4 across all major product segments, with Vehicle Finance up 26% and Consumer up 45%. NIM rose 40 bps YoY to about 8% on lower cost of funds, and pre-overlay ROA was 4.1% versus 3.6% a year earlier. Management booked a INR200 crore precautionary management overlay for geopolitical and fuel-price risks, and said April 2026 early delinquencies, non-starters and first-cut net credit losses were better than April 2025. Guidance for FY27 is 20-23% AUM growth and net credit cost falling from 1.6% (pre-overlay) to about 1.5%.

segments.name: Vehicle Finance
segments.commentary: Disbursements grew 26% YoY in Q4 and AUM 18% to INR1,19,558 crore. FY27 guidance is disbursement growth of 15-20% and AUM growth of about 18%; April showed growth across PV, 2W, HCV and LCV.

segments.name: MSME (LAP, SME, SBPL)
segments.commentary: MSME disbursements grew 11% in Q4 and AUM 29%. LAP AUM INR52,295 crore (+26%), SME INR9,338 crore (+41%), SBPL INR3,537 crore (+46%).

segments.commentary: Consumer disbursements grew 45% YoY, with gold loan disbursing INR1,130 crore in Q4 and Consumer AUM up 20%; Home Loan AUM +23%, and CSEL AUM +4%. Home loan disbursements moderated due to election-related and land-record delays.

segments.name: CSEL

guidance_outlook: FY27 overall AUM growth of 20-23%; LAP and Home Loans 25-30%, Vehicle Finance about 18%, SME/SBPL above 30%.

Remaining CCD balance of INR630 crore expected to convert in H1 FY27.
demand_pricing: Management reported strong April 2026 sales, credit and collections versus April 2025, and no change in customer behaviour at the ground level.
Balraj Menon said April early defaults and non-starters were significantly lower than April 2025 and in line with prior-year April-March trends; first-cut net credit losses were also lower.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 AUM and credit cost trajectory, and what credit filter changes are being made?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth stays at 20-23% and net credit cost is expected to fall from 1.6% pre-overlay to about 1.5%, helped by Gini-coefficient improvements in underwriting. No further overlay is needed for now beyond the INR200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the strong April CV and PV data from OEMs reflected on the ground?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said April sales, credit and collections were very strong versus April 2025, and it has seen no change in customer behaviour.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CSEL growth, opex and ROA outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CSEL pre-tax ROA is expected to exceed 3% this year from Q4 ROA of 2.3%. Q4 opex included a one-time CGTMSE cost (about 6% of the segment's opex), and the opex ratio should normalise to about 4.5%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the business loan book is covered by CGTMSE?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70% of unsecured assets are covered and this may rise to 80-82%. Only the business loan book is in CGTMSE, at about INR3,000-3,500 crore (about 80% of a roughly INR5,000 crore BL book); Q4 CGTMSE cost was about INR38 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Did the overlay change PD-LGD assumptions, and why is NIM up 50 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: No PD-LGD change was made; the overlay was set using COVID and diesel-price experience. The NIM jump relates to ARC receipts recognised as income, offset by higher credit losses, leaving ROTA largely unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital-raising policy and gearing guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Equity raising would be evaluated if Tier 1 approaches 13%. Growth below 23-25% is expected to be funded from internal accruals. Gearing fell from 7.17x to 6.94x.

rows.why: Diversification into CV, CE, car and tractors (70% of book target over 3-4 years, two-wheeler to ~30%), with used car at 8.5% of AUM vs 2% a year ago and CE growth ~75% YoY, is already under way.

rows.label: Scorecard-led disbursement scale-up from end-Q2
rows.why: Approval rate held at 35-40% vs industry 75-80%; management plans to scale disbursements once the in-house scorecard is live, with Q3 festive season expected as the biggest quarter.

rows.label: Equity raise with 2-3 investors
rows.why: Leverage at 4.88x debt-to-equity on ₹678 crore shareholder funds and ₹3,318 crore borrowings; management comfortable up to 6x, but the raise is still pending and management was evasive on it.

rows.label: ECL model revision with possible LGD cut
rows.when: in about four weeks from call
rows.why: LGD could fall from ~50% to 40-42%, a potential provision release, but management is holding it back as a buffer and PCR stays at 50%.

tone.note: Management was confident on asset quality, the CRISIL AA- upgrade and funding costs, but cautious on growth with approvals held at 35-40%; analysts pushed on growth, ROA and the pending equity raise, which management was evasive on.

512008|2026-03.headline: EFC (I) FY26 revenue rose 58% to ₹10,367 mn and PAT 67% to ₹2,347 mn; Q4 PAT margin 23.5%.
512008|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue from operations was ₹10,367 mn (up 58% YoY), EBITDA ₹4,683 mn (up 43%) and PAT ₹2,347 mn (up 67%), with PAT margin rising from 21.4% to 22.6%. Q4 FY26 revenue was ₹2,929 mn (up 39%), EBITDA ₹1,436 mn (up 32%) and PAT ₹689 mn (up 45%). Design & Build and Furniture grew fastest, while Leasing remained the largest, recurring base. Management guided FY27 growth of about 40% for Design & Build, over 50% for Furniture and 18,000–20,000 build seats for Leasing. Management also said working capital needs are rising as the business scales.

financial_highlights.change: +45% YoY vs ₹480 mn; vs 22.7% in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Leasing
segments.commentary: Rental revenue ₹5,356 mn in FY26 (up about 44% from ₹3,722 mn); segment PBIT about ₹2,127 mn. Presence in 25 cities, more than 750 clients, average enterprise tenure about 51 months, payback 18–20 months, top-10 client share down to about 24%.

segments.name: Design & Build (Interior)
segments.commentary: Revenue about ₹4,378 mn in FY26 (up about 66% from ₹2,636 mn); segment profit about ₹1,197 mn. Over 80 designers and engineers, more than 45 clients, presence in 15+ locations, design footprint about 5.5 mn sq ft.

segments.name: Furniture
segments.commentary: Revenue about ₹632 mn in FY26 (up about 202% from ₹209 mn); segment profit about ₹156 mn. Pune plant of 1.2 lakh sq ft, more than 1,500 SKUs, over 60,000 units delivered; management targets about 25% EBITDA for this vertical.

guidance_outlook: Leasing: add about 18,000–20,000 build (revenue-generating) seats in FY27, with about 25,000 seats of total capacity additions; management says most of FY27 build seats are already visible.
Design & Build: about 40% growth in FY27 considered achievable, backed by current order book and pipeline.
Furniture: growth of over 50% targeted in FY27.
Central-level EBITDA margin of 30%+ expected to continue in FY27 and beyond.
Capex: no major new capex planned; growth to come from existing capacity; Leasing adds about 2,000 self-funded seats at about ₹50,000 per seat; no land acquisition planned.
Working capital to be used as growth war chest; management said future QIB or debt raises are possible for larger capex.
capex_capacity: Leasing: 18–20k build seats per year (FY26 achieved about 18k), 25k seats of total capacity added; more than 10% of seats funded by own capital, about 2,000 seats at about ₹50,000 per seat.
Furniture: Pune plant 1.2 lakh sq ft; capacity about ₹200–275 crore in value terms; improvements and some new machinery planned, no land purchase.
Design & Build: contractual model with no capex requirement.
Debt: asset-backed (LRD/property-backed) at about 7.5–7.75%; no immediate repayment pressure in FY27.
demand_pricing: Management says GCC, technology, BFSI and consumer enterprises are moving from capex-led ownership to OPEX-led managed offices; GCC and large enterprise clients are about 70% of revenue per management.
Average rent per sq ft rose to about ₹7,250–7,500 in FY26 from about ₹7,000–7,250 in the last quarter; management expects further increases.
Growth split across zones expected roughly equally (about 30% each) in West/NCR and the Southern belt, with Eastern India growth to follow over time.
Design & Build: management says it is among only the top three to five eligible bidders for contracts of ₹50–200 crore, which limits competition.
On AI, management argues it will create employment and that office demand will not fall; no client renewal data was provided.

qa_highlights.question: If one vertical underperforms, how does that affect consolidated margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Leasing (about 45% of revenue, with 51-month tenures) is very unlikely to underperform, so about 50% of revenue is assured; any hit would be in Design & Build and Furniture, which are project-based and about 10–20% of revenue at risk.

qa_highlights.question: Furniture growth is on a low base; what is sustainable margin and the captive vs third-party split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are the same for captive and third-party sales because transactions are at arm's length. It targets about 25% EBITDA for Furniture and did not give a captive/external split.

qa_highlights.question: Is AI a threat to office occupancy, and what evidence exists?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not seen any negative impact and argued AI will create new employment and more structured businesses; no renewal data was cited.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue came from GCC/MLC and what is the sign-up pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said large enterprise and GCC clients are about 70% of revenue, with 18–20k seats added per year in each of the last two years; no city-wise sign-up numbers were given.

qa_highlights.question: Why was working capital raised through a rights issue, and why not QIP or debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the rights issue went to loyal existing shareholders because capital needs were limited; it framed the raise as a working-capital buffer, noted QIB routes are planned for future capex, and said debt remains part of the capital strategy.

qa_highlights.question: Seat guidance: was there a shortfall versus 20–25k guidance, and what is average rent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no shortfall: 18–20k is revenue-generating build seats, while 25k is total capacity added. Average rent is about ₹7,250–7,500 per sq ft for FY26.

risks_watch: Working capital intensity: receivables, inventory and other financial assets rose; management says collections and working capital efficiency are priorities for FY27.
Project concentration: Design & Build and Furniture are contract- and project-based, and management says a downturn there would hit margins in absolute terms.
Seat guidance clarity: management separates build seats (18–20k) from capacity additions (25k); the FY26 gap versus earlier 20–25k guidance was not addressed in detail.
Leverage: lease liabilities and borrowings rose; management did not give a debt quantum or net debt figure.
Furniture scale-up: targets over 50% growth and about 25% EBITDA on a two-year-old business; margin sustainability is unproven at scale.
512008|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the growth narrative and FY27 targets, but evasive on quantitative detail: no client renewal data, no captive/third-party split, no segment EBITDA for FY27, and no debt quantum. Pushback on the AI question was answered with qualitative argument rather than data.
key_quotes: We are not pursuing growth for the sake of growth. We are building a Company that can scale sustainably, long-term value creation at its core.
Leasing gives us stability, Design & Build gives us growth and execution strength, while Furniture gives us integration and margin opportunities.
So, there is no shortfall. What we mentioned is 18,000 to 20,000 is the build seat that we are talking about and 25,000 seats are the overall capacity that we are talking about.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides central EBITDA margin of 30%+ to continue in FY27 and beyond (FY26 PAT margin rose to 22.6% from 21.4%, Q4 PAT margin 23.5%), with Furniture targeted at ~25% EBITDA, though Q4 EBITDA growth (+32%) trailed revenue growth (+39%).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Leasing adds 18,000-20,000 revenue-generating build seats in FY27 (about 25,000 total seats), with most already visible and about 2,000 self-funded seats at about Rs 50,000 per seat; FY26 achieved about 18k seats.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Design & Build guided ~40% growth and Furniture >50% in FY27, backed by order book and pipeline; Leasing adds 18-20k build seats versus FY26 revenue growth of ~44% (Rs 5,356 mn rental revenue).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says no major new capex planned and no land acquisition; Leasing growth is self-funded at ~2,000 seats and Furniture gets only improvements and some machinery, with debt at 7.5-7.75% and no immediate repayment pressure. Utilisation was not disclosed, so the call rests on stated plans, not on utilisation.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 revenue grew 58% and PAT 67%, and management says the FY27 targets are fairly achievable, but no explicit guidance raise was given and Q4 growth (+39% revenue) was below the full-year pace.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Working capital (receivables, inventory) is rising and Design & Build and Furniture are project-based, with 10-20% of revenue at risk in a downturn; the FY26 seat gap versus earlier 20-25k guidance was not addressed in detail.

rows.label: Working capital as growth war chest; rights issue proceeds
rows.why: Management frames working capital as a growth buffer, notes rising receivables and inventory, and says collections are a FY27 priority; future QIB or debt raises possible for larger capex.

rows.label: Rising rent per sq ft
rows.why: Average rent rose to about Rs 7,250-7,500 per sq ft in FY26 from Rs 7,000-7,250 in the last quarter, and management expects further increases.

rows.label: Balanced West/NCR and Southern growth; Eastern India later
rows.why: Management expects roughly 30% growth each in West/NCR and the Southern belt, with Eastern India to follow over time; no city-wise sign-up numbers were given.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 growth (~40% Design & Build, >50% Furniture, 18-20k Leasing seats) and 30%+ central EBITDA margin, but evasive on renewal data, captive/third-party split, debt quantum, and the AI question, where analysts pushed for data and got qualitative answers.

512008|2026-06.headline: EFC (I) Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29% YoY to ₹282.88 crore and PAT rose 52% YoY to ₹70.85 crore, with PAT margin at 25.1%.
512008|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was ₹282.88 crore, up about 29% YoY, and EBITDA was ₹122.96 crore, up about 20% YoY at a 43.5% margin. PAT grew about 52% YoY to ₹70.85 crore, helped by lower finance cost, which management attributed to rationalised borrowing costs. Leasing remained the largest segment at ₹153.91 crore revenue, while Design & Build and Furniture grew strongly YoY but Design & Build fell sequentially from about ₹120 crore in Q4. Analysts pressed on sequential EBITDA decline (down about 14% QoQ), Furniture margin compression, and the planned demerger/restructuring.

financial_highlights.change: +29% YoY (from ₹219.62 crore); down about 3% QoQ per analyst
+20% YoY (from ₹102.16 crore); down about 14% QoQ per analyst

segments.name: Leasing
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹153.91 crore (+26% YoY from ₹122.18 crore); segment result ₹64.33 crore. Managed workspace across 25 cities with over 84,000 total seats and over 68,000 billed seats.

segments.name: Design & Build
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹100.39 crore (vs ₹84.69 crore in Q1 FY26, about +19% YoY); segment result ₹33.84 crore. Order book above ₹228 crore, with management saying over 85% is external third-party work.

segments.name: Furniture (Ek Design)
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹28.57 crore (+124% YoY from ₹12.75 crore); segment result only ₹2.10 crore, a thin margin of about 7%. Order book about ₹53 crore; over 2,200 SKUs and over 75,000 units delivered to date.

guidance_outlook: Management is 100% confident of adding 18,000-20,000 billable seats in Leasing this fiscal year.
Design & Build targeted at roughly 50% YoY growth for FY27, which management says is backed by the existing order book.
Furniture expected to deliver similar growth; management expects EBITDA above 25% in the vertical at optimal capacity utilisation (60-70%), targeted by end of this year.
Margins are described as stable to improving, with no specific consolidated margin guidance given.
Demerger/restructuring: all subsidiaries to consolidate under EFC (I) Ltd, with EFC Ltd merged in and an asset-holding company kept as a wholly owned subsidiary; no timeline given on the call.
capex_capacity: Managed workspace capacity: over 84,000 total seats and over 68,000 billed seats across 25 cities; more inventory under development without revenue commitment.
Asset monetisation model: acquires vacant assets (about 10 years old), refurbishes and leases them via managed office, capturing rental yield and grade-upgrade appreciation.
Fit-out payback is about 18-20 months per seat on a ₹50,000 per-seat cost, which management says is standard across cities and funded mainly by landlords.
Furniture plant is still scaling; management says optimal utilisation is 60-70% and expects to approach it by end of FY27.
Borrowings are mainly LAP and LRD facilities tied to acquired assets; management says borrowing costs have been rationalised.
demand_pricing: Average occupancy stated at 90%+ and enterprise retention at about 95%+ (churn 4-5%); average enterprise client tenure rose to 51 months.
Enterprise demand from GCCs, MNCs, BFSI, technology, consulting and outsourcing firms.

D&B order book rose to over ₹228 crore from ₹135 crore at end of Q4 FY26, with over ₹100 crore of Q4 orders already executed. Management says Q1 is seasonally slow and projects typically ramp in Q3-Q4.
Competition named on the call: Awfi, Smartworks, WeWork India, IndiQube and large landlords; management cites price, speed of execution, design and fit-out cost optimisation as differentiators.
Management says supply-chain and material-price disruptions persist but have not stopped YoY growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the D&B (₹228 crore) and Furniture (₹53 crore) order books is third-party versus internal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said more than 85% is from external clients, since most internal fit-out work is already done by landlords.

qa_highlights.question: Why did D&B revenue fall from about ₹120 crore in Q4 to about ₹100 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said D&B is project-based with no seasonality; Q1 is typically slow, and projects ramp in Q3-Q4. It reiterated a roughly 50% YoY growth target.

qa_highlights.question: Furniture revenue rose 36% QoQ but segment margin fell from about 75% to about 7%; why?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nothing was wrong and that the business is still below optimal utilisation. It expects a stabilised EBITDA above 25% at 60-70% utilisation, and said QoQ margin comparison is not meaningful yet.

qa_highlights.question: Occupancy, retention and seat addition guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Occupancy is 90%+, retention about 95%+, and 18,000-20,000 billable seat additions are targeted with full confidence.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PAT rise while revenue and EBITDA fell QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the EBITDA dip to Ind AS accounting effects and pointed to PAT as the better measure. It cited lower borrowing costs, cost control, and Leasing performance.

qa_highlights.question: What differentiates EFC against Awfi, Smartworks, WeWork India and IndiQube, and what is the city mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the integrated real-estate-as-a-service model, three revenue streams, economies of scale, design and fit-out cost optimisation. It said the West is strongest; North and South are each above 15%; focus cities are 10 (3 North, 3 South, 3 West, plus Kolkata).

risks_watch: Sequential decline: revenue down about 3% and EBITDA down about 14% QoQ, with Design & Build lower than Q4; D&B growth depends on Q3-Q4 project ramp-up.
Furniture segment margin of about 7% in Q1 versus 25%+ target; sustainability depends on reaching 60-70% utilisation.
Reported PAT growth is driven partly by lower finance costs; watch interest cost and LAP/LRD leverage as asset-monetisation capex grows.
Demerger/restructuring details (timeline, tax treatment, accounting impact) were not specified and need follow-up.
Competitive intensity from Awfi, Smartworks, WeWork India, IndiQube and landlords; supply-chain and material-price pressures on D&B.
key_quotes: There's nothing wrong in the Furniture segment.
The EBITDA reduction is primarily because of the way the Ind AS accounting works.
100% confident on kind of adding about 18,000 to 20,000 billable seats on the Leasing business.
There's no seasonality, which is kind of affecting this business.
512008|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, order book visibility and the 50% D&B and 18,000-20,000 seat targets, but defensive on the sequential decline, Furniture margin (about 7%) and the EBITDA dip, which management attributed to Ind AS effects and pointed to PAT instead. Restructuring answers were high-level, with no timeline or accounting detail given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Furniture EBITDA target is above 25% at 60-70% utilisation by end FY27 (currently about 7% segment margin), and lower finance cost lifted PAT margin to 25.1% from 21.3%, but no consolidated margin guidance was given and EBITDA margin was 43.5%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management is 100% confident of adding 18,000-20,000 billable Leasing seats this fiscal year on a base of 68,000 billed seats (84,000 total), though seat capex and timing by quarter were not quantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Leasing revenue grew 26% YoY to Rs 153.91 crore on 90%+ occupancy, D&B targeted at about 50% YoY growth on a Rs 228 crore order book, and Furniture revenue rose 124% YoY to Rs 28.57 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Occupancy is 90%+ and asset-monetisation capex continues via LAP/LRD borrowings, but no new capex figure or board approval was disclosed; the 18,000-20,000 seat addition is largely landlord-funded at about Rs 50,000 per seat.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: D&B order book rose to over Rs 228 crore from Rs 135 crore at end Q4 FY26 (over 85% external), and management is targeting about 50% YoY D&B growth; upgrade depends on the Q3-Q4 ramp.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 revenue fell about 3% QoQ and EBITDA about 14% QoQ, D&B fell from about Rs 120 crore in Q4 to Rs 100 crore, and Furniture margin is about 7% versus a 25%+ target, so the Q1 dip could persist if the Q3-Q4 project ramp slips.

rows.label: D&B order book up to Rs 228 crore
rows.why: Order book rose to over Rs 228 crore from Rs 135 crore at end Q4 FY26, with over Rs 100 crore of Q4 orders already executed and projects ramping in Q3-Q4.

rows.label: Demerger / consolidation of subsidiaries into EFC (I) Ltd
rows.why: All subsidiaries to consolidate under EFC (I) Ltd with EFC Ltd merged in and an asset-holding company kept as wholly owned subsidiary, but no timeline, tax or accounting detail was given on the call.

rows.label: Lower borrowing costs lifting PAT
rows.why: Finance cost fell to Rs 10.35 crore from the previous quarter and PAT rose 52% YoY to Rs 70.85 crore versus revenue up 29%, though LAP/LRD leverage needs watching as asset monetisation grows.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 18,000-20,000 seat addition, the 50% D&B growth target and order book visibility, but defensive on the 14% QoQ EBITDA dip, the Furniture margin of about 7%, and the restructuring, which had no timeline.

512008|2026-09.headline: EFC (I) Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 30% YoY to ₹332 crore, with PAT up 36% to ₹77 crore and EBITDA margin near 40%.
512008|2026-09.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was about ₹332 crore versus ~₹255 crore a year earlier (+30%), with EBITDA of ~₹134 crore (+21%) and PAT of ~₹77 crore (+36%). H1 FY27 revenue was ~₹650 crore (+30%) and PAT ~₹148 crore (+43%), with EPS of ₹10.11 versus ₹7.09. Management outlined a proposed demerger of the leased-premise managed office business into the listed parent and the acquisition of Ultrafresh Modular Solutions via a share swap. Design & Build growth lagged the 50-60% annual target in H1, which management attributed to order book timing.

segments.name: Leasing (managed workspace)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ~₹168 crore (+30% YoY); H1 ~₹322 crore vs ₹252 crore. Management cites occupancy consistently above 90%, with no change quarter on quarter or year on year.

segments.name: Design & Build (turnkey contracting)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ~₹129 crore (+16% YoY); H1 ~₹230 crore vs ₹196 crore. Management targets 50-60% growth for FY27 and cites an order book of more than ₹300 crore.

segments.name: Furniture Manufacturing (Ek Design)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ~₹35 crore (+149% YoY); H1 ~₹63 crore vs ₹27 crore. Growth is from a small base, and management plans to improve capacity utilisation and inventory management.

guidance_outlook: Management says it is on track for annual targets across all three verticals and expects a stronger H2, consistent with prior years.
Design & Build FY27 growth target of 50-60% reaffirmed, supported by the order book, with Q3 and Q4 expected to be promising.

Long-term margin guidance: consolidated EBITDA above 20%; Leasing ~25% at corporate level and ~30% at centre level; Design & Build 18-22%; Furniture ~24-25% at optimal capacity; integrated margin 20-22% on an annualised basis.
Quarterly margins may fluctuate due to project execution cycles and expense timing; management said annualised margins will hold.
Design & Build working capital cycle guided at roughly 60-90 days (earlier 90-120 days), with retention around 5% of project value.
Demerger subject to NCLT and other approvals; management is confident of approval soon.
Ultrafresh acquisition expected to be EPS-accretive over the long term; integration and synergies are the immediate focus.
capex_capacity: Ultrafresh Modular Solutions acquired for ~₹54 crore via share swap at ₹270 per share, about 1.49x FY26 revenue; it has a manufacturing facility at Nalagarh, Himachal Pradesh, and more than 160 touch points across Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.

Proposed demerger filed with NCLT: the leased-premise managed office business moves into listed EFC (I) Ltd, and owned property stays in wholly owned subsidiary EFC Limited. Project-specific SPVs in Leasing are to fold into the listed entity.
Owned real estate is about 8-10% of the leasing portfolio; the company said it monetised a Pune property through an asset sale and leaseback, earning a 39-40% return on capital.
Management said it is evaluating further opportunities while maintaining capital allocation discipline.
demand_pricing: India office absorption was about 66 million sq ft in the first nine months of 2026, per management; the Indian furniture market is cited at ₹25-29 billion.
Enterprises and GCCs are prioritising flexible, managed workspace that avoids large upfront capex.
Management said material and service prices rose substantially in Q2, adding some margin pressure.
Pricing and quotations for internal group business are set competitively, with big-four firms used for arm's-length benchmarking.

qa_highlights.question: Pramod Mohan: What is portfolio occupancy across mature and new centres, and will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Nikhil Bhuta said occupancy is consistently above 90% and stable quarter on quarter and year on year, and expects this to continue.

qa_highlights.question: Pramod Mohan: Will consolidated margins normalise as Design & Build and Furniture grow in mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins are sustainable, with a consolidated EBITDA target above 20% and an integrated 20-22% annualised, while quarterly margins may vary.

qa_highlights.question: Pramod Mohan: What was the Sanvritti Alpha transaction?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a Pune property bought about a year earlier, redeveloped and fitted out, then sold to an investor on an asset sale and leaseback basis, with the company remaining operating partner. It said this generated a 39-40% return on capital and helps repay asset-backed debt (LRD/LAP).

qa_highlights.question: Sahil Singh: Can Design & Build reach 50-60% growth given H1 growth of only 16-17%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is on target, citing an order book above ₹300 crore and expecting Q3 and Q4 to be strong, and that quarterly numbers are not the right indicator.

qa_highlights.question: Sahil Singh: Why did EBITDA grow 21% when revenue grew 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap to timing differences in leasing development costs and revenue recognition and to sharp increases in material and service prices in the quarter, saying annualised margins will hold.

qa_highlights.question: Vishal Kunden: What was the rationale for the ₹54 crore Ultrafresh share swap and its valuation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited northern manufacturing access, the Tier 2 and Tier 3 distribution network, and modular product expansion. It said the deal was valued at about 1.49x FY26 revenue, with shares valued at ₹270 each by big-four valuers, and expects EPS accretion over time.

qa_highlights.question: Ashutosh Chaudhary: Could receivables and working capital grow disproportionately as Design & Build scales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is working-capital intensive but not disproportionate. Cycles are around 60-90 days depending on project, with retention about 5% of project value and milestone-based billing for institutional clients.

qa_highlights.question: Shailendra: What is the rationale for the demerger, its structure, timeline and arm's-length dealing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the demerger separates asset-light leasing (into the listed parent) from owned property (in EFC Limited) to give clearer capital allocation and ROCE. Related-party pricing is said to be arm's length, benchmarked by big-four firms and reported to SEBI.

risks_watch: Design & Build H1 growth of 16-17% against the 50-60% full-year target. Watch whether Q3 and Q4 close the gap.
Q2 EBITDA growth (21%) lagged revenue growth (30%). Watch whether margins recover as guided.
Working capital and receivables as Design & Build scales; watch debtor days and retention balances.
Pending NCLT approval for the demerger, plus its cost and timeline, which were not quantified on the call.
Ultrafresh integration risk and the dilution from the share swap.
512008|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth and margins, but defensive when questioned on the Design & Build target gap and the margin trend, where it repeatedly redirected to annualised figures. Answers on related-party pricing and the demerger were long and general, with few specifics on cost or timeline.
key_quotes: Our ambition is not simply to build a larger EFC, but to build a stronger, more competitive and more valuable EFC, one that delivers consistent performance and create long-term value for all stakeholders.
So we are absolutely confident on achieving the targets that have been set.
Margin comparison should happen on an annualized level.
So believe this is absolutely EPS-accretive transactions in the long-term.

512068|2026-03.headline: Deccan Gold turned debt-free after Rs.315 Cr rights issue; Jonnagiri gold sales and Geomysore profit flowed in, but Kyrgyz project needs Rs.60-100 Cr more.
512068|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as a defining quarter: Rs.315 Cr rights issue used to repay about Rs.219 Cr of debt, leaving the company debt-free by end-March. The associate Geomysore (26% stake, Jonnagiri gold project) began selling refined gold and reported profit, which management said flowed into Deccan's books. Kyrgyzstan (60%) gravity circuit is commissioned, with Merrill-Crowe/leach circuit targeted for June-July and full-scale commercial production in August 2026. Management disclosed a funding gap after Rs.55 Cr was diverted to Geomysore's rights issue, and said it is talking to promoter-linked investors for Rs.60-100 Cr; an EGM on related-party transactions is scheduled. Bhalukona nickel-copper-PGE drilling is showing wide mineralised intersections, with mining lease application targeted by April 2027.

financial_highlights.value: Rs.219 Cr (largely Hira Group and Godavari Power & Ispat)
About Rs.31 Cr: interest income Rs.18.3 Cr plus currency exchange gain balance

financial_highlights.metric: Jonnagiri gold production March and April 2026
Jonnagiri refined gold produced to end-March 2026

financial_highlights.value: About Rs.3,000 per gram vs market about Rs.16,000 per gram

segments.name: Jonnagiri (Geomysore, 26%)
segments.commentary: Open pit operating at 1,000 tpd licence capacity (about 300,000 tpa), recovery above 90%; FY27 production guided at about 600 kg, FY28 about 800 kg-1 t; FY27 revenue about Rs.900 Cr, EBITDA about Rs.630 Cr, PAT about Rs.470 Cr, with Deccan's 26% share about Rs.120 Cr, though management expects no dividend in FY27.

segments.name: Altyn Tor, Kyrgyzstan (60%, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Gravity concentrate production started; Merrill-Crowe and leach circuit to produce doré from June, full commercial production by August 2026. FY27 production guided at about 160 kg and FY28 at 300-350 kg; FY27 revenue about Rs.300 Cr, PAT about Rs.100 Cr (Deccan share about Rs.60 Cr). Processes about 1.6 Mt tailings and low-grade stockpiles (about 1-1.1 g/t) for about four years; 17% revenue share with Kyrgyzaltyn and 5% royalty to government.

segments.name: Bhalukona, Chhattisgarh (100%, nickel-copper-PGE)
segments.commentary: Seven diamond holes, 1,200 m drilled; first hole intersected about 30 m of sulphide mineralisation (about 0.4% Ni), including 2.6 m at 1.01% Ni, 0.29% Cu and 0.2 g/t Pd. Management's indicative resource is 75,000-80,000 t nickel-equivalent and about 7-8 t gold-equivalent, unverified.

segments.name: Ganajur (Karnataka)
segments.commentary: Gold deposit under litigation (High Court and Supreme Court, Indocil case); no ruling in the quarter. Management said timeline to production is about 2.5-3 years if the case is won.

segments.name: Gold-tungsten-tin, Spain (Logrosan)
segments.commentary: MoU to acquire 51% for EUR1.76 million with rights to go to 95%; 4 holes and about 1,500 m drilled, assays pending about 1-2 weeks. Earlier historic hole: 1 m at 96.2 g/t Au.

segments.name: Kalevala Gold, Finland
segments.commentary: Three projects (Syrjala about 2 Mt resource targeted to 4 t, Pahkalampi about 2 t at 3.5 g/t, 4P undrilled); company can go to 51%. Little work done this year due to funding constraints.

segments.name: Mozambique and Tanzania
segments.commentary: Mozambique lithium-tantalum surface targets identified, drilling deferred for lack of funds. Tanzania: three of five tenements relinquished, exploration focus reduced.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated targets (at current prices): Jonnagiri about 600 kg, Kyrgyzstan about 160 kg; FY28 Jonnagiri about 800 kg-1 t, Kyrgyzstan 300-350 kg.
Kyrgyzstan full-scale commercial production by August 2026; plant inauguration pencilled for 15 or 31 August.
Management funding need: at least Rs.60 Cr (outer limit Rs.100 Cr) for Kyrgyzstan; Rs.400-500 Cr for Bhalukona processing plant; Rs.800-1,000 Cr aggregate across projects in the next year or so.
Bhalukona mining lease application due by about April 2027; Spain mining lease application by October-November 2026.
2030 vision: Jonnagiri 1 tpa, Altyn Tor 700-800 kg, first Indian nickel-copper-PGE mine, and two to three gold mines plus critical minerals in production.
capex_capacity: Jonnagiri 1,000 tpd plant capex about Rs.350-400 Cr; Bhalukona processing plant about Rs.400 Cr; Spain about Rs.500 Cr (Finland underground would need more).
Kyrgyzstan underground development (decline) estimated at Rs.50-100 Cr, starting after three to four years, to be funded from internal accruals per management.
Jonnagiri expansion beyond 2,000 tpd needs public hearing and permits; clarity expected in 6-8 months, reflected in FY28 numbers.
Kyrgyzstan revised resource estimate to state reserve company by end-June; revised mine design and life-of-mine plan by August 2026.
Bhalukona: 2,000-3,000 tpd plant potentially, 15-year life, if resource is proven to 200 m depth.
demand_pricing: Model assumptions: gold about Rs.15,000/g for Jonnagiri and about $4,000/oz for Kyrgyzstan, a discount to spot. Management said there is no hedging policy.
Royalties: Jonnagiri pays 4% to Andhra Pradesh plus 1.28% (DMF and NMET), about 5.28% of top line; Kyrgyzstan 5% royalty plus 17% revenue share to Kyrgyzaltyn.
Jonnagiri refined 999 gold sold to bullion refiners and jewellers at IBJA price; Kyrgyz doré must be sold to National Bank (right of first refusal) at LBMA price less refining charges.
Bhalukona concentrate expected to be sold to smelters (Adani or Vedanta named); management said crude-price impact on Kyrgyz costs is under 5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is other income so high and what is its breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about Rs.18.3 Cr is interest income on the Kyrgyz loan at 15% and the balance is currency exchange gain, totalling about Rs.31 Cr.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the Rs.100 Cr needed in the next three months, and can it come from internal accruals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs.100 Cr is an outer limit; actual need is about Rs.60 Cr over two to three years. Geomysore dividends may not come in FY27, so the company is talking to promoter-linked investors for debt or equity.

qa_highlights.question: Who are the promoters providing funds, and is any promoter selling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the funding is from key promoter-group investors and an Australian promoter; Yandal Investments (about 10%) and Halcyon (about 5%) are not selling, with sales coming from retail promoter-group holders.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for Bhalukona mining lease and what could be the next production asset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the mining lease application is due by about April 2027, with plant design then and production possibly around 2029; Bhalukona is the next candidate, with Spain also filing by Oct-Nov 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Is an FPO or preferential issue planned and is the team ready?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has been in touch with merchant bankers and FPO planning would follow the present projects; it committed to nothing specific on timing.

risks_watch: Kyrgyz funding gap of Rs.60-100 Cr must close before winter construction; a bank transfer delay of a month would push completion months later.
Ganajur litigation outcome is unresolved; management is pursuing government policy routes.
Geomysore dividends not expected in FY27, so Deccan's Rs.120 Cr PAT share may not translate into cash; Kyrgyz loan repayments with 15% interest depend on production starting.
Bhalukona and Spain drill assays are pending and the Bhalukona resource figures are management's own geological estimates, not a JORC resource.
Gold price assumptions are below spot, but there is no hedging policy; a sharp fall in gold prices would hit revenue projections directly.
Management confirmed that Jonnagiri's FY27 revenue and profit forecasts assume about 600 kg; delays have occurred in past timelines.
512068|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and promotional on project potential (Bhalukona described as a personal favourite, Jonnagiri as transformational), but cautious on funding and timelines, repeatedly saying figures are indicative and not committing to dates. Evasive on several questions: no concrete answer on Geomysore IPO or reverse merger, and deferred the FPO question to after project milestones.
key_quotes: One of our associate companies that is Geomysore has recorded a profit and we could show some profit as a 26% shareholder of that Company.
We repaid all the debt that is about Rs.219 crores.
So we require up to Rs.100 Crores at least minimum Rs.60 Crores we require to complete that Kyrgyz project.
So by next April, we have to submit the mining lease application.
Rs.100 Crores is the completely outer limit that we are taking in case of any emergencies, but the actual requirement is around Rs.60 Crores.
