512068|2026-06.headline: Deccan Gold Q1 FY27: Jonnagiri sold 59 kg gold for ~Rs87 Cr revenue, Rs6.35 Cr share of PAT; Rs137 Cr fundraise approved by Board.
512068|2026-06.overview: Management said the June quarter established the company as a producer, led by Jonnagiri (Geomysore Services) gold production and first dore output from Altyn Tor (Kyrgyzstan). Jonnagiri sold about 59 kg of gold for about Rs87 Cr revenue and Rs25 Cr PAT, of which Deccan's share was Rs6.35 Cr; about 80 kg of gold equivalent sits in inventory. Management framed the company as having two verticals, gold and battery-metal critical minerals, and said Rs137 Cr of CCDs, equity and warrants is pending shareholder approval. Management said the next quarter should be much bigger, but margins were low in Q1 and the company asked for another quarter before giving clearer guidance.

financial_highlights.metric: Gold inventory at quarter end (incl. dore)
financial_highlights.value: About 80 kg gold equivalent (40 kg gold + 60 kg dore)
Rs137 Cr via CCDs, equity shares and warrants

segments.name: Jonnagiri (Geomysore, gold, India)
segments.commentary: Q1 sales of 59 kg gold for about Rs87 Cr revenue and Rs25 Cr PAT; Deccan's share Rs6.35 Cr. Production about 1 kg/day, with 2,500 tpd expansion planned, targeting up to 2 tonnes/yr around FY29-30.

segments.name: Altyn Tor (Kyrgyzstan, gold)
segments.commentary: Dore production started via Merrill-Crowe; gravity circuit and leach circuit added. Full-scale commissioning expected soon; tailings of about 0.6 Mt at about 1.3 g/t for first 4-5 years of output.

segments.name: Kalevala (Finland, gold)
segments.commentary: Drilling to start around Sept 15; about 1,500 m planned. Kuikka mining lease pending; feasibility targeted in 2027; production seen 2028-29 or later with about 800 tpd plant.

segments.name: Critical minerals (Chhattisgarh nickel-copper-PGE, Bhalukona)
segments.commentary: 2,500 m drilled, 1.3 km mineralised zone identified; resource estimate and mining lease application targeted next year; 3,000 tpd plant considered.

segments.name: Logrosan tungsten (Spain)
segments.commentary: About 3,000 m drilled; full Dehesa results expected mid-September, resource model by early October; 1,000 tpd plant considered.

segments.name: Mozambique lithium-tantalum
segments.commentary: About 150 sq km, three licences; 200 tpd concentrator targeted by end-2027 or Q1 2028 for concentrate.

guidance_outlook: Jonnagiri FY27 production 500-600 kg (earlier guidance retained); FY28 750-800 kg. Management will confirm after next quarter.
Altyn Tor: about 150-160 kg in FY27 and 300-350 kg thereafter, per management comments.
Jonnagiri EBITDA margin expected to stabilise at 65-70% within one to two quarters; Q1 margins were significantly lower.

capex_capacity: Jonnagiri processing approvals of 1,010 tpd, with expansion to 2,500 tpd being sought; Bhumi Puja done for expansion.
Altyn Tor leach circuit and new tailings dam (10-year life) under construction; commissioning date to be announced after Chairman-level visit next week.
Finland: about 1,500 m drilling from mid-September; Kuikka pit targets about 70 kg gold; underground mines planned.
Chhattisgarh: 15th drill hole under way; plan 3,000 tpd plant; process flow sheet by mid-next-year.
Spain: Dehesa first-phase drilling complete; Maria drilling from end of this month; 40 sq km Maria licence plus 30 sq km pending.
Mozambique: 1,500-2,000 m drilling from September; 200 tpd concentrator by end-2027.
demand_pricing: Management said gold price in Q1 was about Rs1,50,000 per 10 grams and improved in the current quarter, supporting holding inventory.
Tungsten prices up 622% and tantalum up 196% over the last year; lithium up 108%; graphite up 5% (management figures).
Management plans to sell Jonnagiri stock in the coming quarter; Q1 sales lagged production because the inauguration was on June 24.
Dore from Jonnagiri is refined in-house at a small refinery (cost about Rs4-5 Cr); Altyn Tor dore must go to a government refinery at LBMA price.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Jonnagiri profit margin well below the expected ~65% EBITDA, and what is the outlook for Jonnagiri and Kyrgyzstan revenue and profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said low Q1 sales (59 kg) and initial expenses explain the low margin; 65-70% EBITDA margin expected in one to two quarters. Further clarity expected next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex estimate and funding plan for the project pipeline (about Rs2,000 Cr)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said more than Rs1,000 Cr is needed for the next two or three projects; funding via offtake arrangements for critical minerals, combined debt and equity; gold projects possibly 50:50 or 40:60 equity to debt.

qa_highlights.question: Will Bhalukona be funded by a rights issue like the earlier Rs80 per share issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not confirm a specific route; said the Rs137 Cr raise is a bridge and a larger QIP may follow once drilling outcomes are clearer.

qa_highlights.question: Will Hutti Gold and Ganajur progress, and what is the legal position?
qa_highlights.answer: Ganajur is a mining lease with court proceedings pending; management cited recent judgments on restoring pre-2015 rights. Hutti is a prospecting licence, so it is more tedious; focus remains on Ganajur.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be dividends from Jonnagiri, and is a strategic promoter being sought?
qa_highlights.answer: Dividend depends on Geomysore board; management doubts dividends this financial year. No decision yet on a large strategic promoter; the company remains professionally run.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the company not refine dore in Kyrgyzstan?
qa_highlights.answer: Kyrgyz law requires dore to be sent to a government refinery, which settles at LBMA price; no in-house refinery is possible there.

risks_watch: Jonnagiri margin normalisation: management guided EBITDA to stabilise at 65-70% within one to two quarters, versus Q1 margins well below that; Q1 PAT of about Rs25 Cr on Rs87 Cr revenue (about 29%) is the key test next quarter.

Inventory realisation: about 80 kg gold equivalent (40 kg gold + 60 kg dore) unsold at quarter end, plus about 90 kg expected in Q2; sales timing depends on gold price and the Q1 consolidated inventory line was unchanged in P&L.

Funding gap: management cited more than Rs1,000 Cr needed for the next two to three projects (about Rs2,000 Cr overall in analyst framing), with Rs137 Cr raise subject to shareholder approval; mix of offtake, debt and equity not finalised; QIP may follow.
Ganajur court case: no regular hearing yet; outcome depends on court and on mining lease status; Hutti remains a prospecting licence.

Altyn Tor commissioning date not yet fixed (to be announced after Chairman visit next week); revised mine design and life-of-mine plan due by October 2026; Jonnagiri dividend to Deccan unlikely in FY27 per management.

Exploration catalysts due next quarter: Dehesa full results by mid-September, resource model by early October; Kalevala drilling from about 15 September; Chhattisgarh resource estimate and mining lease application next year.
key_quotes: As a snapshot, it has established us as clearly as producers.
I think the next quarter is going to be much bigger than this.
So, to stabilize to about 65%, 70% of EBITDA, I believe it will take another quarter or two.
Hence, I honestly, I doubt whether we get dividends in this financial year.
So, we cannot have a refinery of our own in Kyrgyzstan.
I think please give us time till the next quarter.

512179|2026-03.headline: Sunteck FY26 presales rose 25% to INR3,157 crore and FY26 PAT grew 34% to INR202 crore; management guides similar growth for FY27.
512179|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 presales were INR1,064 crore (up 22%) and Q4 collections were INR432 crore (up 39%). Q4 operating revenue was INR339 crore with EBITDA of INR97 crore (29% margin) and PAT of INR63 crore (19% margin). For FY26, revenue was INR1,124 crore (up 32%), EBITDA INR305 crore (27% margin, up 64%) and PAT INR202 crore (18% margin, up 34%). Business development spend rose to over INR800 crore from under INR200 crore in FY25, adding three projects with about INR50bn GDV, and net debt/equity stayed at 0.06x.

segments.name: Uber luxury and premium luxury
segments.commentary: Management says these segments drive a growing share of presales; uber luxury and other commercial were about 50% of current sales (about INR600 crore), premium luxury 40-45% (INR360-370 crore in Q4). Q4 uber luxury (BKC and Nepean Sea Road) sales were INR609 crore, about INR1,500 crore in 12 months.

segments.name: Aspirational luxury
segments.commentary: Contributed about 10-15% of current sales (INR94-100 crore); management sees early demand recovery on lower home loan rates and tax benefits.

segments.name: Redevelopment and new acquisitions
segments.commentary: Three projects added in FY26 with about INR50bn combined GDV: Andheri Western Express Highway redevelopment (1-2.5 acres), Mira Road joint development (3.5 acres), and outright Andheri airport-side 1.75 acre land. Total GDV stands at about INR441bn gross of presales.

guidance_outlook: FY27 presales growth guided at a similar rate to FY26 (about 25%), with management 'very confident' even excluding Dubai.
Recently signed projects expected at 30-35% EBITDA margin; blended margin about 35-40%; minimum 30-35% per project for any new acquisition, redevelopment or JV/JD.
FY27 collections to improve as a share of sales; management expects strong cash flow in FY27 and FY28.

Approximately INR6,000-7,000 crore GDV of launches planned over the next 12 months, including Andheri redevelopment, Sunteck Sky Park Mira Road tower, two towers at Sunteck Beach Residences Vasai, new phase at Sunteck World Naigaon, Mira Road acquisition, and Nepean Sea Road.
Revenue recognition expected from Sunteck One World Naigaon delivery in FY27 plus ready inventory.
Business development spend in FY27 to be higher, subject to maintaining high IRR and equity multiple.

512296|2026-03.headline: Bhagyanagar India crossed ₹2,000 crore revenue and ₹50 crore PAT in FY26; Q4 revenue ₹735 crore, PAT ₹18.5 crore, EBITDA margin ~5%.
512296|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 as a record year: revenue above ₹2,000 crore, operational EBITDA above ₹100 crore and PAT above ₹50 crore for the first time. Q4 was the best quarter of the year, with revenue of about ₹735 crore, EBITDA of about ₹36 crore and PAT of about ₹18.5 crore. Volumes rose about 34% to 24,000 tonnes, and value-added share reached about 62% by Q4 (from 52% in Q1). Management guided to roughly 5% EBITDA margin, 20% volume growth and a 25% revenue CAGR, and said the demerger into copper and real estate verticals awaits NCLT hearing on 9 June.

Q1 FY27: volume marginally below Q4 but well above Q1 FY26 (Q1 FY26 revenue about ₹486 crore); EBITDA margin expected to hold near 5%.

512296|2026-06.headline: Bhagyanagar India Q1 FY27: revenue above ₹700 crore and EBITDA margin a record 5.43%, but volume fell to 5,200-5,278 tons on April-May supply disruption.
512296|2026-06.overview: Management reported revenue of over ₹700 crore, PAT of ₹20 crore (up 9.5% QoQ, 167% YoY), and a record 5.43% EBITDA margin. Volume fell to 5,278 tons (down 9.5% QoQ, 6.5% YoY) because trade-route disruption and material shortages hit April and May. Management said June volume alone was 2,200 tons and supply had normalised, and it cut FY27 volume growth guidance to 12-15% from about 15-20%. Margin gains in April-May came from shortage-driven realisations across commodity and value-added products, and management guided to 5-5.5% EBITDA margin for the rest of the year.

financial_highlights.change: Lower volume; no YoY figure stated
Commodity exports are the bulk of this
Relates to FY2022-23 supplier registration cancellation; company plans to contest in tribunal

segments.commentary: Management said margins improved across commodity and value-added products during the shortage. Commodity exports are the main part of the 18% export share.

segments.name: Value-added products
segments.commentary: 63% of Q1 sales, the highest so far. Target is 63-64% for FY27, rising about 1-2% a year toward 68-69% over 3-4 years. About 250 tons of tin-coated product sold in Q1, with about 600 tons estimated for data centers.

segments.name: Copper business restructuring (Tieramet)
segments.commentary: All copper business moves from Bhagyanagar Copper to new wholly-owned subsidiary Tieramet Limited, then Bhagyanagar Copper merges into the parent and Tieramet is demerged. Parent keeps three city land parcels and the windmill project. NCLT hearing is set for 7 August 2026.

capex_capacity: 35,000 metric tons of capacity has been added and is online now.

CTC wire capacity is about 80 tons per month, moving to 150 tons per month after a new 48-conductor machine (earlier about 28 conductors).
Two Hyderabad units: a 4-acre and a 60-acre facility. Capex of ₹40 crore is planned over FY27-FY28.
demand_pricing: Management cites third-party data: India copper consumption about 2.4 million tons by 2030; secondary copper demand to double from 0.7 to 1.4 million tons in five years.
Recycled copper market in India said to grow at 12-13% CAGR by some estimates; overall copper market 5-6% (or about 8.5% in other reports). Company says it is growing at 2-2.5x the market rate.
Primary copper refining charges have turned negative; Indian primary producers (Vedanta, Hindalco, Adani) are buying recycled copper.
Margins are set as a percentage of LME: raw material purchases at 86-95% of LME. Management says percentage margin is more stable than rupees per kg.
Data center: 800V DC architecture could cut copper bus bar demand by about 50%; management said this would have no material impact on the company.

Customers added: Crompton Greaves, TMC and Atlanta (transformers); Blue Star, Micron, OBO and L&T (Al data center bus bars). More than 100 tons of bus bars exported to North America in the last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Has sourcing normalised, and is 15-20% volume growth still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said June normalised supply, so FY27 volume growth is now guided at 12-15%. Average realisation is expected to be about 30% higher YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 EBITDA per kg so high, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to shortage-driven realisations in April-May across commodity and value-added products, not exports. From June, margins are back to a normal 5-5.5% range.

qa_highlights.question: What was the GST impact of ₹17-18 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Surendra Bhutoria said it relates to FY2022-23 scrap purchases from a supplier whose registration was cancelled retrospectively. ₹17 crore was deposited and the company is contesting the case at the tribunal, which it believes it will win.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company's value-added mix changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Value-added share is targeted at 63-64% for FY27, rising gradually toward 68-69% over 3-4 years. Management said it will not jump as it did in the last two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 5,000 crore FY30 revenue target and debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated ₹5,000 crore by FY30 regardless of copper price. Debt is projected at ₹300-350 crore by 2030, and management says the 5% EBITDA margin cash flow will fund growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fundraise timing and purpose?
qa_highlights.answer: First tranche of ₹52 crore is finalised, with funds expected in August. A second tranche is expected around March after the demerger. Management said MCX margin funding depends on copper prices.

512329|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 reported EBITDA of INR56 crores, of which INR50 crores business EBITDA, with management reiterating FY27 annualised EBITDA of INR300-350 crores.
512329|2026-03.overview: SG Mart delivered its strongest quarter by revenue (above INR1,800 crores) and EBITDA of INR56 crores in Q4 FY26, despite a disrupted March from the Middle East crisis. Underlying business EBITDA was about INR50 crores, with INR6 crores of inventory gain; FY26 EBITDA rose 35% to INR137 crores. Working capital was cut to 20 days, operating cash flow was about INR300 crores, and net cash closed at INR750 crores. Steel shortages hit the B2B trading volume and renewable structures, while service centres and the new steel profile business ramped up. Management kept FY27 guidance of INR300-350 crores annualised EBITDA, subject to war-related disruption.

segments.name: B2B metal trading
segments.commentary: Volume fell versus Q3 on steel supply shortage that began in January and worsened with the war; April and May commitments described as slow. EBITDA of INR700-1,000 per ton, and management says it contributes little to earnings.

segments.name: Service centres (India and Dubai)
segments.commentary: Q4 volume about 190,000-191,000 tons vs 163,000 tons in Q3, with Dubai at 37,000 tons (about 10%). Per-ton EBITDA of INR1,700-2,000. Stock-and-sell is about 20-25% of volume; cut-to-length about 75%.

segments.name: Renewable structures
segments.commentary: Q4 volume slightly down on coated steel shortage; monthly average about 5,000 tons. Per-ton EBITDA of INR3,000-5,000. FY27 volume guided at 130,000-150,000 tons; capacity is about 150,000 tons a year with no further capex needed.

segments.name: Steel profiles (incl. puff panels)
segments.commentary: New line launched in Q4 with about 7,000 tons, sold under APL Apollo brand and group network. April run-rate 5,000-6,000 tons. Per-ton EBITDA of INR5,000-8,000; puff panel margins guided at 5-8%. Profile capacity about 120,000 tons per annum; FY27 volume guided at 100,000+ tons.

guidance_outlook: FY27 annualised EBITDA guidance of INR300-350 crores retained; management said it should be near that unless war-related losses in B2B or Middle East operations deepen.
Quarterly business EBITDA of about INR50 crores expected to keep rising through FY27; management sees no deterioration in per-ton EBITDA spreads in Q1 FY27.
Renewable structures FY27 volume of 130,000-150,000 tons, with monthly volume rising from 5,000-6,000 to 8,000-9,000 tons once coated steel supply improves.
Service centre network to reach 11-12 by end of FY27 (three additions); FY27 renewable plus profile volumes expected above 230,000 tons combined.

Three-year targets: about 20 service centres at 8,000-10,000 tons per month each (about 2 million tons annualised exit run-rate), 250,000-300,000 tons renewables, 300,000 tons profiles; B2B volume not guided.
capex_capacity: Approved capex of about INR600 crores over FY27-FY28 described as the minimum; roughly one-third for service centre build-out, about half for land acquisition (at least four or five land parcels), and 15-20% for profile machines.
Land acquired in Ahmedabad, Indore and Kolkata; active scouting in Hyderabad, Chennai and Punjab, with more land acquisitions expected in the next two to three months.
Plan to add three service centres in FY27; a cut-to-length machine is being added at the Dubai centre.

Renewable capacity of about 150,000 tons is sufficient for FY27 with no new capex; additional lead time for machines is three to four months, and capacity is added once volume reaches about 10,000 tons per month for four to five months.
Puff panel capacity of 80,000 tons being set up against an industry size of about 150,000 tons (per the presentation).
demand_pricing: Steel supply shortage (linked to gas supply to steel mills) constrained B2B and coated steel supply; management expects improvement in May and June but says timing is unpredictable.
Dubai service centre (about 10% of volume) disrupted by the war; March business was almost nil and teams are only now returning.
Management says the company has moved away from low-margin B2B trading toward value-added verticals; trading is not expected to grow much.
Management says JSW and other platforms are in different product areas, with no direct overlap in SG Mart's value-added products.
Management stated the inventory loss in Q3 was about INR15-20 crores and the FY26 full-year EBITDA would have been above INR150 crores after adjusting for steel price swings.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost and other income decline QoQ despite a rise in cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed lower interest cost to working capital cut to 20 days and surplus cash. Net cash was INR750 crores vs INR740 crores in Q3, so the increase was only INR10 crores because of INR250 crores of capex.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27-28 capex plan and its split?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR600 crores approved over two years as the minimum, roughly one-third for service centres, half for land, and 15-20% for profile machines.

qa_highlights.question: What exercise price applies to the ESOP approval?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the exercise price is INR367, set about 1.5 years ago, and the approval covers balance unused ESOPs from the existing pool with no new issuance.

qa_highlights.question: Why does PAT growth lag EBITDA growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher depreciation from the fixed-asset build-out of service centres and renewable and profile capacity, plus interest cost. Management says cash profit growth should track EBITDA growth.

qa_highlights.question: What was the inventory impact on FY26 EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Q3 had an inventory loss of about INR15-20 crores and Q4 an inventory gain of INR6 crores; H1 saw few price swings.

qa_highlights.question: What is per-ton EBITDA by vertical?
qa_highlights.answer: B2B INR700-1,000; B2B stable band INR1,800-2,100 (as stated); renewable structures INR3,000-5,000; steel profiles INR5,000-8,000; service centres INR1,700-2,000 per ton.

Dubai operations (about 10% of service centre volume) and Middle East disruption; management did not quantify the Dubai profit hit beyond fixed costs in March.
Unresolved analyst query on consolidated-minus-standalone gross margin and net block (about INR108 crores difference cited); management disputed the figure on the call and said it would revert.
Depreciation and interest costs are holding PAT growth (about 10-11%) well below EBITDA growth (35%); the gap is expected to persist for about two years of heavy capex.
Capital allocation: management plans no dividend for about two years; cash on books may be used for working capital as the business scales.

512455|2026-03.headline: Lloyds Metals Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA rose 498% YoY to INR1,679 crore at a 33.73% margin; FY27 iron ore guidance is 26 million tons.

rows.why: Chemaf will not produce in FY27 and meaningful output is guided only from July 2027, about 90,000 t over 3-5 years, dependent on sulfuric acid supply being solved within about three months and on plants being completed (85-90% complete).

rows.label: Debt-funded capex at 1-1.5x EBITDA
rows.why: About INR15,000 crore consolidated capex in FY27 with debt at 1-1.5x EBITDA and no equity planned, plus Chemaf roughly USD330 million non-recourse and a further USD200 million asset-level borrowing, against standalone net debt of INR3,901 crore at 31 Mar 2026.

rows.label: Hedri to Ghugus pipeline cuts logistics cost
rows.why: The 195 km pipeline is in advanced planning and expected to cut logistics cost by more than INR500/t for most iron ore output, but no commissioning date was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on pellet ramp-up, margins, FY27 volumes and the Chandrapur steel plant, but evasive on consolidated receivables rising to INR1,480 crore from INR171 crore, the FY27 revenue and EBITDA bridge and Congo capex, while analysts pressed on the Tata Steel slurry pipeline exclusivi

512455|2026-06.headline: Lloyds Metals Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 127% YoY to INR5,413 crore with record 39.2% EBITDA margin.
512455|2026-06.overview: Standalone revenue reached INR5,413 crore (up 127% YoY, up 10% QoQ), EBITDA INR2,120 crore (up 172% YoY) and PAT INR1,527 crore (up 141% YoY). Management attributes the margin gain to the slurry pipeline cutting logistics costs, higher realisations and a richer value-added mix, with pellets now 41% of standalone revenue. Second pellet plant reached 100% utilisation within four months of its May 2026 commissioning. Thriveni (mining subsidiary) grew revenue 63% YoY but margins were hit by fuel costs, with pass-through negotiations ongoing. Management also outlined large capex (about INR11,000-11,500 crore per year for two years, rising to INR15,000-20,000 crore in year three) and Chemaf/copper JV financing that is still pending.

segments.name: Iron ore (standalone)
segments.commentary: Production 6.05 million tons (+53% YoY), sales 5.46 million tons (+58% YoY); realisation INR6,068/t and EBITDA INR2,230/t. Management said realisation was flat YoY; higher internal consumption reduced merchant sales.

segments.name: DRI and power
segments.commentary: DRI sales 1,83,920 tons (+133% YoY) at INR27,376/t realisation and INR6,273/t EBITDA; power volumes up 87% YoY.

segments.name: Pellets
segments.commentary: Production 1.69 million tons, 100% utilisation within four months of second plant start in May 2026; realisation INR11,783/t, EBITDA INR5,803/t. Sales mix 75.3% domestic, 24.7% export.

segments.name: Thriveni (mining and logistics)
segments.commentary: Iron ore volumes including BHQ 19.09 million tons (nearly 2x from 9.87 million tons). Gadchiroli ROM handling capacity raised from 10 to 55 million tpa; 12.83 million tons produced in the quarter. Odisha volume guided to 34-35 million tons in FY27 (+39%).

segments.name: Copper (Chemaf / JV)
segments.commentary: Existing DRC asset running at about 800 tons per month (about 2,400 tons per quarter); larger JV asset carries about $800 million+ book size and needs about $300 million+ more capex, targeted for operation in Q1 FY28.

guidance_outlook: Thriveni FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 28-30% reiterated, though the Q1 figure was impacted by fuel costs; pass-through talks are underway.
Thriveni logistics EBITDA margin expected to rise from 32% to 40% via EV/LNG fleet shift (200 more vehicles, 50 LNG and 150 EV).
Odisha iron ore volumes expected at 34-35 million tons in FY27; Laserda-Pacheri (1.5 mtpa) started in Q1 and Dalpahar (3 mtpa) expected Q2 FY27.
Steel plant (1.2 mtpa long products) targeted for commissioning by March 2027; BHQ beneficiation by March 2028 with recovery of 38% vs 35% originally planned.
Chemaf financial closure expected in 3-4 months; debt restructuring expected to cut consolidated debt by about 40-50% (roughly $700-800 million).
capex_capacity: Capex of INR13,513 crore in FY24-FY26 and INR3,005 crore in Q1 FY27; about INR8,500 crore planned for FY27 excluding the Konsari steel project, with INR11,000-11,500 crore over the next two years.
Capex guidance for year three is INR15,000-20,000 crore, with further increase once the steel plant is included; copper PNG (Panguna) project excluded and still at study stage.
Foreign (copper JV) capex of about $300 million+ to be spent over the next nine months, with financing (equity and debt) closure expected in about three months.
BHQ beneficiation: 30 million tpa throughput across 9 modules, about 16-17 million tons of saleable output in two phases.
Pellet conversion ratio about 1.07 t iron ore per t pellet; pellet to DRI about 1.5; about 2 t iron ore per t steel.
demand_pricing: Iron ore realisation flat at about INR6,000/t YoY; management said pricing is unpredictable and is not forecasting it.
Pellet export mix about 25%; export markets include Kenya, South Africa, South Korea, Indonesia and China; about 3/4 domestic and 1/4 export by volume.
Slurry pipeline saves about INR500-550/t on pellet cost.
About 2.4 million tons of iron ore and pellet to be consumed internally by FY28 (1.4 million additional for the steel plant), per management.
Thriveni external contracts: Tata Steel MDO volume 3-4 million tons; NTPC and OMC contracts growing 3-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did iron ore EBITDA per ton stay flat despite 58% volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sales price stayed around INR6,000/t and more ore was used internally, so merchant sales volume and per-ton margin in the reported figure did not rise; the margin shifted to value-added products.

qa_highlights.question: Is the pellet margin structural or one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the slurry pipeline saves about INR550/t, export share is expected to stay around 25%, and the margin gains are structural rather than cyclical.

qa_highlights.question: NTPC wage receivable of about INR300 crore: why no provision?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no provision is planned; the arbitration award was won, NTPC has not accepted it, the matter is sub judice, and resolution is hoped for in 2-3 months. Management also said NTPC relations remain sound with a new contract awarded.

qa_highlights.question: Chemaf debt restructuring: will consolidated debt fall by $700-800 million?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said restructuring will complete in the next quarter before creditor deadlines, and debt will fall significantly, by about 40-50%, though some new debt may replace old debt.

qa_highlights.question: Why was INR650 crore raised in Thriveni?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said proceeds are to refinance high-cost debt, fund conversion of conventional equipment to electric equipment and fund overseas subsidiaries for mining; Thriveni's blended interest cost is about 9-9.5% and Q1 interest was about INR115 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What about the DRC copper export ban?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the DRC exports mainly cathode, and both assets will produce final cathodes, so there is no impact on them.

risks_watch: Iron ore pricing and pellet realisation are cyclical; management declined to guide on pricing and margins beyond FY27.
Thriveni margins fell due to higher fuel costs; pass-through agreements with clients are still under negotiation.
NTPC receivable of about INR300 crore is unprovided and under arbitration; outcome and timing uncertain.
Copper JV: $300 million+ capex and financing closure still pending; Chemaf debt restructuring not yet complete; management declined to disclose copper margins or timing of profitability.
Steel plant and Panguna (PNG) copper projects not board-approved; capex beyond FY27 is not finalised.
512455|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and celebratory on the quarter's results and margins, but evasive on forward pricing, copper margins, PNG and the larger steel plant, saying plans are not yet finalised or are too early to quantify.
key_quotes: I'm proud to say our pellets operations reached 100% capacity utilization within just 4 months.
This is a structural re-rating of the earnings base, not a cyclical spike.

We are confident that these margins can sustain in the cyclical commodity because we continue to actively pursue better and higher value markets for every product we make, chasing realization and not just volume.
Our teams are evaluating and making a plan on how we can increase the production capacity in these mines over the next 3 to 5 years.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Standalone EBITDA margin hit 39.2% (+631 bps QoQ) on slurry pipeline savings of INR500-550/t and a richer pellet mix (pellets 41% of standalone revenue), but iron ore realisation is flat at about INR6,000/t and management declined to guide on pricing or margins beyond FY27.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Dalpahar 3 mtpa mine is expected Q2 FY27, Laserda-Pacheri 1.5 mtpa started in Q1, and the 1.2 Mt steel plant is targeted for March 2027, supporting Odisha volumes of 34-35 mt in FY27 (+39% YoY).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Iron ore production up 53% YoY to 6.05 Mt in Q1 and Odisha volumes guided up 39% to 34-35 Mt in FY27, though more ore is going internally, so merchant sales growth is smaller (sales +58% YoY to 5.46 Mt).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Pellet plant 2 is at 100% utilisation within four months, and management guides about INR8,500 crore capex in FY27 plus INR11,000-11,500 crore a year for two years, rising to INR15,000-20,000 crore in year three, though the steel plant and Panguna are not board-approved.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held Thriveni FY27 EBITDA margin at 28-30% rather than raising it, and declined to forecast iron ore pricing, which is flat at about INR6,000/t YoY.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Thriveni Q1 margin fell on fuel costs (pass-through talks ongoing), and the INR300 crore NTPC receivable is unprovided and under arbitration.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Steel plant of 1.2 Mt long products targeted for March 2027, and BHQ beneficiation (30 mtpa, 9 modules, about 16-17 Mt saleable output) by March 2028, but both timelines are not yet finalised for steel.

rows.label: Chemaf debt restructuring cuts consolidated debt 40-50%
rows.why: Consolidated net debt is about INR19,000 crore; restructuring is expected to cut about $700-800 million before creditor deadlines, with financial closure in 3-4 months, though some new debt may replace old.

rows.label: Thriveni EV/LNG fleet shift lifts logistics EBITDA margin from 32% to 40%
rows.why: Plan adds 200 vehicles (50 LNG, 150 EV) and Thriveni's Q1 margin was hit by fuel costs, with pass-through deals still under negotiation.

rows.label: NTPC INR300 crore receivable resolution
rows.why: Arbitration award won but NTPC has not accepted it, the matter is sub judice, and management hopes for resolution in 2-3 months while not provisioning the INR300 crore.

tone.note: Management was confident on the record pellet margins, 100% pellet utilisation and Odisha volume growth, but evasive on iron ore pricing, copper margins, PNG and the steel plant's board approval; analysts pressed on the unprovided NTPC receivable, Chemaf debt restructuring and the INR650 crore Thriv

512529|2026-03.headline: Viyash Q4 FY26 revenue INR920 crore (+19.1% YoY), adjusted EBITDA about INR200 crore at 21.7% margin; FY26 PAT INR225 crore.
512529|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was described by management as the strongest quarter in company history, the first full 12-month results of the combined Viyash-SeQuent entity. Revenue rose 19.1% YoY to INR920 crore, with formulations up 28% to INR499 crore and APIs up 5% to about INR384 crore. Adjusted EBITDA rose about 64% to INR200 crore and PBT swung from a INR37 crore loss to a INR125 crore profit. FY26 revenue was INR3,420 crore (+13.8%), adjusted EBITDA INR702 crore (+59.6%), and PAT INR225 crore versus INR16 crore in FY25. Management also cited a credit rating upgrade to AA- (long-term) and A1+ (short-term).

financial_highlights.value: INR125 crore PBT / INR66 crore PAT
financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR37 crore PBT and loss of INR32 crore PAT in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.value: INR349 crore PBT / INR225 crore PAT
financial_highlights.change: PBT more than 26x; PAT more than 14x vs INR16 crore

segments.name: Animal Health formulations
segments.commentary: All regions growing strongly per management. Animal health business moved from a flat INR350 crore plus or minus INR10 crore over five years to a INR400 crore run rate this year. Companion animal platform build-out is planned for FY27 with a Boehringer Ingelheim distribution partnership.

segments.name: Human health formulations
segments.commentary: Q4 formulations up 28% YoY. Shift toward complex products and internalised APIs; a dedicated potent oncology lab in R&D is being readied this quarter or next. US subsidiary (60% owned) revenue about INR400-425 crore.

segments.name: API and CDMO
segments.commentary: FY26 API revenue up 8% to INR1,491 crore; Q4 API up 5%. Management deliberately cut low-margin intermediates. Life cycle management CDMO business with 8-10 innovators is about INR200-225 crore and is expected to grow about 40% in FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 life cycle management (innovator) CDMO business expected to grow about 40% from a base of about INR200-225 crore.
Management expects comfortable double-digit API growth next year, roughly in line with formulations growth.
Management sees 15% annual growth as possible over the next five years; a detailed strategy and investor meeting are planned, possibly in June.
Revenue target of INR1,000 crore EBITDA stated, with timing to be confirmed at the investor meeting; management earlier cited INR800 crore for FY27 or FY28.
Synergies accrued at about INR50-60 crore annualised, with a target of INR125-150 crore annualised over the next 12-18 months.
Tax rate to be modelled at about 27% for FY27 and FY28, moving to 26-27% after one-off merger-related adjustments roll off.
Goodwill amortisation to fall to about INR35 crore in FY27 from about INR100 crore in FY26; depreciation excluding this to stay similar to FY26.
EBITDA margins expected to be maintained, but FY27 is an investment year with higher R&D and pre-operating costs.
Management is evaluating selective inorganic opportunities and options to buy out minority stakes (Spain option by 2028).
capex_capacity: Manufacturing expansion in Spain and debottlenecking at the Turkey manufacturing site are underway.
Capex approved for R&D expansion; companion animal R&D to expand 5-6x, targeting 7-8 products per year, with R&D hiring starting over the next six months.
Capex for capacity increase in Viyash has been invested and is awaiting approval, which management expects to bring further synergies.
Two high-potent dedicated API facilities; API batch capability ranges from 0.5-1 kg up to 100 kg.
API R&D team of about 250 scientists including analytical and process; human health formulation R&D about 55-60 scientists.
demand_pricing: Animal health: about 70-80% of API volumes go to innovators; generics pricing falls to about 60-70% of innovator price versus 10-15% in human generics.
Companion animal addressable market in Europe about $1 billion (excluding vaccines); India companion animal market a few hundred crore.
Formulation model is partnership-based, with development paid by partners and profit share typically 50:50 (customers cited include Cipla and Dr. Reddy's).

Raw material and freight: impact in March was immaterial; freight added INR1-2 crore in Q4; solvent costs were the main pressure. Price increases are being used to offset, with key materials stocked for 1-2 quarters.
Commodity intermediate margins are about 30-35%; management is exiting these in favour of APIs and formulations.

qa_highlights.question: How large is the CDMO business and how will it scale over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the life cycle management CDMO business is about INR200 crore with 8-10 big innovators, and 90%-plus of relationships are existing. Ramp-up of NCE Phase III CDMO work takes years.

qa_highlights.question: Which subsidiaries drive minority interest, and how big are they?
qa_highlights.answer: Viyash owns 60% of the US formulations business (revenue about INR400-425 crore) and 60% of the Spain business (FY26 revenue about INR550 crore). Minorities account for about 20% of PAT; Spain buy-back option exists by 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Animal health growth priorities and Boehringer Ingelheim partnership?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is on API for patent expiries from 2028 onwards (15-20 products identified, 5-6 large), geography expansion for large animal products, and companion animals with the BI distribution deal and 7-8 new products per year.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin sustainability versus pure-play API peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects gross margins to hold at current levels, plus or minus 1-2%, through forward and backward integration and dropping commodity products. Margin gains beyond that are expected only with CDMO scale-up.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables growth and cash conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables rose mostly with revenue; days increased by only about 5-6 days in Q4. Focus is on converting EBITDA into PAT, with a tax regime shift for some subsidiaries from 34-35% to 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material and geopolitical impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Impact began in March and was not material; key materials are stocked for 1-2 quarters and price increases are being used to offset solvent and freight costs.

qa_highlights.question: Why is API growth single digit and when will it turn double digit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said intermediates were cut deliberately; quality API and animal health APIs are growing double digit, and FY27 should see comfortable double-digit API growth with more approvals.

risks_watch: Investment year in FY27 (R&D, pre-operating costs) may dilute EBITDA margins despite management's margin-maintenance guidance.
Raw material cost volatility (solvents, freight) linked to geopolitical disruption; management says price increases can offset only for now.
Receivables growth outpacing revenue in some geographies (e.g. Turkey) with long credit periods; EBITDA-to-PAT conversion remains a stated focus.
Synergy realisation (INR50-60 crore run-rate versus INR125-150 crore target) depends on approvals taking 12-18 months.
US companion animal generic guidance is complex (BA/BE requirements), delaying the planned US entry.
Minority interest (about 20% of PAT) and the Spain buy-back timeline.
512529|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and integration, with a clear focus on execution. Management was less precise on specific numbers (e.g. revising the INR1,000 crore EBITDA target timing and asking for later confirmation at an investor meeting), and it deferred detailed strategy until a planned June meeting.
key_quotes: Q4 FY '26 is the strongest quarter in the company history. EBITDA surpasses INR200 crores.
We are able to take it to INR400 crores run rate.
Whatever we are doing this year, I can expect next year at least 30%, 40% growing innovator business.
Yes, 15% definitely quite possible. Still, we are working on the detailed strategy.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects gross margin to hold within plus or minus 1-2% of the 55.1% Q4 level, and FY27 is an investment year with higher R&D and pre-operating costs, so EBITDA margin expansion beyond the 21.7% Q4 level is not guided; gains depend on CDMO scale-up.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Spain manufacturing expansion and Turkey debottlenecking are under way, and a Viyash capacity capex is approved and awaiting clearance, but no capacity sizes or dates were given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides comfortable double-digit API growth in FY27 (vs +8% in FY26 and +5% in Q4), with the life-cycle management CDMO business (INR200-225 crore base) expected to grow about 40%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex has been cleared for R&D (companion animal R&D to expand 5-6x) and the Viyash capacity capex is awaiting approval, with a strategy and investor meeting planned for June, so a further capex update is probable.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 adjusted EBITDA rose 59.6% to INR702 crore and Q4 PAT swung to INR66 crore, but management has not raised numbers and is only pointing to a INR1,000 crore EBITDA ambition with timing still to be confirmed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 is an investment year with higher R&D and pre-operating costs, and solvent and freight costs add pressure (freight INR1-2 crore in Q4), though price increases and 1-2 quarters of stocked materials are offsetting for now.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Companion animal platform with Boehringer Ingelheim is planned for FY27 with 7-8 new products per year targeted, and an oncology potent lab in R&D is being readied this quarter or next.

rows.label: US companion animal generic entry
rows.why: US entry is planned but delayed by complex BA/BE requirements, with no timeline given.

rows.label: Spain minority buy-out option by 2028
rows.why: Minorities hold about 20% of PAT and the Spain (60% owned, FY26 revenue about INR550 crore) buy-back option exists by 2028; management is evaluating selective inorganic options.

rows.label: Synergy ramp to INR125-150 crore annualised
rows.why: Synergies are accruing at INR50-60 crore annualised today, and the target is INR125-150 crore, dependent on approvals taking 12-18 months.

tone.note: Management was confident on integration, Q4 record quarter and FY27 API and CDMO growth, but cautious on the margin investment year, raw material pressure, and vague on the INR1,000 crore EBITDA target timing; analysts' questions focused on API growth being single digit, receivables and EBITDA-to-PA

512529|2026-06.headline: Viyash Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to Rs 946 crore, EBITDA margin expanded to 21.6% (up ~530 bps) and PAT more than doubled to Rs 79 crore.
512529|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations reached Rs 946 crore (up 19.5% YoY, 2.9% QoQ), with EBITDA of Rs 205 crore and margin of 21.6% versus 16.2% a year earlier. PAT of Rs 79 crore is after about Rs 19 crore of incremental ESOP cost tied to the post-amalgamation grant. Net debt fell to Rs 86 crore (0.1x EBITDA), and management said the Sequent-Viyash integration is complete. Human API revenue was flat QoQ due to customer deferrals during raw material price volatility, which management expects to reverse in Q2.

financial_highlights.change: vs 51.9% in Q1 FY26 (~+220 bps YoY)
vs 16.2% in Q1 FY26 (~+530 bps YoY)
vs Rs 20.4 crore in Q1 FY26
Net debt/EBITDA 0.1x vs 0.24x last quarter, ~1x a year ago

financial_highlights.value: Rs 25 crore total, of which Rs 19 crore incremental
financial_highlights.change: Grant of 1.3 crore options, 2.8% of post-amalgamation paid-up capital

segments.name: US (Human formulation)
segments.commentary: Grew about 60% per management (about 45% YoY and 6% QoQ in USD per analyst); Rs 126 crore of Q1 revenue is Human formulation. Management said 60% growth will not repeat, but growth is stable, with a 50-55% US market share.

segments.name: Europe (Animal Health)
segments.commentary: Reported roughly 13% growth; analyst computed EUR 16.8 million flat YoY in constant currency. Management guided full-year Europe growth of 18-20% INR, citing phasing across quarters.

segments.name: Emerging markets (Animal Health)
segments.commentary: Grew 36% (about 23% in USD per analyst); volume growth was 25%, led by Turkey, Brazil and Mexico. Management said 25% volume growth will not be sustained every quarter.

segments.name: Animal Health India domestic
segments.commentary: Grew about 60%; management plans to expand field force and portfolio.

segments.name: API (Human and Animal)
segments.commentary: Broadly flat QoQ due to customer deferrals during raw material volatility. Animal API run-rate about Rs 100 crore, with Vizag capacity commercialised from July. API is about 40-45% of total revenue, roughly two-thirds Human and one-third Animal.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q2 to be the best quarter in company history for API, citing a rebound in orders after customers delayed purchases in June.
FY27 double-digit growth, with management citing 13-15% overall (Human API 13-14%, Animal Health 20%+).
Europe growth of 18-20% INR for the full year; Europe double-digit growth in FY27 excluding FX.
ESOP cost of about Rs 150 crore for FY27 (Rs 25 crore in Q1, about Rs 40 crore per quarter thereafter), falling to Rs 25-30 crore in FY28.
Depreciation plus goodwill amortisation of Rs 25 crore per quarter; drops to about Rs 10-11 crore in Q2, and management expects about Rs 15 crore benefit per quarter from Q3 onward.
Minority interest expected at about 16-17% of total profit; minority stakes in the US and Spain to be fully acquired within 1-2 years.
Capex of Rs 250-300 crore per year; companion animal tablet capacity targeted to be ready by January-February 2027.
Bio For Life (Italy) acquisition SPA signed; closing expected in the next few months and within FY27. Bigger revenue expected after 18-24 months.

Human high-potent oncology first product expected in 2029; majority of new product revenue after 2030. Management targets Rs 1 billion (~Rs 10,000 crore?) aspiration by 2032 implying 18% CAGR from FY27 base.
capex_capacity: Companion animal tablet manufacturing: design finalised, construction to start within weeks, target completion January-February 2027 for exhibit batches.
High-potent formulation development lab completed last week; three high-potent API modules built over last 18-24 months.
Albendazole capacity expanded; US approval received for Vizag site, commercialisation started from July 2026.
R&D ramped up for companion animal products; equipment ordered and people hired.
Annual capex of Rs 250-300 crore, described as modest relative to existing business.
demand_pricing: Human API demand deferred in June as customers waited for raw material/solvent prices to stabilise; management says orders are returning after July.
Management noted it raised prices when raw material costs rose and may reduce them if solvent prices fall.
Human high-potent and oncology products expected to face 50-60% price erosion at generic entry versus 95% for general APIs, per management.
Target market share for new products: 10-15% on average, with 25-30% in best cases.
Europe: Spain performing strongly; Benelux and other countries lagging in tenders. Europe volume and pricing are the main growth drivers.
Animal Health portfolio focus shifted to differentiated products; the company has stopped developing mature commodity products.

qa_highlights.question: Naman Bagrecha (IIFL): Europe revenue looks flat YoY on a constant-currency basis; what is driving this and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Europe grew about 13% and computed EUR 16.8 million versus EUR 16.8 million in Q1 FY26 was disputed in the exchange; Rajaram Narayanan said full-year Europe growth should be close to 18-20% in INR, with Q1 phasing tied to tenders and contract timing, and Q3 typically the peak quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Emerging markets grew about 23% in USD; what drove it and will it continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth led by Turkey, Brazil and Mexico with volume up 25%; management said volume growth will not run at 25% every quarter.

qa_highlights.question: US business grew about 45% YoY and 6% QoQ in USD; what drove it and is the margin improvement sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited restructuring: moving volume products to India, vertical integration of some products with in-house API, new launches and higher R&D revenue; 60% growth will not repeat but growth is stable with 50-55% market share; management expects the margin improvement to continue.

qa_highlights.question: Why was API flat QoQ, and what is the Animal API revenue run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers delayed June purchases while waiting for raw material and solvent prices to settle after the war; management said orders returned after July and Q2 would be the best API quarter in company history. Animal API run-rate is about Rs 100 crore, with Vizag Albendazole capacity commercialised from July.

qa_highlights.question: Sahil Sanghvi (Monarch Networth): Can API growth exceed 20% for several quarters, and what is the full-year outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided Animal Health above 20% and overall FY27 growth of 13-15%, with Human API 13-14%; big Human launches are expected later, from FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ESOP cost trajectory and what are the Q2-Q4 expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 ESOP cost was about Rs 25 crore including Rs 19 crore incremental; about Rs 40 crore per quarter for Q2-Q4, about Rs 150 crore for FY27, falling to Rs 25-30 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Bharat Sheth (Quest): How big is the high-potent oncology business and what is the pipeline and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capability was built over 18-24 months with three API modules and a high-potent formulation lab completed last week; first formulation product expected in 2029, majority of revenue after 2030; at least 5-6 APIs filed and at least 50% of portfolio is first-to-file or first-to-launch.

qa_highlights.question: Depreciation and goodwill amortisation and interest cost trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation plus goodwill amortisation was Rs 25 crore in Q1; about Rs 10-11 crore in Q2, with about Rs 15 crore per quarter benefit from Q3. Management is restructuring interest, including Ireland debt, after the Sequent India debt restructuring last year.

qa_highlights.question: Chintan Sheth (Greek Capital): What is the minority interest outlook and the Human vs Animal split?
qa_highlights.answer: Minority interest was about 17% in Q1 and about 20% for FY26; management guided 16-17% of total profit going forward. Minority stakes in the US and Spain to be bought out within 1-2 years. 513023|2026-06.headline: Nava Q1 FY27 consolidated total income hit an all-time quarterly high of INR1,269 crore; Phase 2 thermal (MEL) slips to Q2 FY28-29 commissioning.

513097|2026-03.headline: FY26 consolidated revenue rose 12.3% to ₹570.9 crore and EBITDA margin expanded ~250 bps to 22.9%, with a PAT of ₹95.8 crore (+24.8%).
513097|2026-03.overview: Management framed FY26 as a shift toward value-added components, assemblies and OEM/Tier-1 engagement, with consolidated EBITDA up 26.0% to ₹130.7 crore. Standalone revenue grew on broadly flat volumes, which management attributed to better realisation (shunt component mix moving from ~55% to ~65%, ~10-12% realisation uplift). Contacts (silver-based) grew sharply, but management said only about 30-31% of the ~54-60% growth was underlying volume, with the rest from silver price pass-through. Management guided to a multi-year re-acceleration led by a US shunt customer's component recovery and a new Pune PCBA/busbar facility targeting ₹250-350 crore revenue over 2-3 years.

segments.commentary: Revenue up ~54-60% in FY26, of which management said ~30-31% is underlying growth and ~21-22% is silver price pass-through. Now a 100% subsidiary (formerly JV until 2023); new plant partially ready for 7-8 months.

segments.commentary: India demand flat as domestic consumption has not grown; Europe showed strong traction. Market share in India reportedly ~90%; management is pursuing high-volume export orders, potentially at 1-2% margin sacrifice.

513097|2026-06.headline: Shivalik Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 33.4% YoY to ₹182.2 crore and PAT rose 44.9% to ₹33 crore, with FY27 revenue growth guided at 20-30%.

513228|2026-03.headline: Pennar Q4 FY26 PAT rose 14.91% to INR41.04 crores on total income of INR933.7 crores; management commits to 20% PAT growth in FY27.
513228|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income rose 2.26% to INR933.7 crores while EBITDA grew 15.27% to INR114 crores and PAT grew 14.91% to INR41.04 crores, with PAT margin at 4.44% versus 3.9%. FY26 was a record year: total income INR3,666 crores (up 12.33%), PAT INR138.83 crores (up 16.22%), PAT margin 3.83% versus 3.7%. Management attributed the Q4 revenue slowdown to revenue slipping into Q1 and a solar hit in diversified engineering, and blamed labour shortages for PEB India underperformance in FY26. Working capital rose to 82 days, and gross debt-to-equity rose to 0.98x, both of which management is targeting to reduce.

segments.commentary: Order backlog about INR34 crores, up from INR22 crores at the prior update; US tariff impact has moderated and orders are returning. European markets being explored.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said labour is resolved and not expected to recur in the medium term, and that the Q4 shortfall was revenue slipping into Q1, not labour supply.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost increases have been passed on to customers, the company has modelled them, and it sees no impact on revenue or margin plans beyond energy price risk.

qa_highlights.answer: Legacy businesses are 30% to 35% of revenue; management said prioritised business units are growing faster, and the overall growth rate divided by 0.7 gives their rate.

513228|2026-06.headline: Pennar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 3.6% to INR884.55 crore while PBT grew 16% to INR46.8 crore, with PBT margin at 5.38%.

Management attributed margin gains to mix shift toward PEB US and engineering services, though PEB India margins dropped for a month or two due to delayed steel pass-through. Order books are at record levels in PEB India (INR1,008 crore), PEB US (above USD100 million) and boilers (INR150.75 crore), while Hydraulics orders softened on US tariff uncertainty. Management guided to double-digit sequential revenue and profit growth in Q2 and reiterated a 7% PBT margin target over about three years. Questions on segment EBITDA, employee cost growth, other income and the promoter warrant issue drew deferred or defensive answers.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 7% PBT margin over about three years is the guide, and that PAT margin of about 10% is the practical ceiling given 15-20% operating margins and the roughly half-to-PAT conversion. Competitors are at 7-8%, and it called this a Mount Everest target rather than a hard limit.

513262|2026-03.headline: Steel Strips Wheels Q4 FY26 revenue up about 20% YoY to INR 1,475 crore; management guides FY27 EBITDA per wheel near INR 300 and EBITDA INR 650 crore.

rows.why: Bhuj aluminium wheel plant (1.2 mn wheels p.a., INR420 crore) is under construction with commercial start early April 2027, Bhuj knuckles (1.1 mn units) target Q4 FY27, and Dappar tractor wheel addition (0.5 mn sets, INR120 crore) is under construction; aluminium capacity goes beyond 6.2 mn.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 revenue +44% YoY to INR3,440 crore, tractor volume up about 15% in H1 with share at 45% from 43%, domestic steel wheel demand up 28% in H1, and management expects record October CV sales; aluminium capacity is near full so growth beyond debottlenecking (10% uplift to 5.4 mn) depends on new plants.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Board approved INR1,400 crore Sambhajinagar greenfield over 60 months on top of over INR600 crore FY27 capex, with aluminium wheel capacity near full utilisation and management saying shortage of capacity exists in the market.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 already exceeded FY27 guidance of revenue growth above 20% and EBITDA per wheel above INR310 (H1 INR362), management is 'extremely confident' of strong H2, and FY27 export target could rise from INR600 crore to INR700-750 crore on a US trade deal.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Risks include volume taper from high CV and tractor base affecting EBITDA per wheel, the INR183 crore H1 supplementary invoicing that may not repeat, execution on Bhuj and Sambhajinagar timelines, and freight/Hormuz cost headwinds, with debt funding of INR1,400 crore flagged as high.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Bhuj aluminium knuckles commercial production targeted Q4 FY27 (1.1 mn units p.a.) and hot stamping line commissioning targeted Q1 calendar 2027 (1.3 mn strokes p.a., about INR400 crore turnover) with anchor customer in Maharashtra.

rows.label: Export ramp via European OEM steel wheel approvals
rows.when: from Q4 FY27; INR1,500 crore in 3 years
rows.why: Management sees INR1,500 crore exports in 3 years (possibly INR2,000 crore) driven by approvals with MAN, Scania, Daimler, with export revenue already +69% YoY in Q2 to INR187 crore, though qualification cycles run about 9 months to 12 years depending on certification.

rows.label: Sambhajinagar hot stamping anchor order
rows.why: Hot stamping line (1.3 mn strokes p.a., about INR400 crore turnover, around INR170 crore investment) has an anchor customer in Maharashtra and management says the plant will start sold out.

rows.label: Debt funding of INR1,400 crore Sambhajinagar project
rows.why: Funded by debt, internal accruals and likely strategic partners (unnamed), and analysts flagged already high debt, so leverage could rise before the plant contributes.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, the INR404 per-wheel sustainability and the Sambhajinagar plant, but defensive on the INR140 crore supplementary invoicing and declined to give project IRR; analysts pressed on EBITDA quality, high debt and 12-13% incremental ROCE.

513349|2026-03.headline: Ajmera Realty FY26 presales hit record INR 1,701 Cr (+57% YoY), beating INR 1,600 Cr guidance; FY27 presales target set at INR 2,200 Cr.
513349|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year for Ajmera Realty: presales of INR 1,701 Cr (+57% YoY), collections of INR 1,103 Cr (+71%), and total sales revenue of INR 1,098 Cr (+46%). EBITDA rose 25% to INR 306 Cr and PAT rose 24% to INR 157 Cr. Debt-to-equity fell to 0.53x against an annual guidance of 0.85x. Management guided FY27 presales to about INR 2,200 Cr and debt-to-equity to 1.00x, citing the Kanjurmarg land conversion, a planned INR 1,800 Cr of business development, and eight launches. Most Q&A focused on the Kanjurmarg conversion timeline, Versova luxury sales pace, Manhattan pricing, and the reason for the higher gearing guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for Wadala boutique offices and Manhattan 3, and Borivali?

513349|2026-06.headline: Ajmera Realty Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23% YoY to INR320 crores, PAT up 14% to INR45 crores, debt cut to INR680 crores.
513349|2026-06.overview: Revenue for Q1 FY27 was about INR320 crores, up 23% YoY from INR265 crores, with EBITDA of INR94 crores (about 29% margin) and PAT of INR45 crores (14% margin). Ajmera Solis entered revenue recognition for the first time this quarter. Debt fell by INR57 crores to INR680 crores, taking debt-equity to 0.47x. Sales value was INR146 crores against collections of about INR173 crores, and INR89 crores was received from a property asset monetisation against a INR330 crores target.

segments.name: Residential (Mumbai)

segments.commentary: 19% of inventory sold; piling and shoring in progress; management aims to speed up execution.

segments.name: Wadala (Manhattan 2 and others)
segments.commentary: Over 50% of inventory sold, excavation in progress; boutique office Phase 1 part of ~INR18,000 crore Wadala GDV.

guidance_outlook: Revenue visibility of INR3,846 crores (INR1,661 crores committed sales plus INR2,185 crores unsold inventory), rising to INR10,000-plus crores with the upcoming launch pipeline of about INR6,500 crores.

FY27 launch pipeline of about INR3,000 crores (call mentions INR6,500 crores for launches in another part of the call); Wadala boutique office launch in a single phase of about INR3,600 crores, targeted for Q3.
Estimated cash flow potential, pre-tax and post-debt, from ongoing projects, upcoming projects and other revenue of about INR3,380 crores over project life cycles.
Remaining INR241 crores of the INR330 crores asset monetisation target; a further stake sale in a JV was signed in early July 2026 and will be reported in Q2.

Debt-equity target of 1x by FY27-end was reiterated, but management said Q1 and Q2 may see higher working-capital borrowing before deleveraging resumes. Finance cost is expected to normalise to about INR20 crores from next quarter.

Ajmera One (Versova) demand is for larger apartments; management expects subdued sales this year until superstructure progresses.
Mid and luxury segments are seeing an uptick per management, though overall sales were subdued due to fewer large launches this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Kanjurmarg land conversion and tie-up for the 7-acre plot?
qa_highlights.answer: Conversion targeted in 2-3 months, before the December deadline; tie-up talks are active but will only conclude after conversion. Deal is a single transaction, with a mix of outright and JV bids.

qa_highlights.question: Confidence in the INR3,600 crore single-phase Wadala boutique office launch and why it was scaled up?
qa_highlights.answer: Approval changes added ~1 million sq ft FSI and ~INR3,000 crores GDV. Office launch scaled from 4-5 lakh sq ft to 8-8.5 lakh sq ft, supported by GCC and connectivity-driven demand.

qa_highlights.question: Why have Pune and Borivali launch timelines moved?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly regulatory reasons; management is choosing to launch at plinth level for better demand and pricing, not at excavation stage.

qa_highlights.question: Why are sales weak at Ajmera One (Versova)?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand for larger units appears only after RCC level; the project is at excavation, so management will not push desperate sales and expects a year before traction.

qa_highlights.question: Why did consolidated finance cost rise from ~INR21 crores to ~INR30 crores QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Solis entered revenue recognition, so accumulated interest on its high-cost PE-funded debt was charged to P&L. Cost is expected to normalise to about INR20 crores from next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Was there any P&L impact from the INR89 crores monetisation, and why was SV Concrete dropped?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR89 crores is a balance-sheet financial asset realisation with no P&L impact. SV Concrete was swapped for Whitefield (INR389 crores GDV, Q4 FY27 target).

513349|2026-09.headline: Ajmera Realty Q2 FY27 revenue rose 45% YoY to INR320 crore and PAT 55% to INR49 crore; debt cut to INR646 crore.
513349|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 sales were INR224 crore (72,883 sq ft carpet) against collections of INR190 crore, and H1 sales reached INR370 crore. Revenue, EBITDA and PAT all grew strongly YoY, with 33Fifteen (Bandra commercial) recognising revenue for the first time this quarter. Debt fell INR34 crore QoQ to INR646 crore, debt-equity is 0.44x and weighted cost of debt dipped to 10.75%. Management's near-term story rests on about 8 launches (~38 lakh sq ft, ~INR7,000 crore top line) mostly in Q4 FY27, plus the Kanjurmarg 7-acre land conversion, which has slipped repeatedly and drew the most investor pushback.

financial_highlights.value: INR370 crore sales (1,16,620 sq ft) / INR363 crore collections
INR3,510 crore (INR1,550 crore committed sales + INR1,960 crore inventory to sell)
INR7,008 crore; total visibility above INR10,500 crore

segments.commentary: 25% of inventory sold in the quarter, with excavation ongoing. Revenue recognition began this quarter on fast-track execution.

guidance_outlook: About 8 launches in H2 FY27 (~38 lakh sq ft, ~INR7,000 crore top line): Solis early Dec or mid-Dec; Bangalore projects mid-Jan to Feb; Boutique office (Wadala) by mid-to-end Feb; Borivali and Whitefield by March; Vishrantwadi (Pune) first sales and TDR revenue by end March; Doddabalapur by Feb.
Management is confident of exceeding the INR2,200 crore presales target over the next six months, against INR370 crore in H1.
Wadala commercial (captive, annuity) to be built in two phases of about 10 lakh sq ft each; Phase 2 expected in FY28.
Management expects leverage headroom to roughly double from 0.44x to fund launches within the guided leverage range; financial closure reportedly in place for Wadala.
Estimated pre-tax cash flow post debt from ongoing and upcoming projects is about INR3,900 crore-plus over project life cycles.

Kanjurmarg 7-acre conversion: management hopes for conversion in this or the next quarter, possibly two quarters, but it is not guaranteed before 31 December. Conversion cost was earlier estimated at INR300-330 crore, and management declined to update the figure.
capex_capacity: Launch pipeline is about 8 projects, 38 lakh sq ft in total, spread across 8 micro-markets and multiple cities, so management sees limited internal cannibalisation.

Kanjurmarg 7-acre plot: the strategic partner route (monetisation, JV or funding) is still open; conversion is the gating item and the 55-acre master plan is largely frozen but not yet tied up.
demand_pricing: Management says Mumbai residential registrations are resilient and that premium homes above INR1 crore are a growing share of sales.
Commercial leasing is strong, led by GCC tenants, with Grade A office demand described as good.
RBI raised the repo rate by 25 bps in its October policy. Management sees limited impact unless rates rise further.

Vann (Versova) pricing: competing stock is available at INR38,000, INR45,000 and INR50,000 per sq ft. Management is holding prices and expects sales to pick up when plinth and upper floors are visible.

qa_highlights.question: Kanjurmarg 7-acre tie-up and conversion timing; will conversion happen before 31 Dec before cost rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says conversion is hoped for before 31 Dec but hurdles remain; it is a government process and it declined to quantify the cost if it slips. Commercial talks have not started, though title and approvals have progressed.

qa_highlights.question: Will presales of INR2,200 crore be met given the Q4 launch cluster?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident of exceeding the target within six months, citing 8 launches and early agent interest. It acknowledged up to one or two launches could slip because approvals are not fully in place.

qa_highlights.question: Balance sheet capacity to fund Wadala commercial plus launches within 6 to 9 months.
qa_highlights.answer: CFO says leverage is 0.44x with room to roughly double, financial closure is in place for Wadala, and Solis collections will accelerate cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Margin sustainability with cost inflation and pricing pressure.
qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects geopolitics and commodity pressure to normalise and will time launches and sales velocity against cost and pricing elasticity. No margin number was given.

qa_highlights.question: Kanjurmarg timeline visibility and what follows conversion.
qa_highlights.answer: Management could not commit to a timeline. After conversion it expects a 4-5 month routine master plan and approvals step, then a commercial and residential launch together and a 7-acre monetisation or JV.

qa_highlights.question: Vann sales slow and Kanjurmarg-style questions on water scarcity and BMC restrictions.
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed micro-market competition and redevelopment supply for Vann's slow sales. It said water shortages in Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28 will be managed through tankers and borewells, and there are no BMC restrictions yet.

risks_watch: Kanjurmarg 7-acre conversion depends on government and court processes; the timeline has moved from June to December to 'next quarter or two', and the conversion cost may rise after 31 Dec.

Rate hike and affordability; cost inflation and margin pressure from labour and materials; Q4 and Q1 water shortage affecting construction pace.

513375|2026-03.headline: Carborundum Universal FY26 standalone sales rose 8.6% to INR 3,024 crore, while consolidated PBIT fell 25.3% to INR 404 crore on subsidiary losses.
513375|2026-03.overview: Standalone performance rebounded through H2 FY26, with Q4 sales up 23.1% YoY to INR 845 crore and Q4 PAT more than doubling to INR 122 crore. Consolidated sales crossed INR 5,000 crore (INR 5,149 crore, +6.5%), but consolidated PBT before exceptions fell 27.2% to INR 416 crore, driven by VAW sanctions, Foskor, Awuko and Rhodius losses. Management decided to wind down Awuko and to close Foskor Zirconia, booking exceptional items of INR 135 crore in FY26. FY27 guidance is for about 4-4.5% consolidated sales growth, which falls to 11-12% excluding Foskor and Awuko, with capex of about INR 400 crore.

segments.name: Standalone Abrasives
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 1,270 crore (+6.2%); H1 down 2.8% to INR 594 crore, H2 up 15.6% YoY to INR 675 crore. PBIT INR 195 crore (+0.9%), margin 15.3% vs 16.1%.

segments.name: Standalone Electrominerals
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 906 crore (+11.1%), with exports up 100% to over 33% of sales. PBIT rose 31.1% to INR 82 crore; management said growth was mainly volume with price roughly flat.

segments.name: Standalone Ceramics
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 1,000 crore (+6.5%). PBIT fell 8% to INR 214 crore. Wear ceramics de-grew 9%; engineering ceramics grew 30% on SOFC demand; metallized cylinders grew 9% after a H1 production issue.

segments.name: Consolidated Abrasives
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 2,271 crore (+5.1%); Q4 INR 610 crore (+13.4% YoY). PBIT margin 4.3% vs 7.0%, with Rhodius loss about INR 45 crore and Awuko loss about INR 75 crore.

segments.name: Consolidated Electrominerals
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 1,632 crore (+3.7%), held back by VAW Russia sales down 35% in roubles. Foskor losses hit PBIT; consolidated segment PBIT INR 91 crore vs INR 177 crore.

segments.name: Consolidated Ceramics
segments.commentary: FY26 sales INR 1,268 crore (+9.3%); reported margin 20.2%. Industrial ceramics INR 569 crore (+7.8%); refractories and anti-corrosives INR 437 crore (+4.7%).

segments.name: Rhodius (Germany)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales EUR 61 million, down 8.8% from EUR 67 million, after about EUR 5 million lost to a Q1 logistics transition. PAT loss EUR 2.6 million vs EUR 0.2 million in FY25.

segments.name: Awuko
segments.commentary: Sales EUR 10.5 million (+4.6%); loss before tax rose to EUR 7.7 million. Voluntary winding-up started in Germany.

segments.name: VAW Russia
segments.commentary: Sales about 6 billion roubles vs 9.4 billion (-35.3%) under US sanctions; profit before tax 617 million roubles vs 1.7 billion, but still profitable.

segments.name: Foskor Zirconia (South Africa)
segments.commentary: Sales ZAR 461 million (+11.2%); loss before tax ZAR 77 million vs ZAR 37 million. Operations being discontinued as not commercially viable.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated sales growth of about 4-4.5%; about 11-12% excluding Foskor Zirconia and Awuko (together INR 343 crore of FY26 sales).
FY27 standalone Abrasives growth about 12% per management; consolidated Abrasives sales +5.5-6% (11-12% excluding Awuko).
FY27 consolidated Ceramics growth of 15-15.5%; consolidated Electrominerals sales -6.5% to -7% due to Foskor closure (8-9% excluding Foskor).
Margin guidance FY27: Abrasives 9.5-10% (FY26 comparable 7.9%), Ceramics 20.5-21% (reported 20.2%), Electrominerals 9-9.5% (comparable FY26 9.1%).
FY27 capex of about INR 400 crore, mainly advanced ceramics for power electronics, brown-fused alumina expansion, a 110 kV substation and a tunnel kiln for refractories.
Rhodius expected to grow sales about 5% in FY27 with a very small loss; Aspiration 2030 targets were not formally quantified.
capex_capacity: Consolidated capex FY26 INR 309 crore (standalone INR 235 crore) against INR 350 crore guided earlier.
Semiconductor wafer fab equipment components facility: first module commissioned in H1 FY26 at INR 66 crore; serial supplies start FY27, material revenue expected from 2029.
Aerospace and defence ceramics facility at INR 49 crore; STANAG 4 vehicle armour qualification secured; SCOMET approval awaited.
White fused alumina furnace upgrade from 2 MVA to 4.5 MVA at about INR 53 crore, adding up to INR 95 crore revenue potential; treatment facility INR 30 crore for up to INR 120 crore revenue.
Thin wheel capacity at Hosur using DRONCO-acquired assets: INR 83 crore outlay, 46 million wheels, peak revenue about INR 120 crore.
Refractories fired capacity to rise 75%; metallized cylinder capacity to be expanded in three phases over 18-24 months.
demand_pricing: Standalone H2 FY26 growth was broad-based, with Abrasives, Ceramics and Electrominerals each up double digits sequentially. Management attributed part of the rebound to GST rationalisation and festive demand.
China cut its abrasive export rebate from 9% to 0% from April 2026 (one analyst cited 13%). Management called it good for domestic industry but too recent to show in numbers.
Electrominerals growth was mainly volume; price roughly flat. Chinese import intensity has not declined.

Ceramics growth of 9.3% missed the 13-14% guided earlier, mainly due to deferred projects, especially in the glass segment. Management attributes the 15% FY27 outlook to backlog and customer forecasts.
Over 80% of Ceramics sales are exports; under 10% of Abrasives sales are exports.

qa_highlights.question: How large can the SOFC ceramics business become, and what is the wallet share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give wallet share but said it is an important supplier, with customer visibility to about 2028, and it expects a meaningful share of revenue as the engineered segment grows.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Ceramics growth miss the 13-14% guidance, and does it signal structural competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed mainly deferred projects, not structural change, and expects the 15% FY27 growth to be backed by backlog and customer forecasts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for semiconductor fab-equipment ceramics revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Material qualification takes four to six years; samples are tested and serial production starts, with material revenue expected from 2029 onwards.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to profitability at Rhodius?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects sales growth of 6-7% with the one-time EUR 5 million logistics loss not recurring, plus a special profitability programme, to return it to a small loss or breakeven in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Are there alternatives to Russian silicon carbide supply from VAW?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said replacing the capacity would be costly and difficult; it awaits sanctions relief and has no alternative for now.

risks_watch: Foskor Zirconia closure needs approvals in South Africa; the Awuko winding-up is ongoing in Germany.
VAW Russia sales are constrained by US sanctions, with no alternative supply route identified.
FY27 consolidated growth of 4-4.5% is low versus the 11-12% comparable figure, so the reported drop from exits needs watching.
Ceramics growth depends on the timing of deferred projects and on the US business, where exports fell 40% in FY26 for wear ceramics.
Rhodius returning to breakeven depends on recovering the lost EUR 5 million in sales and on cost actions.
