513375|2026-06.headline: Carborundum Universal Q1 FY27 standalone sales rose 21.2% YoY to INR 846 crores; consolidated PAT up 23.4% to INR 76 crores, with Electrominerals up 33%.
513375|2026-06.overview: Standalone sales grew 21.2% YoY to INR 846 crores, broad-based across Electrominerals (+33%), Ceramics (+15.2%) and Abrasives (+14.7%), and were flat QoQ. Standalone PAT was INR 88 crores, up 14.3% on a like-to-like basis excluding a one-time INR 68 crore subsidiary dividend in Q1 FY26. Consolidated PAT of INR 76 crores was helped by a INR 25 crore gain on leasehold transfer at Sterling Abrasives, while Abrasives standalone margins were squeezed by an oil-linked and fuel cost push of about INR 16 crores. Management raised the consolidated Ceramics growth guidance to 23-25% and kept other segment guidance unchanged, while Foskor divestment and Awuko closure updates are now promised for Q2.

segments.name: Electrominerals (standalone)
segments.commentary: Sales INR 282 crores, +33% YoY and +12.2% QoQ, mainly volume and export-led with very little price increase; PBIT rose to INR 39 crores from INR 7 crores. Exports rose to about 40% of segment sales from about 35% last year.

segments.name: Ceramics (standalone)
segments.commentary: Sales INR 274 crores, +15.2% YoY but -1.6% QoQ on refractories seasonality; PBIT INR 59 crores vs INR 62 crores YoY as IC gains were offset by fuel, alumina and unabsorbed costs in new semicon and aerospace/defence lines.

segments.name: Abrasives (standalone)
segments.commentary: Sales INR 328 crores, +14.7% YoY, volume-driven; PBIT INR 34 crores with margin falling to 10.4% from 13.1% YoY, due to about INR 16 crores cost push (resins, oil, fuel) and INR 8-9 crores volume drop QoQ.

segments.name: Rhodius (Germany, Abrasives)
segments.commentary: Sales EUR 15.6 million, +18% YoY and +1.1% QoQ (INR 172 crores, +33.9% YoY); loss after tax EUR 0.7 million vs EUR 1.6 million a year ago. FY27 guidance of about 5% growth and a small PAT loss is maintained.

segments.name: CUMI Awuko Abrasives (Germany, being wound up)
segments.commentary: Sales EUR 2.89 million, +11.1% YoY; loss after tax EUR 1.69 million vs EUR 0.9 million a year ago. Voluntary winding up is in progress and management aims to complete it in about a quarter.

segments.name: VAW Russia (Electrominerals)
segments.commentary: Sales RUB 1.58 billion, -14.1% YoY in roubles but INR 201 crores, +3.1% YoY in rupee terms; PAT RUB 52.1 million vs RUB 71.5 million a year ago. Business is domestic-focused.

segments.name: Foskor Zirconia (51% subsidiary, Electrominerals)
segments.commentary: Sales ZAR 107 million, -14.7% QoQ; deemed commercially unviable. Q1 consolidated PBIT absorbed a INR 17 crore loss; divestment or exit options are being explored, targeted for Q2.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated sales growth: FY27 guidance of about 4-4.5% reported, or 11-12% excluding Foskor and Awuko; management says it could reach about 15% on a comparable basis given the order book.
Consolidated Abrasives sales growth: guidance of 5.5-6% retained; 11-12% excluding Awuko (about INR 108 crores).
Consolidated Ceramics sales growth: raised to 23-25% from 15-15.5%; management expects the Ceramics margin to be at the higher end of the guidance.
Consolidated Electrominerals sales: guidance of a 6.5-7% decline retained (reported basis); 8-9% growth excluding Foskor, and management says this could be 9-10%.

Margins: Abrasives 9.5-10% and Electrominerals 9-9.5% retained, with Ceramics 20.5-21% maintained. Q1 consolidated Abrasives margin was about 2.5% excluding the Sterling gain, which management attributes to Awuko losses.
Capex of about INR 400 crores for FY27 retained. Rhodius guidance of about 5% growth with a small PAT loss is unchanged.
capex_capacity: Consolidated capex was INR 53 crores in Q1 FY27 against INR 64 crores a year earlier; the FY27 target of about INR 400 crores is unchanged, and management would not give project-wise splits.

FY27 capex covers expansion in advanced ceramics for power electronics (including substrates), metallized tubes, rings and brazed assemblies, brown-fused alumina expansion, an integrated furnace for thermal spray powders and a zirconia furnace.
Metallized substrate facility is being set up with one anchor customer and a technology tie-up; it should be commissioned in FY27, with revenue from FY28.

Semiconductor wafer fab equipment components: small in FY27, picking up in FY28, with a peak targeted for FY30. Aerospace and defence will improve in FY27 with the main ramp from FY28. Powder purity is moving from 5N to 6N.
Refractories capacity expansion is on track, per management.
demand_pricing: Standalone Abrasives growth was volume-driven with very small price increases; management sees early easing of Chinese import competition but says exchange rates and China's export-rebate changes make the trend unclear.
Ceramics: growth was seen across segments; Wear Ceramics returned to growth this quarter after several quarters, and Metallized Cylinders and Engineered Ceramics are growing mainly through exports.

Electrominerals: volume-led, with treated-product mix helping margins; little or no price increase. Export share is rising toward 40%, helped by European duties on Chinese imports, with US and Asia efforts under way.

Abrasives cost push: oil-linked inputs such as resins rose sharply in May and June, with oil reaching about $117 a barrel. Grains (80-85% of COGS) rose only 3-5%. The US-Iran conflict that began end-February 2026 drove the cost pressure.
Management said it will not pass on further price increases until the cost environment is clearer, and will decide one quarter at a time.

qa_highlights.question: Ravi (Avendus): How much of standalone Abrasives growth is value vs volume, traction by sub-segment, and are Chinese import changes helping share gains?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth was predominantly volume-driven with very small price increases. Import competition from China has just started to ease, but management said exchange rates and China's export-benefit withdrawal make the trend unclear; it sees the trend as positive.

qa_highlights.question: Ravi: Where is Ceramics traction strongest across Wear, Technical, Metallized Cylinders and Engineered Ceramics, and is Metallized Cylinder/Engineered Ceramics growth domestic or export?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth optimism is across all segments except Wear, which is normal growth; Wear returned to growth this quarter after several quarters. Metallized Cylinder and Engineered Ceramics growth is predominantly export.

qa_highlights.question: Harshit (Equirus): How will semiconductor wafer fab, aerospace/defence and substrate revenues phase across FY27 and FY28, and does the Ceramics guidance upgrade come mainly from SOFC?
qa_highlights.answer: Substrate facility to be set up in FY27 with revenue from FY28; wafer fab components very small in FY27, picking up in FY28 and peaking in FY30; aerospace/defence slightly better in FY27 with main ramp from FY28. The upgrade is a combination of Engineered Ceramics, Metallized Cylinders and SOFC Ceramics, with no split given.

qa_highlights.question: Harshit: What are plans for zirconia products and Foskor divestment progress, and what drove the Electrominerals volume vs price split?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has a couple of options after discussions with South African partners and aims to close the Foskor process by Q2; a fuller update is promised then. Electrominerals growth was mostly volume and product mix (treated products), with very little or no price increase.

qa_highlights.question: Harshit: Why was Abrasives margin under pressure if Electrominerals prices were not up significantly?
qa_highlights.answer: Grains (80-85% of COGS) rose only 3-5% and were offset by normal price increases; the pressure came from oil-linked inputs such as resins, which rose sharply in May and June with oil reaching about $117 a barrel, plus fuel costs.

qa_highlights.question: Amit Anwani (PL Capital): What is the strategic view on VAW Russia, its utilisation and sales update, and SOFC contribution and volume vs price in the 11-12% comparable guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No change in Russian business, which remains domestic-focused; management's aim is to stay put, comply with laws and serve the domestic market. Full-year growth is expected to be predominantly volume-driven with normal price increases; no individual SOFC split was shared, and pricing beyond normal will be decided one quarter at a time.

qa_highlights.question: Varun Jain (Dolat): Excluding the Sterling gain, consolidated Abrasives margin is about 2.5% versus 9-10% guidance; what is the comment, and what is the CAPEX breakdown and unallocated expense run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap is largely Awuko losses, which are still being incurred, so it holds the 9-10% guidance. Project-wise CAPEX split was not shared. Consolidated unallocable expense of INR 19 crores was mainly a forex loss versus a gain last year.

qa_highlights.question: Sajal Kapoor (Antifragile): How does the group distinguish a temporary setback from a signal to exit, and how does it make decisions in semiconductors and defence without operating history?
qa_highlights.answer: Awuko and Foskor were exited after management gave enough time; it waits at least four to eight quarters before deciding if a trend is temporary. For semicon, it is entering as a supplier of ceramics to fab equipment makers, building on 40-50 years of ceramics experience and working via anchor customers.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya (Kotak): How large are exports in standalone Electrominerals, and is European duty on Chinese imports a driver; what is the semicon 6N and substrate roadmap and any inorganic plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Export share has risen from about 20% earlier to 35% last year and is now on a path to 40%. Europe's duties are helping, with US and Asia efforts under way. 5N to 6N powder purity is being worked on; substrate benefits start FY28. Management said the focus is to remain a raw material supplier, with no inorganic plans stated.

risks_watch: Abrasives margin recovery: standalone Abrasives margin fell to 10.4% from 13.1% YoY; oil-linked resin and fuel cost push (about INR 16 crores) and whether normal price increases can offset it, given no further pricing is planned until the cost environment clears.
Awuko winding-up completion (guided within about a quarter) and the exceptional costs still to come; Q1 Abrasives losses from Awuko depress consolidated margins.
Foskor divestment or exit: options being explored, targeted to close by Q2; Q1 consolidated PBIT absorbed about INR 17 crores of Foskor loss.

Consolidated Ceramics margin: management expects the high end of 20.5-21% guidance, but standalone Ceramics PBIT was flat YoY on fuel, alumina and unabsorbed costs in new semicon and aerospace/defence lines.
Sustainability of Electrominerals export-led growth (33% standalone YoY) given that pricing was flat and the growth was mostly volume and mix.
VAW Russia: RUB sales down 14.1% YoY with geopolitical uncertainty; management says it is too difficult to predict and the aim is to stay put.
Unallocable costs: consolidated INR 19 crores in Q1 due to forex loss and lower interest income; forex swings may recur.
key_quotes: Growth at standalone level was broad-based and driven by all three segments.
So, it's going to be very tough and it's going to be tough for us to say that based on which we will start putting up price, etc., is also going to be tough.
We always wait at least four to eight quarters to see whether these are temporary trends or fundamentally things are changing.
Right now our focus is that we should be a raw material supplier and so we stay focused on that.

It repeatedly said the situation changes daily and that it will decide one quarter at a time, and declined to give CAPEX project splits or a SOFC breakdown.

rows.why: Standalone Abrasives margin fell to 10.4% from 13.1% YoY on about INR 16 crore resin, oil and fuel cost push, and management will not add price until costs clear; Ceramics is guided to the high end of 20.5-21%, and Abrasives 9.5-10% and Electrominerals 9-9.5% are held, so recovery depends on pricing and Awuko losses ending.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Metallized substrate facility with one anchor customer is to be commissioned in FY27 with revenue from FY28, and brown-fused alumina and furnace expansions are under way within the ~INR 400 crore FY27 capex; no project-wise timing or sizing was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Standalone sales grew 21.2% YoY with Electrominerals +33% and Abrasives +14.7% on volume; consolidated FY27 guidance is 4-4.5% reported but 11-12% comparable and possibly ~15% on the order book, and Ceramics was raised to 23-25%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Q1 consolidated capex was INR 53 crore and FY27 capex of ~INR 400 crore is held with the capacity programme under way; utilisation was not disclosed, so no new capex beyond the existing programme is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Ceramics growth guidance was raised to 23-25% from 15-15.5%, and management says consolidated comparable growth could reach about 15% on the order book, while Electrominerals could be 9-10% ex Foskor against 8-9% guided.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Abrasives margin was about 2.5% ex the Sterling gain and Awuko losses are still being incurred, against 9.5-10% guidance; oil-linked cost pressure (oil near $117 a barrel) and flat pricing could pull margins down further.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Semiconductor wafer fab components are small in FY27 and peak in FY30, aerospace and defence ramp from FY28, and the 5N to 6N powder purity move is in progress, with no specific launch dates given.

rows.label: Foskor divestment or exit and Awuko winding-up
rows.when: Q2 FY27 for Foskor update; Awuko completion within about a q
rows.why: Foskor absorbed about INR 17 crore of Q1 PBIT loss on ZAR 107 million sales (-14.7% QoQ), and Awuko is being wound up with a loss of EUR 1.69 million, with management promising updates in Q2.

rows.label: Abrasives pricing decision one quarter at a time
rows.why: Management will not pass on further price increases until the cost environment is clearer, against about INR 16 crore of resin, oil and fuel cost push in Q1.

rows.label: Electrominerals export share rising to 40%
rows.why: Export share rose from about 35% to about 40% of segment sales, helped by European duties on Chinese imports, with US and Asia efforts under way, and Electrominerals PBIT rose to INR 39 crore from INR 7 crore.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth and the raised Ceramics guidance, but cautious and at times evasive on pricing, the cost outlook, and project-level capex and SOFC splits; analysts pushed on the Abrasives margin gap, Foskor and Awuko, and semicon and defence entry without operating history.

513375|2026-09.headline: Carborundum Q2 FY27 standalone sales rose 28% YoY to INR 911 crores, a record, while consolidated PAT fell to INR 12 crores on INR 80.3 crores of exceptional items.
513375|2026-09.overview: Standalone sales hit a record INR 911 crores (+28% YoY, +7.7% QoQ), with all three segments growing double digits in H1. Consolidated sales rose 13.1% YoY to INR 1,455 crores, but consolidated PAT after NCI fell to INR 12 crores from INR 75 crores, driven by INR 80.3 crores of exceptional items linked to AWUKO closure and Foskor Zirconia. Management raised FY27 Ceramics guidance to 25-28% growth and margin to 22.5-23.5%, but cut Abrasives margin guidance to 8-8.5% excluding AWUKO. Operating cash flow was weak in H1 on working capital build, which management expects to reverse in H2.

financial_highlights.change: +12.4% YoY; down from INR 88 crores in Q1 FY27
vs INR 75 crores in Q2 FY26; after INR 80.3 crores exceptional items
vs INR 162 crores in H1 FY26
debt INR 362 crores, cash INR 251 crores; D/E 0.09

segments.name: Standalone Ceramics
segments.commentary: Sales INR 313 crores (+37.2% YoY, +14% QoQ); PBIT INR 67 crores (+48.2% YoY). Growth led by Engineered Ceramics and Metallized Cylinders, with refractories also contributing.

segments.name: Standalone Electrominerals
segments.commentary: Sales INR 279 crores (+31.3% YoY, flat QoQ); PBIT INR 29 crores (+49.1% YoY, down 24% QoQ from INR 39 crores). Management cited product and industry mix for the QoQ margin drop.

segments.name: Standalone Abrasives
segments.commentary: Sales INR 357 crores (+15.9% YoY, +8.6% QoQ); PBIT INR 37 crores (-19.9% YoY), margin around 10%. Cost pressure from phenolic resins and oil-linked inputs, with only a small pass-through.

segments.name: Consolidated Ceramics
segments.commentary: Sales INR 410 crores (+36.1% YoY, +17.6% QoQ); PBIT INR 101 crores (+62.1% YoY). Growth across India, Americas and Australia.

segments.name: Consolidated Electrominerals
segments.commentary: Sales INR 443 crores (+11.1% YoY, -6.3% QoQ) due to lower Foskor Zirconia sales; PBIT INR 26 crores (-20.9% YoY).

segments.name: Consolidated Abrasives
segments.commentary: Sales INR 607 crores (+4% YoY); PBIT INR 40 crores (+20.8% YoY). RHODIUS sales EUR 14.5 million (-16.8% YoY) with loss of EUR 0.3 million; AWUKO sales EUR 1.1 million vs EUR 2.9 million.

segments.name: VAW Russia
segments.commentary: Q2 sales RUB 1.55 billion, flat YoY; PAT RUB 98.7 million vs RUB 222 million a year earlier, up from RUB 52.1 million in Q1.

segments.name: Foskor Zirconia
segments.commentary: Under closure as commercially unviable; Q2 sales ZAR 53 million and loss of ZAR 24 million.

guidance_outlook: Consolidated sales growth FY27 approx 4-4.5% as reported; 11-12% excluding Foskor and AWUKO (INR 343 crores in FY26). Revised earlier guidance of 15% retained.
Consolidated Ceramics sales growth raised to 25-28% (from 23-25%); Ceramics margin raised to 22.5-23.5% (from 20.5-21%).
Consolidated Abrasives sales growth 5.5-6% as reported, 11-12% excluding AWUKO (about INR 108 crores). Abrasives margin 8-8.5% excluding AWUKO, down from 9.5-10% guidance.
Consolidated Electrominerals sales decline 6.5-7% as reported; 8-9% ex-Foskor. Prior 9-10% revision retained. Margin guidance 9-9.5% retained.
Consolidated capex guidance of INR 400 crores retained.
RHODIUS: FY27 sales now expected flat YoY (previously +5%), with a smaller loss than FY26; breakeven targeted by Q1 FY28.
Semiconductor equipment components segment: top line of INR 300-350 crores expected around FY30-31; segment margins to be above the 20-21% baseline in a stable state.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex INR 127 crores vs INR 162 crores in H1 FY26; FY27 consolidated capex guidance INR 400 crores retained.

Armor line capex of about INR 50 crores mentioned; electronic substrate (AMB/DBC) program in trials, first articles expected this year; management said at least a year before completion and gave no revenue figure.
Hosur thin wheel facility established to absorb the Uttarakhand thin wheel operations; qualification under way with 6-7 major international customers.
AWUKO sold property, plant, equipment and inventory for INR 5.34 crores; liquidation and de-registration in progress. Foskor exit expected to be completed in the current quarter, per management.
demand_pricing: Standalone Abrasives growth was mainly volume-driven, with a small price contribution; demand supported by industrial, construction and infrastructure activity.
Abrasives cost pressure from phenolic resins and oil-linked inputs; only a small portion passed to market, with management calling it largely timing. Management expects margins to recover toward 15%.
Ceramics exports are about 85%+ of sales; growth led by Engineered Ceramics (including Bloom-related products) and Metallized Cylinders, while wear ceramics also grew.
Refractories: demand strong in project orders, focused on high-temperature segment rather than consumables.

Chinese competition persists in Abrasives and Electrominerals, but is easing with export duty rebate withdrawal and a strong dollar/weak rupee making imports costlier. Electrominerals treated and specialty products are a value-add mix shift.
Foskor Zirconia supply to be replaced by an existing independent source; management says no disruption.

qa_highlights.question: Where is Ceramics growth coming from, and is export growth driving it?
qa_highlights.answer: Engineered Ceramics (including Bloom-related products) and Metallized Cylinders are the two growth drivers; bare ceramics grew less. Exports are typically 85%+ of Ceramics sales and that ratio held.

qa_highlights.question: Why did AWUKO/Foskor exceptional items arise and are more write-offs expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no further AWUKO write-offs are expected; the Foskor exit is on a realisable basis and no extraordinary write-offs are seen, though options are being explored. RHODIUS does not need a write-off.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin outlook for standalone Abrasives?
qa_highlights.answer: Management views margins as bottomed out at about 10%, with a normal trajectory of 15% to 16%, and is working on pass-through of resin and oil cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: Why is H1 operating cash flow weak and will it reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivables rose on strong September sales collected in October-November, and inventory was built for H2 growth. Management expects both to reverse in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What revenue potential exists in semiconductor components and electronic substrates?
qa_highlights.answer: Semiconductor components segment top line of INR 300-350 crores around FY30-31. Electronics substrate timelines are still uncertain; management said at least a year to complete base work and would share later.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for RHODIUS?
qa_highlights.answer: Breakeven targeted by Q1 FY28, followed by small profits. Sales expected flat in FY27 and the loss lower than FY26, after a warehouse move that disrupted the prior year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of VAW Russia volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Status quo: operations remain under the same constraints, with no volume improvement expected in H2.

risks_watch: Abrasives margin compression: standalone PBIT margin near 10% over two quarters; recovery depends on passing through resin and oil-linked cost increases.
Working capital: H1 operating cash flow weak; receivables and inventory build must unwind in H2.
Foskor Zirconia exit and AWUKO liquidation: completion timing and any residual impact; management says none expected.
RHODIUS breakeven target by Q1 FY28; FY27 sales guided flat.
Ceramics growth guidance raised to 25-28%; sustainability depends on Engineered Ceramics and Metallized Cylinders demand.
Chinese import competition in Electrominerals and Abrasives; import pressure may ease with duty changes and currency.
Electronics substrate and armor programs: revenue and timing not yet quantified.

These are specific issues that we are facing largely because of the sudden cost increases, particularly on the phenolic resins, all the oil-based products, and that cost, and of course, you don't stock these items much.
So electronics, we would feel that we should require some more time.
Sridharan Rangarajan: Yes. I think your observation is correct, and this should get reversed in H2, is our view.
We expect the top line from this segment could be somewhere in the range of about INR 300 crores to INR 350 crores.
513375|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on operations and demand: management repeatedly stressed record standalone sales, strong Ceramics momentum and raised Ceramics guidance. Cautious and evasive on Abrasives margins (passing through resin and oil costs is still a work in progress), on AWUKO and Foskor write-offs (said "not really" but left options open), and on electronics substrate and armor timelines, which were deferred with no revenue figure.

513472|2026-03.headline: Simplex Castings FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 18% to Rs 202 crore and PAT 40.5% to Rs 21.26 crore; FY27 target Rs 300 crore.
513472|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 consolidated revenue up about 18% to Rs 202 crore, EBITDA up 20% to Rs 37.39 crore with margin expansion, and PAT up 40.5% to Rs 21.26 crore. Q4 revenue was slightly below the prior-year Q4 (about Rs 67 crore cited by an analyst), which management attributed to customer site delays and LPG/gas supply disruptions that held back dispatches. The company received RDSO approval to restart wagon bogie manufacturing, with cast bogie capacity of 200-250 sets a month now built. Management guided FY27 revenue of Rs 300 crore and a FY28 aspiration of Rs 500 crore, contingent on execution, acquisitions/EPC and railway orders.

segments.name: Railways (cast and fabricated bogies)
segments.commentary: RDSO approval received to restart wagon bogies; 200-250 cast bogies a month capacity built. Cast bogie sale value about Rs 3.5 lakh per bogie, about Rs 7-8 lakh per wagon. Developmental order for fabricated loco bogies; FY27 target Rs 50 crore from cast railway business.

segments.name: Power
segments.commentary: Management targets about Rs 50 crore from power in FY27, linked to BHEL and L&T orders for 32 and 16 coal-based thermal plants to be commissioned by 2032.

segments.name: Steel (coke oven doors and castings)
segments.commentary: Coke oven door segment estimated at Rs 50-60 crore of about Rs 200-220 crore revenue; management claims about 70% share of India's coke oven doors and expects growth toward Rs 100 crore over 2-3 years. Recent orders from SMS and Thyssen for SAIL stamp-charging batteries.

segments.name: Defence and shipbuilding
segments.commentary: Supplies A-brackets, B-brackets and stern boss castings to shipyards and components to Gun Carriage Factory Jabalpur (Dhanush). Management says margins above 10% but segment, with other rest-of-business, expected at only 15-20% of revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target Rs 300 crore: about Rs 200 crore from existing business (stated as already closed), Rs 50 crore from cast railway business and about Rs 50 crore from power.
FY27 margins guided similar to FY26; cost-reduction gains expected to show in Q3-Q4 FY27.
EBITDA/PAT margin floor of 8-10% reiterated as minimum goal.
FY28 revenue aspiration of about Rs 500 crore, dependent on execution, acquisition and EPC, and railway orders.
FY27 capex planned at Rs 25 crore.
Expects an order of 100-200 bogies within about a month and consistent 200-bogie production from September onwards.
capex_capacity: Cast bogie capacity of 200-250 sets a month built under the first preferential issue; in CWIP until commercial production and prototype/first order.
Second preferential issue of about Rs 50 crore; about half earmarked for fabricated bogie facilities (Rs 25 crore capital and Rs 25 crore working capital).
FY27 capex target Rs 25 crore; FY26 capex about Rs 15 crore.
Spare land available at both Bhilai and Rajnandgaon units for expansion and semi-mechanisation.
Centrifugal rolls project (Rs 1.5-2 crore investment) dropped after market survey.
demand_pricing: Wagon bogies: wagon makers about 70-75% of market and railways spares about 20-25%; management targets both channels.
Possible wagon mega-order: management estimates 6,000 bogies (about 2 tonnes cast weight each) for 8,000-10,000 wagons over 3 years, with 20-30% typically outsourced.

Coke oven doors: India has an estimated 150-180 batteries; replacement demand about 3-4% a year; order flow of 2-3 batteries a year, plus about 70-80 batteries for planned 140 million tonne capacity expansion by 2030-2040.
Power and steel demand strong; management says it has become choosy on orders.
Gas (LPG) supply disruptions hit fabrication plants and top line in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 revenue fall YoY versus last Q4 (about Rs 67 crore), and what drove margins higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said dispatches slipped because customer site activity was delayed, leaving finished goods inventory that was expected to be realised in April-May. Gas (LPG) shortages also hit fabrication plants. Management said the margin goal is at least 8-10%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company supply full bogies or only parts, and what is the realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: The company assembles bogies from its own castings plus outsourced springs, side bearers, brakes and pads. Cast bogie sale value is about Rs 3.5 lakh per bogie, about Rs 7-8 lakh per wagon. Couplers and draft gears are planned later.

qa_highlights.question: When will orders from RDSO approval arrive and is further capex needed?
qa_highlights.answer: An order of 100-200 bogies is expected in about a month. No further capex is needed for the cast bogie line; it is awaiting the prototype and first order.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 targets, margins, acquisitions and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue target is Rs 300 crore, with margins similar to FY26. Two acquisition talks remain open after one failed; they are in the same line of business. FY27 capex is Rs 25 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the coke oven door market size and share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimates 150-180 batteries in India, 3-4% annual replacement, and about 70% market share. Coke oven doors are about Rs 50-60 crore of revenue, with growth to about Rs 100 crore expected over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY28 Rs 500 crore target risk and how will it be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Risks are execution, acquisitions/EPC and railway orders. Management said acquisitions in India had prohibitive multiples, so it is looking abroad in steel, power or railways, size about Rs 20-100 crore. Funding may come from debt or equity; the second preferential issue is a Rs 50 crore part of that.

risks_watch: Execution capacity and workforce availability; management plans to skill local labour and mechanise.
Gas/LPG supply and steel price volatility disrupting fabrication and dispatches.
Customer site delays pushing dispatches and inventory across quarters.
Funding for the fabricated bogie and FY28 plan; the second preferential issue (about Rs 50 crore) may need to be supplemented by debt or equity.
Acquisition pipeline: one deal failed on valuations; two remain open with unclear size and funding.
Dependence on the wagon mega-order and RDSO-approved bogie orders for the FY27 railway contribution.

513472|2026-06.headline: Simplex Castings Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 35% YoY to ₹60.95 crore and PAT rose about 45% to ₹6.86 crore, with near-term order book at ~₹150 crore.
513472|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was ₹60.95 crore, up about 35% YoY from ₹45.21 crore and up 11% QoQ from ₹54.76 crore. EBITDA rose about 25% YoY to ₹11.52 crore, with margin of 18.89%, and PAT rose about 45% YoY to ₹6.86 crore (PAT margin 11.25% vs 10.48%). Management said the near-term order book has expanded to roughly ₹150 crore+ from a historical ₹80–100 crore range. Management guided to ~₹300 crore FY27 revenue and ~₹500 crore by FY28, and flagged working capital reduction as a FY27 transition priority.

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Not yet contributing; management targets more than ₹100 crore next year from railway business, including casted bogies (~200 per month capacity conditional on wagon orders) and fabricated locomotive bogies at Tedesara expected at ₹60–70 crore turnover.

segments.name: Power sector fabrication
segments.commentary: No power/BHL orders in last year; management targets ~₹100 crore from power sector next year via orders secured through RXIL with BHL and L&T.

segments.name: Shipbuilding (Mazgaon Dock)
segments.commentary: First order of 5 sets about ₹4.5 crore; 3 sets already cast and first offered for inspection. A further pipeline order is about ₹8 crore.

segments.name: Steel and metallurgical
segments.commentary: Steel is the core market; management says ~₹300 crore of FY27 revenue will be fed by steel sector. Non-ferrous is about 20% of order book.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Target 5–10% of business in FY27 (with shipbuilding, 10–15%), working first with one ordnance factory (Khamaria, Jabalpur); not expected to grow 20–30%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance ~₹300 crore; management says ₹60 crore done in Q1 and balance ~₹150 crore order book to be executed in FY27, plus pipeline orders by March.

Revenue target of ~₹500 crore by FY28; management says the current fundraise is sufficient to reach this, and expansion beyond existing two units (~₹300–350 crore capacity) will come via organic or inorganic routes.
Capacity utilisation currently 50–60%, targeted at least 80% by end of FY28.
Working capital: FY27 described as transition year; target operating cycle of 60–70 days by FY28 from about 100–120 days today.
Fabrication capacity expansion of 1,500 tons per month (~18,000 tons annual) versus ~6,000 tons currently being done, implying an addition of 6,000–8,000 tons.
EPC business to be restarted selectively: order sizes ₹100–150 crore, ~2-year execution, minimum margin 15–20%, targeting about ₹100 crore annual revenue, funded from bank limits and accruals.
capex_capacity: Capex in progress at Tedesara (Rajnandgaon) unit, expected to complete in FY27; CWIP about ₹30 crore incl. working capital.
Fabrication expansion: 1,500 tons per month capacity addition, roughly 18,000 tons per year, for power and fabricated bogies.
Foundry is debottlenecking only: one CNC machine at ₹4–5 crore plus conveyors and cranes; machine moulding plant only on drawing board.
Capacity utilisation 50–60% currently; targeted 80% by end FY28.
Future capacity beyond current two units is not yet committed; management says investments will be funded from internal accruals, not new borrowings.
demand_pricing: Order book near-term ~₹150 crore+; management intends to keep it at ₹100–150 crore to limit liquidated damages (typically capped at 5%, some up to 10%).

Working capital: product mix shift at Unit 1 toward fast-moving, shorter-cycle products; Unit 3 to follow. Railway bogie cycle 30–45 days; RXIL and Invoice Mart discounting payments in ~30–35 days after dispatch at ~5–5.5% discount rate.
Steel demand supported by ArcelorMittal expansions (two in Odisha, one in Andhra Pradesh); management says steel boom expected to last 4–5 years.
Non-ferrous and metallurgical (Balco, Vedanta, Hindustan Zinc, Nalco, Aditya Birla) about 20% of order book.
Competition from Shyam Metalics and Rungta also expanding; management says Simplex is one of few large players in Bhilai.

qa_highlights.question: Current capacity utilisation and target?
qa_highlights.answer: Running at roughly 50–60%; targeting at least 80% by end of next financial year, with gradual increase starting this year.

qa_highlights.question: Is ₹300 crore FY27 revenue guidance on track?
qa_highlights.answer: ₹60 crore done in Q1, with ~₹150 crore order book to execute in FY27 and pipeline orders to come by March; management said ₹300 crore is in line.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital fall from 60–90 days (or 100–120 days) to target levels, and what is the margin cost of invoice discounting?
qa_highlights.answer: Shift to railway bogies (30–45 day cycle, payment upfront from wagon builders) and RXIL/Invoice Mart (30–35 days post dispatch). Discounting costs about 5–5.5%. Management said ₹300 crore revenue would need only about ₹50 crore working capital at 60 days.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins fall as railway and power fabrication (tender-based) grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management conceded railway and power fabrication will be at similar margins to today, not higher; margin uplift will come from selecting more complex, niche products.

qa_highlights.question: Is the fundraise sufficient to reach ₹500 crore, and any further borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current fundraise is sufficient for the ₹500 crore projection; further expansion will be funded only from internal accruals.

qa_highlights.question: Green hydrogen DRI project status?
qa_highlights.answer: Project closed. Grant of ~₹160 crore was subject to GST (~₹30–35 crore) because of IP and asset-sharing conditions; the reissued tender required an operating DRI plant, so Simplex did not bid.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term opportunities beyond ₹500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Too early to detail; areas mentioned include machine tool castings, defence and possible technology JVs or acquisitions; management reiterated no concrete plans yet.

Deployed in working capital and capex

Wheel hub line: due end Q2 FY27, relies on shifting existing machines and some special-purpose machinery still to be procured; ₹20 crore potential is samples-stage.
Customer concentration: top five customers 30-40% of revenue; conrod growth depends on three customers' share-of-wallet gains.
Equity raise planned with promoter participation; no quantum or timing given; debt repayment use unquantified.

Management says machining capacity to reach 3 lakh/month by end FY27 (from 1.8 lakh at 90-95% utilised), so capex execution is key.
key_quotes: Q1 FY27 PAT is a normalised PAT and reflects the true trend of growing profitability.
We are targeting internally 20% as an EBITDA margin over the coming quarters, and this is in line with our industry benchmarks.
We do have plans to raise equity in the future.
So we would use some of the equity to repay debt, but it's too soon to state any numbers at this point.

513517|2026-03.headline: Steelcast FY26 revenue rose 13.33% to ₹423.17 crore and PAT 20.31% to ₹86.86 crore; management guides 20%+ volume growth for FY27.
513517|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations reached ₹423.17 crore (up 13.33% YoY), EBITDA ₹129.64 crore (margin 30.64%, up 104 bps) and PAT ₹86.86 crore (up 20.31%). Q4FY26 revenue of ₹112.43 crore rose 15.43% QoQ, with EBITDA ₹34.25 crore and PAT ₹23.18 crore, but management acknowledged volumes and revenue were below the prior-year quarter. Margin pressure in Q4 came from higher maintenance, power and energy costs (fuel prices), and export-related provisions, with raw material costs up about 10% since March 1. Management said the capacity expansion decision will be taken by end-July 2026 instead of December 2026, citing stronger customer indications.

financial_highlights.change: +20.31% YoY from ₹72.20 crore; margin +119 bps from 19.34%

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports contributed over 60% of FY26 revenue and outperformed domestic business in both the quarter and the full year; North America and developed markets were steady, with new engagement from global OEMs.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Domestic business grew sequentially in Q4FY26 but trailed exports; management did not give a separate domestic revenue figure.

segments.name: Ground engaging tools (GET)
segments.commentary: GET was 1.1% of FY26 sales; management plans to take it to 3.8% in FY27 from existing customers.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Management has shifted focus away from defence; repeat overseas orders for compact-vehicle parts (prototypes approved, awaiting serial supply) could yield ₹15-18 crore in sales if they materialise.

guidance_outlook: Management targets 20%+ volume growth in FY27 and sees 20%+ cumulative annual growth through FY29; the PAT aspiration is more than ₹100 crore in FY27 (described as an aspiration, not guidance).
Sustainable EBITDA margin of 25-26% is seen as realistic over the longer term, though levels nearer 30% may occur at times.
Raw material costs rose about 10% from March 1; price pass-through of 4-5% expected, with partial compensation from April 1 and the balance from July 1. Management expects to be largely covered.
Aspiration to double sales by FY29 versus FY26 using present capacity (cited as ~₹860 crore in FY29).
2.4 MW hybrid power project due for commissioning by June 2026, with expected annual savings of ~₹3.6 crore.
capex_capacity: Capacity expansion decision to be taken by end-July 2026 (previously contemplated by December 2026); exact size and numbers to be shared then, and management said it is about halfway through the exercise.
Current-year capacity utilisation expected at about 63-64%; management no longer plans to wait for 75% utilisation before expanding.
Over 50 new parts are at various development stages; new parts are moving into serial supply, which management says is significantly accelerating in the last 4-6 weeks.
Part weight range within existing capability is 5 kg to 2,500 kg.
Order book for Q1FY27 is about ₹130-135 crore as of 1 April, with a typical cycle of 110-120 days.
demand_pricing: Management says realisations are steady; sales price variation formulas with all customers allow cost increases to be passed through automatically (and cost decreases passed back).

Exports are supported by supply-chain diversification (China+1) and steady North American demand; some serial orders from overseas are delayed by the Iran-US conflict, with management expecting them in one to two quarters.
Management sees no significant data-centre demand for steel castings.

Target end markets are mining, earthmoving, construction, locomotives, railroad and ground engaging tools. Railroad development has faced unresolved challenges; competition is more favourable in the other segments.
Working capital cycles are generally 75-110 days; the blended receivables are about 90-95 days per an analyst's reading of the company's figures.

qa_highlights.question: Will domestic demand rise from data-centre capex, and will defence exports expand to new geographies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said data centres need practically no steel castings, so no meaningful demand uplift is expected. Overseas defence parts are approved and await serial orders, expected within one or two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will capex now proceed before 75% utilisation, given demand visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; current utilisation is about 63-64%, and the company will decide on expansion by end-July 2026 instead of December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of cost increases and pass-through on realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material costs rose about 10%, with a 4-5% sales price impact; partial compensation applied from April 1 and the rest from July 1. Realisations remain steady under variation formulas.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin outlook 25-26% or 28-30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 25-26% is the more realistic sustainable EBITDA margin over the longer term, though levels near 30% can occur at times.

qa_highlights.question: What is the contribution expected from GET in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: GET was 1.1% of FY26 sales; the company plans 3.8% in FY27 from existing customers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company going to disclose a more detailed revenue breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed to add sector-wise and granular export breakdowns from Q1FY27.

risks_watch: Q4FY26 showed margin pressure from maintenance, power and fuel costs; the pass-through timing (July 1 balance) and rupee depreciation will determine the Q1FY27 margin.
Railroad development problems remain unresolved, and management did not quantify the impact.
Delays in overseas serial orders linked to the Iran-US conflict; the defence order sizing (₹15-18 crore) depends on conversion.
Capacity expansion decision and sizing due end-July 2026; capex project cost and timeline not yet disclosed.
Management clarified the PAT ₹100 crore goal is an aspiration with no firm date, and the 20% growth refers to volume, not PAT; investors should not read it as PAT guidance.

513517|2026-06.headline: Steelcast Q1 FY27 revenue rose 17% to INR124.82 crores and PAT 19.26% to INR23.71 crores; management guides 25-30% FY27 volume growth.
513517|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR124.82 crores, up 17% YoY, with EBITDA of INR35.24 crores (28.23% margin vs 28.14%) and PAT of INR23.71 crores (19% margin vs 18.64%). Management said input-cost increases will be passed through via sales price variation formulas, with the bulk of the price correction effective 1 July. Capacity utilisation was 66% in April-June, and a greenfield foundry of 8,500 tonnes (about INR120 crores over two years) was approved, targeted for commissioning by 31 March FY28. The order book stood at INR140 crores, roughly 3-4 months of forward booking.

financial_highlights.change: Export share 60% by tonnage (management also cited 62% by value)
Not quantified vs last year; management said it is higher

segments.name: Sector mix (sales, current year guidance)
segments.commentary: Mining about 27%, earthmoving about 43%, construction about 15%, defense about 1%, with the remainder across other sectors. Ten years ago mining was about 84% of sales, earthmoving near zero and construction 15-16%.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Exports have historically run at 45-50% of sales; FY27 guided at about 49-50% exports, and the next year at 47% exports and 53% domestic. Sales now go to about 16 countries; the US and Germany together are about 70% of exports.

segments.name: Ground engaging tools (GET)
segments.commentary: Under 1% of revenue today, with FY26 at about 1%; guided to about 3.5% of sales in FY27 and 4.5-5% by FY29 as new parts move into serial supply.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth guided at about 25% over FY26; in Q&A the chairman said 30% volume growth is a distinct possibility, and FY27 volume was implied at about 18,000 tons at 63% utilisation.
Long-term growth target of about 20% CAGR over the coming years.
Sequential quarter-on-quarter top-line improvement expected for several quarters.
EBITDA margin guided to stay in range; in Q&A the chairman said a 150-200 bps rise to 28.5-29% for FY27 is theoretically achievable and is the aim. FY27 margin was about 27%.
Price correction for input costs (raw materials and natural gas) effective 1 July, passed through under the sales price variation formula with a one-quarter lag.
Capacity utilisation target of 63% for FY27 and 90% by FY29 on existing capacity; management said above 90% is not advisable.
New facility revenue potential at peak about INR300 crores; commissioning target 31 March FY28.
Two renewable power projects (2.4 MW wind-solar hybrid and 1.4 MW solar) expected to be commissioned before 31 December 2026.
capex_capacity: Greenfield foundry of 8,500 tonnes approved by the Board, steel castings from 5 kg to 1,000 kg, planned investment about INR120 crores over two years, with an internal commissioning target of 31 March FY28.
Land of about 100,000 sq m provided by the Gujarat government; the new site is 12 km from the existing facility.
Existing capacity is about 29,000 tonnes; FY27 utilisation target is 63% and 90% by FY29.
Plan to start recruiting around mid-year for FY28 readiness; staff currently adequate for FY27 targets.
Considering shifting some manufacturing fuel from natural gas to electricity over 2-3 years; natural gas is about 50-55% more expensive than at end-February prices.
demand_pricing: Pricing is pass-through under a sales price variation formula with customers; the chairman said all major raw material increases will be recovered, but declined to give a percentage range.
Over 100 new parts developed in the last 18-24 months; about 20% of revenue expected from new parts over the next 2-3 years, with 80% from existing parts.
Management said US railroad work has been deprioritised in favour of better-priced industrial markets, and defense is a low priority because pricing is better elsewhere.
Rupee movements are shared with customers, not hedged.
Management says all 9 end-user sectors are seeing demand increases, with automobile growing 10-15%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the input-cost increase will be passed to customers, and how much is done so far?
qa_highlights.answer: Only a minimal correction took effect 1 April; most comes from 1 July. All major raw materials are in the formula, so the chairman said all increases will be passed on, without quantifying a range.

qa_highlights.question: Does the 25% growth mean volume or volume plus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth of 25%, with price increases on top; the chairman later said 30% volume growth is a distinct possibility.

qa_highlights.question: Will utilisation reach 100% by FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Target is 90% by FY29 on existing capacity, and new capacity starts adding volume afterwards.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin improvement and what is the new facility's peak revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly scale and operating leverage, with minimal price increase so far. Peak revenue potential from the new facility is about INR300 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company considering a rights issue or bonus issue, and is it focusing on defense?
qa_highlights.answer: Company has about INR120 crores of reserves and will fund the capex from internal accruals; a rights issue is not needed because it would dilute EPS. A bonus issue will be taken to the next Board meeting. Defense is deprioritised because it is a single-customer, higher-risk business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the segment split and how has it changed over 10 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Mining, earthmoving and construction together are about 70% of sales. Mining fell from about 84% to about 54% over 10 years, and earthmoving rose from near zero to about 36%.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk that exports are understated because of Tier 2 supply to OEMs?
qa_highlights.answer: The chairman said 98-99% of sales are direct Tier 1 supply to OEMs, and OEMs may export part of what they buy, so total export share may be a little higher.

risks_watch: Realisation of the 1 July price correction, which management says follows a one-quarter lag and has not been quantified.
Inventory build (WIP) during the ramp-up; management described it as a 1-2 month timing effect, to be watched in Q2.
Natural gas and energy cost volatility, with gas about 50-55% higher than end-February prices.
Concentration: the US and Germany account for about 70% of exports, and mining, earthmoving and construction for about 70% of sales.
Tracking of the 25-30% volume guidance and the INR140 crores order book against actual quarterly top line.
Israel defense component trials, which management expects to hear on in coming months.
Recruitment plan from mid-year for FY28 capacity.
key_quotes: And all the major raw materials are part of the formula, and we will be able to pass on everything, all increases.
So, quarter-on-quarter, you will see improved sales.
Yes, theoretically, that should happen, and this is what we are going to strive to achieve.
Yes, you are right. I did say 25%, I should have said 30% because indications from most of our customers are very strong.

513519|2026-03.headline: Pitti Engineering FY26 revenue rose 12% to INR1,953 crore and adjusted EBITDA 20% to INR326 crore, with a new INR290 crore casting capex announced.
513519|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 7% YoY to INR506 crore, but export shipments slipped as roughly INR20 crore of sales (largely export laminations and machine components) could not be dispatched in March due to container and energy disruptions. Full-year adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 17% from 15.9%, though Q4 margins were hit by a mid-quarter energy and commodity spike. Management announced a greenfield casting facility in Hyderabad (INR290 crore, casting capacity to 36,000 tons by Q1 FY30) and said Q1 FY27 will not be worse than Q4 but will not see a sharp recovery. Net debt is about INR570 crore, with a working-capital release of about INR125 crore expected.

segments.name: Traction motor and railway components
segments.commentary: 33% of FY26 revenue, down from 38% per analyst; Q4 absolute sales about INR165 crore vs INR178 crore a year earlier, attributed to about INR20 crore of export shipments slipping (Wabtec, Siemens Mobility).

segments.name: Power generation
segments.commentary: 15% of FY26 revenue; management describes demand as stable across DG sets, thermal and hydro plants.

segments.name: Industrial and commercial motors
segments.commentary: 13% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Special purpose motors
segments.commentary: 7% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Mining, oil and gas
segments.commentary: 6% of FY26 revenue; cited as a growth area in new product development.

segments.name: Renewable energy (wind)
segments.commentary: 3% of FY26 revenue; growth moderated but offset by data centers and industrial motors.

segments.name: Data centers
segments.commentary: 3% of FY26 revenue; three new data-center programmes added, with commercial revenue expected from Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Lamination and assemblies volume
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume 18,400 tons (+7.3% YoY); FY26 volume 69,517 tons (+10% YoY), with assemblies growing faster than loose lamination.

segments.name: Raw casting and machine components volume
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume 2,783 tons, with temporary year-end softness; FY26 volume 12,012 tons (+15.4% YoY).

guidance_outlook: FY27 targets: lamination sales of about 78,000 tons (about 72% of stated capacity) and machine components of about 16,000 tons; management estimates about INR2,300 crore top line at current commodity prices.
Consolidated lamination capacity is about 108,000 tons (no standalone/subsidiary split); no further lamination capex announced, and current capacity is sufficient to about FY28.
Q1 FY27 expected to be slightly slower than Q4 for both machine components and laminations, and not worse than Q4; no sharp recovery expected in Q1.

Working capital release of about INR125 crore expected as payables rise; net debt seen falling to about INR470 crore before current-year cash generation, and about INR250 crore by FY29 without further lamination capex.
Effective tax rate expected to remain around 33% for FY27 and FY28 due to ESOP, forex hedge accounting and depreciation differences; management did not give PAT guidance.

Maharashtra investment promotion subsidy (on about INR400 crore invested in Aurangabad over four years) may begin in FY27 under a 7-year recovery plan; company is seeking a 9-year plan or may defer accounting by one year.
ESOP cost of about INR10.3 crore per year continues in FY27 and then tapers off; a schedule is to be posted on the website.
capex_capacity: New greenfield casting and machine components facility in Hyderabad, adjacent to existing foundry, at INR290 crore; expected commissioning by Q1 FY30 (2 to 2.5 years), adding 11,400 tons and taking casting capacity to 36,000 tons.

Machine hour capacity to rise from 720,000 to 1.08 million hours, phased in from FY28 and FY29; about INR110-120 crore of the INR290 crore goes to the foundry and the rest to machining centres; allocation about 30% land and civil, 70% plant and machinery; asset turn about 1.2x.

Earlier capex (announced last year, INR150 crore): about INR100 crore spent as of 31 March 2026, with about INR50 crore pending; expected operational by end H1 FY27, debottlenecking casting capacity to 24,000 tons.
Capex funding: about INR100 crore from internal accruals, balance through net debt.
Q4 FY26 utilisation: sheet metal 80%, machining 87%, casting 64%; FY26 full year: sheet metal 76%, machining 81%, casting 71%.
demand_pricing: Quarterly price-change mechanism with international clients passes currency and commodity moves through; management says currency depreciation does not lift margins but helps India's cost competitiveness versus China.
Steel price exposure is managed by one month of raw material inventory and quarterly pricing offset; management says commodity hedging is not needed, while forex is 100% hedged.

Per-ton economics given: loose lamination about INR1.70-1.80 lakh/ton selling price; high value-added assembly about INR2.20-2.30 lakh/ton; raw casting EBITDA about INR30,000-35,000/ton; machined casting EBITDA about INR80,000-1 lakh/ton; loose lamination EBITDA about INR15,000-18,000/ton; high value-added assembly EBITDA about INR30,000-60,000/ton.
Mix: machine components about 80% export, 20% domestic; high value-added assemblies about one-third to 40% export; stator frame and rotor shaft assemblies roughly 50:50.
Management sees FY28 lamination volume of about 90,000 tons, of which about 60,000 tons loose and low value-added assemblies.

Export and new-customer pipeline: a competitor of an existing customer on a new export product from Q3 FY27; data-center casting and assemblies for Caterpillar, with commercial revenue expected from Q3 FY27; Progress Rail added as a customer; Siemens Mobility served via Dakshin Foundry; Alstom is an existing Indian customer.

517041|2026-03.headline: Ador Welding Q4 FY26: revenue up ~3% YoY, EBITDA ~INR38 crore (+200 bps), with management guiding to 100–200 bps further EBITDA margin gains.
517041|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 revenue growth of about 3% YoY, EBITDA of about INR38 crore (up 200 bps) and gross margin of about 36%, excluding the Kuwait recovery and exceptional items. For FY26, standalone revenue grew about 2%, gross margin rose about 250 bps to 38%, and the Kuwait recovery of INR14 crore lifted PBT to about INR130 crore excluding the Uran onerous cost. The Flares and Process Equipment division has been folded into a single welding segment, with loss-making large projects being wound down in favour of product-line business. Management declined to give formal guidance, but flagged Middle East dispatch disruption in March, a Saudi market that is now the third-largest export market, and a longer-term aspiration to triple earnings.

segments.name: Welding (consumables, equipment, MNR)
segments.commentary: Now the only reported segment after the Flares and Process Equipment division was merged in. Management says welding is growing roughly in line with steel consumption and that domestic India is about 80%+ of sales. Consumables and equipment are said to grow in similar cycles, with equipment spiking during capex upcycles.

segments.name: Flares and Process Equipment (PE)
segments.commentary: Folded into the welding business effective around end-March 2026 and run as product lines of INR20-30 crore. Management says there is no further loss, and that the Uran project is about 96-97% complete. The Q4 result included a INR3 crore gain from an ONGC reorder.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal guidance, but expects EBITDA margin to improve by a further 100-200 bps over coming periods, partly via gross margin, and sees it as feasible within FY27 barring severe supply shocks.
Aspirational target: revenue of INR2,000 crore by FY29 (roughly 25% CAGR) is still referenced, but management says the main principle is to triple earnings over the period.
Management's planning assumption is growth at least in line with IIP/GDP (6-8%), and it believes it can outperform that.
Capex is guided at about INR30-35 crore for FY27 (maintenance INR10-12 crore; two to three new consumable lines), possibly up to INR40 crore a year over the next two years.

Management says it would be feasible to reach INR1,500-1,600 crore of welding revenue by FY28 only if the economy stays strong, which implies about 18-20% growth a year; it has not committed to that figure.
Exports were flattish in FY26 (last year's total cited as about INR154 crore), with a better outlook from order book and approvals.
capex_capacity: Current utilisation is about 70% on a fair estimate, with some lines running at 90-95% and needing capex.
Normal sustainable operating range is cited as 70-90% depending on equipment age and technology.
Two to three new consumable lines are due this year and next, all in welding consumables rather than equipment.
Capex needed to double volume over five to seven years is estimated at INR100-150 crore (plant and machinery, excluding land).
demand_pricing: Demand is described as okay since November-December 2025, but customers are cautious because of inflation in steel and macro conditions.
Around 80-85% of sales go through distributors, so the order book is short-cycle and not a long backlog.

Middle East: March quarter dispatches were hit in the first three to four weeks by the situation there. Most of the pent-up volume was cleared by the end of the quarter, and management says demand remains good.
Saudi Arabia is now the third-largest export market (it was second last year), and inquiries from there have been healthier since December 2025.
Market share is put at about 17-18%, plus or minus a few percent.
Shipbuilding: management says it has approvals for about 75-80% of the required work, but it has not disclosed the revenue from that sector.
Management says it is seeing its best-ever welding automation order book, though the base is still small.
Steel: pricing and inflation are challenging, but management says the cycle is on a brighter footing.

qa_highlights.question: Why are process equipment losses continuing after one-off adjustments, and where does that finish?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no further negative. The INR3 crore Q4 gain came from an ONGC reorder, the FY26 hit was about INR25 crore, and the division has been restructured into product lines of INR20-30 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is 12% EBITDA margin sustainable, and what is the medium-term growth outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management treats ~12% as the base and aims for incremental, step-by-step improvement. It declined to share internal targets and gave no guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to INR1,500-1,600 crore of welding revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: That would need about 18-20% YoY growth for two years. Management says it is feasible if the economy stays strong, but it would not commit to a number.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East exposure and were dispatches affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Exposure is high for exports, but management says receivables are secure and demand is firm. March dispatches were hit in the first three to four weeks, and most of the backlog has since cleared.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 capex plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is about INR30-35 crore, with INR10-12 crore of maintenance. Two to three new consumable lines are coming, with the spend all in welding consumables.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company open to acquisitions, and what is the cash position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is open to acquisitions that are more targeted, focused on technology as well as market share. It has not announced any transaction and says the company has a healthy cash balance.

risks_watch: Middle East disruption to dispatches and supply, despite stated strong demand and secure distributor terms.
Steel and supply-chain inflation, which is making customers cautious on orders.
Uran project still at about 96-97% completion with commissioning delays, and a possible further ONGC recovery or LD impact.
Pending Indian income tax demand of about INR14 crore, under appeal; BIS magistrate court proceedings listed for June-July 2026.
Management's growth aspirations (INR2,000 crore by FY29; tripling earnings) are not backed by specific guidance.
Export volumes flat in FY26, and the company is reporting only one segment going forward, so less visibility on the breakdown.
517041|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on margins and the clean-up of legacy issues, but cautious and often evasive on forward numbers: management repeatedly declined to give guidance, targets, segment revenue or product-level breakdowns. It was most direct on the completed restructuring and Uran/Kuwait closure.
key_quotes: There is no further loss, there is a gain.
There is no further negative left. We took the biggest hit we did in Q1 and we are working towards recovery on what we can.
So far this year, what we have seen is the order book, inquiry base, and approvals where we are set up, exports should do better -- should do well, should do better for the markets we operate in.
We don't like to give guidance, but that is the way we look at it.

517041|2026-09.headline: Ador Welding Q2 FY27 revenue rose about 23% YoY to INR345 crores, but gross margin fell to 34.2% on steel-led input inflation.
517041|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew about 23% YoY to INR345 crores and H1 revenue rose 23% to INR654 crores, supported by infrastructure, power, oil and gas, railways, shipbuilding, defence and heavy fabrication demand. Gross margin fell to 34.2% as steel and other raw material costs rose sharply; management attributed about 80% of the dip to input inflation and 15-20% to aggressive growth and product mix. EBITDA grew 9% in the quarter and H1 EBITDA margin was 11.2%, slightly above last year. Management said calibrated price increases were taken, with pass-through lagging in Q2 and improving in Q3, and declared an interim dividend of INR7.5 per share.

financial_highlights.change: H1 at upper end of range
from about INR0.27 crores at FY26

segments.name: Consumables
segments.commentary: Management said consumables tend to have strong returns, depending on product mix; specialised high-performance products are being introduced for demanding applications. No segment revenue figures were given.

segments.name: Industrial M&R (Fontech)
segments.commentary: Management said Fontech is around INR220-230 crores in revenue, roughly flat to pre-merger levels, and that fabrication-related products were moved into the wider welding business. Growth expected at 8-12%, well below other markets.

segments.name: Equipment and automation
segments.commentary: Hypertherm master distribution in India for plasma cutting, Liburdi Dimetrics orbital welding tie-up, and WelDoS welder-data add-on. Automation margins are expected to take time to reach equipment and consumables levels.

segments.name: Flare segment
segments.commentary: Management said the flare segment is essentially exited, with revenue insignificant and no EBITDA losses in H1.

Gross margin ideally at least 36-38%, with recovery expected from Q3 FY27; management said early days in Q3.
Volume growth expected at high-single to double digits, with sales teams given aggressive H2 targets.
Aspiration of about INR2,000 crores revenue by FY29; management said the company is fairly on track.
Capex of about INR30-35 crores in FY27, with an elevated INR60-70 crores in FY27-28 before reverting to a normal INR35-40 crores a year; no debt or equity dilution planned.
capex_capacity: Normal annual capex is about INR35-40 crores, with FY27 at about INR30-35 crores.
FY27 and FY28 capex expected at INR60-70 crores, driven by investment in a new consumables line.
Management said the balance sheet is strong enough to fund the capex without debt or equity.
Five manufacturing units; management said investment is to modernise the base and support scaling.
demand_pricing: Steel prices rose about 7-8% QoQ in Q2 FY27 per management; other inputs such as copper, electronics/PCBs and imported components also rose, and freight added to import costs.
Price increases were taken in line with steel moves, with pass-through lagging due to timing and contracts; management said most is being passed through now.
Export mix: Middle East about 80-85% of exports (Dubai hub), plus the US, parts of Africa and two European markets with a third being entered.
Management said order book is confidential and declined to quantify it; shipbuilding opportunity described as significant.
Inventory and payables rose at 30 September: about 75-80% from order backlog and 15-20% from steel availability concerns.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable margin level and what drove the Q2 gross margin dip?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about 80% of the dip to input cost inflation and 15-20% to aggressive growth and product mix; sustainable EBITDA margin is 12-13%, with gross margin ideally 36-38%.

qa_highlights.question: What was the volume growth in Q2 and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth was about mid-teens in Q2; management expects it to continue, with aggressive targets for H2 and international markets offering upside.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR2,000 crore FY29 revenue target achievable and does the current capacity support it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company is fairly on track. It expects 60-70% of incremental growth to come from product mix, one-third from innovations, partnerships and automation, and noted capex of INR60-70 crores in FY27-28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did short-term borrowing rise to about INR28 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly LCs and BGs, plus a smaller working-capital component and strategic steel purchases; management said H1 should not be read as a trend.

qa_highlights.question: Are there acquisition plans in automation or robotics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said options are being explored in automation, but it is very early and the ecosystem is small, so nothing is imminent.

qa_highlights.question: Has the company's share of wallet with large customers improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said top 50 and top 100 customers are a focus area, with hiring and strategy in place, but this takes time; product gaps from the last 2-3 years have largely been plugged.

Pass-through lag and contract timing; Q3 gross margin recovery is the key test.
Working capital: inventory build and payables decline, plus rising short-term borrowing (about INR28 crores).
Export concentration: Middle East about 80-85% of exports.
Inorganic growth and automation acquisitions remain at an early exploration stage.

517059|2026-03.headline: Salzer Q4 FY26 revenue rose 26% YoY to INR 474 crore, but margins fell to 7% on petrochemical and copper cost pressure; FY27 EBITDA guidance is 9-9.5%.
517059|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 26% YoY to INR 474 crore, with EBITDA excluding other income of INR 31 crore (7% margin) and PAT of INR 10 crore. FY26 revenue rose 24% to INR 1,758 crore, but EBITDA margin was about 8% and PAT grew only 3% to INR 54 crore. Management attributed the margin squeeze to plastic (petrochemical-linked) cost increases of 2-3% of margin, copper and silver increases, freight and Middle East disruption. Working capital reached about 30% of revenue against a stated 25% ceiling, and management guided to a return to 25% in FY27.

financial_highlights.value: INR 60 crore / INR 8 crore / INR 5 crore

segments.commentary: 56% of FY26 revenue and 51% of Q4; grew 20% YoY in FY26 and 15% in Q4. EBITDA margin 11% in FY26 and 8% in Q4; management says switchgear gross margin is about 35-40%.

segments.commentary: About 5% of FY26 revenue and 6% of Q4; grew 16% YoY in FY26 and 36% in Q4.

segments.commentary: About INR 45 crore of business executed over the last year; no large long-term orders secured yet. Addressable market about 17 crore meters, with AMISP requirements of 2-3 crore meters under discussion. No FY27 smart meter guidance given.

segments.commentary: INR 200 crore Bangalore Corporation street-lighting automation project under execution; revenue expected to start in Q2 FY27 at a steady monthly run rate.

Margins expected to be under pressure in Q1 FY27 and stabilise from Q2 FY27; switchgear EBITDA margin expected at 12-13% from Q2 onwards.
Existing-business revenue expected at INR 2,000-2,100 crore in FY27, excluding smart meter upside.
June 2026 price increase of 7-10% across products, after a roughly 15% increase in February 2026; management expects 100% cost pass-through over the two increases.
Exports targeted at about 25% of FY27 revenue; Middle East and Africa exports of about INR 24 crore expected to double over FY27-28.
Interest cost expected to rise at least 10% in FY27 on higher working capital; depreciation flat. Average short-term borrowing cost about 8%.
Working capital to return to 25% or below of revenue in FY27; target ROCE of about 18%, with management implying 18-20% by FY30.
capex_capacity: Saudi Arabia manufacturing plant delayed about six months by the Middle East conflict from February 2026; capital equipment ordered, expected by August 2026, with operations from September or October 2026.

Aurawin SPV formed with a smart-metering market participant to act as a bidding company for future tenders.
Management said it is not yet giving a smart meter guidance and expects some orders, but is holding inventory currently.
demand_pricing: Management expects Indian electrical equipment market to grow at double digits over the next four to five years, driven by electrification, data centres, renewables, EV charging and smart meter rollout.

Price increase in February 2026 of about 15% did not fully offset costs; plastic price increase in Q4 to be offset only with the June 2026 price increase. Market accepted the February increase smoothly, per management.

Exports grew about 5% YoY in FY26; US tariffs cut exports about 6% and Middle East crisis reduced business by around 10-12%. Americas and Europe together make up about half of exports. UK benefits from favourable currency and zero import duty.

Competitive position: management says Salzer is in the top three in most products on quality and pricing, and commands a premium in some categories; competitors include foreign, Chinese and other country players.
Largest client concentration is Schneider Electric at about 12% of revenue (includes business formerly with L&T).

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management of the FY27 EBITDA margin guidance given recent price hikes and April volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance cut to 9-9.5% for FY27 (whole year). A further 7-10% price increase in June 2026 is planned; Q1 pressure expected, with margin stabilising in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the wires and cables EBITDA margin so low, and does the segment cover its interest cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly B2B (about 70% per the answer), and copper cost rise means a fixed absolute profit is now a lower percentage (margin was 6.5-7% a couple of years ago). Management said the business earns about 2-3% PAT after interest.

qa_highlights.question: Would management consider demerging wires and cables or other shareholder value unlocking steps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the suggestion was taken positively and would be looked at, with no commitment or timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Why has working capital and short-term debt risen, and when will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital reached about 30% of revenue versus a 25% ceiling, due to margin erosion, smart meter capex and slow scale-up. Management expects a return to 25% or below in FY27. Receivable days are 90-95 on net sales basis.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Saudi plant business model and investment?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant aimed at local content requirements in Saudi projects; delayed about six months; Phase-1 capex about INR 15 crore; target INR 100 crore revenue for GCC.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the EV charging business margins and revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently break-even due to low volumes; target EBITDA 12-15% at scale; FY27 revenue expected about INR 25 crore.

risks_watch: Petrochemical-linked plastic and copper/silver costs; Q1 FY27 margins expected to remain under pressure before the June price increase takes effect.
Working capital and short-term borrowing (INR 503 crore) versus the 25% of revenue target; interest cost expected to rise at least 10% in FY27.
Smart meter execution remains slow, with no large long-term orders secured and inventory being held.
Middle East conflict affecting Saudi plant timeline and exports; US tariffs reducing export volumes.
Saudi plant commissioning (August-October 2026) and the INR 200 crore Bangalore project revenue starting in Q2 FY27.
Shareholder value concerns over low wires and cables returns and the possible demerger, which management has not committed to.

517059|2026-06.headline: Salzer Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13% to INR498 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 6% and management cut FY27 EBITDA margin guidance to 8-8.5% from 10%.
517059|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 13% YoY to INR498 crore, led by industrial switchgear, wires and cables, and building products. EBITDA (excluding other income) fell to INR31 crore from INR42 crore, with margin at 6%, and PAT dropped to INR8 crore from INR17 crore (2% margin). Management attributed the compression to copper, silver and plastic input inflation with a lag in passing costs to customers in switchgear, which is not on a cost-plus model. Management now expects margins to normalise from Q3 with FY27 EBITDA around 8-8.5%.

517146|2026-03.headline: Usha Martin Q4 FY26 operating EBITDA rose 52% to INR 212 crore at a 21.6% margin on revenue up 9.3% to INR 979 crore.
517146|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 9.3% YoY to INR 979 crore, with operating EBITDA up 52% to INR 212 crore and margin at 21.6%, the highest since the steel business sale. FY26 revenue reached INR 3,691 crore (+6.2%) with operating EBITDA of INR 705 crore (19.1% margin vs 17.2%). Rope volume growth was only about 5% in Q4 because Middle East demand fell short by roughly 900 tons, and LRPC revenue fell 20.4%. 517146|2026-06.headline: Usha Martin Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 16.4% YoY to INR 1,033 crore and EBITDA grew 44% to INR 208 crore at a 20.1% margin.
517146|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 16.4% YoY to INR 1,033 crore, with operating EBITDA up 44% to INR 208 crore and margin up 380 bps YoY to 20.1%. Value grew faster than volume, driven by pass-through of input costs, a richer mix of value-added rope and plasticated LRPC, and a higher rope share. Wire rope volumes were marginally down as the Middle East fell about 28%, while India, the US and Europe grew. Operating cash flow was about INR 242 crore (116% of EBITDA), and free cash flow was INR 135 crore after INR 73 crore capex. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 10-12% rope volume growth and about 15% value growth, with a 20% minimum EBITDA margin base.

segments.commentary: Volumes up about 19% and revenue up about 32% YoY; largely domestic, with early European supply in automotive and rockfall protection. Wire realisation about INR 85,000 per ton.

First international plasticated LRPC order for stay cable applications. Blended black and plasticated realisation about INR 79,000 per ton; management flagged some realisation softness from monsoon and project slowdowns.

segments.commentary: Revenue has trended up for five consecutive quarters, now about GBP 2-3 million per year with a GBP 10 million target over the next few years. Gross margin 65-70%; estimated TAM INR 1.5-2 billion.

Europe contributed about 27% of revenue, and the US/Americas about 9-10%; US market share is below 5% and Europe about 10-12%.

rows.label: Plasticated LRPC FY27 volume ramp and domestic-share customer approval
rows.why: Verbal approval from a major domestic-share customer with paperwork pending; FY27 target of 3,500-4,000 tons vs ~2,500 tons in FY26 against 6,000 tons front-end capacity.

517206|2026-03.headline: Lumax FY26 revenue rose 23% to INR 4,184 crore with EBITDA margin at 9.8%; management guides FY27 margin 10.5-11%.
