qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 margins hold given input cost volatility and the pass-through lag?
qa_highlights.answer: No precise FY27 guidance given due to volatility. Full-year EBITDA margin still seen at 10.5-11%, with monthly price amendment talks underway with some OEMs to shorten the roughly one-quarter lag.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for mould/tooling revenue?

517206|2026-06.headline: Lumax Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 32.6% y-o-y to INR 1,223 crore, with EBITDA margin flat at 9.2% as commodity recoveries slipped into Q2.
517206|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 32.6% y-o-y to INR 1,223 crore and EBITDA rose 34% to INR 113 crore, with margin held at 9.2%, in line with Q1 FY26. PAT including associates rose 41.2% to INR 51 crore, at a 4.2% margin. Management said OEM price recoveries for West Asia-driven commodity and electronics costs were not realised in Q1 (about 150 bps margin drag) and are expected in Q2. FY27 capex guidance was raised to INR 200-250 crore from INR 100-150 crore on new order wins.

Order book about INR 2,500 crore (about 90% LED); about 60% (roughly INR 1,500 crore) to enter SOP in FY28. Maruti wallet share expected to rise from under 30% to 35-40%.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex raised to INR 200-250 crore from INR 100-150 crore, driven by order wins over the last four months; FY26 capex was INR 410 crore.

Brownfield projects underway at Sanand and Bawal to support new order wins at those locations.

demand_pricing: Industry Q1 production per SIAM: total 93.5 lakh units (+22% y-o-y); PV +17%, 2W +23%, 3W +39%, CV +15%.

Commodity recoveries: OEMs have not agreed to monthly amendments for most of the industry (only aluminium accepted); still quarterly or six-monthly. About 150 bps Q1 margin impact from unrealised recoveries.
Management expects competition intensity to rise as new players enter, but says top OEM concentration (4-5 players, 80-90% share) limits new entrants' share.
Content per vehicle for a passenger car currently INR 15,000-20,000 (outliers up to INR 30,000); management expects at least 50% growth over 4-5 years.
Honda HVAC business was about INR 18-20 crore annualised vs an estimated peak of INR 35-40 crore; Honda volumes weaker than expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin still below 10% despite LED penetration and localisation, and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Anmol Jain said OEMs have not agreed to monthly price amendments, so recoveries slipped; margin was hit about 150 bps in Q1. Realisations expected in Q2 could lift margin to about 10.5-11%, in line with FY27 guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why are CV and tractor orders not yet visible, and how is the company positioned on EV content?
qa_highlights.answer: Deepak Jain said CV lighting tech is standardised and the company is in talks on new platforms. Anmol Jain said CV is about 5% of revenue and grew 30-35% annualised. Lighting is powertrain-agnostic; EV content is higher in value per vehicle. 12% of order book is EV.

qa_highlights.question: Why did M&M revenue stay flat when the company holds a 40-50% wallet share?
qa_highlights.answer: Anmol Jain said the XUV700 EV platform, where Lumax is not present, drove Mahindra volumes; management expects full-year growth in line with Mahindra.

qa_highlights.question: What is the mould revenue outlook and FY27 capex split?
qa_highlights.answer: Mould sales are targeted at INR 250-300 crore (vs INR 180-185 crore), mostly in Q3/Q4. Maintenance capex is INR 40-50 crore; the rest goes to new business and capacity.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins expand 50-100 bps a year, and can 30% growth continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed about 100 bps expansion in FY27 (9.8% in FY26 to 10.5-11%). It said 30%+ quarterly growth will not persist due to high base; full-year growth guided at 15-20%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the localisation plans and tooling sourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: Deepak Jain said localisation is a priority but not all in-house; tooling remains imported, with tool localisation possibly by 2030. China sourcing continues for cost, with a new China office set up.

517206|2026-09.headline: Lumax Q2 FY27 revenue rose 33% y-o-y to INR 1,342 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 8.2% on raw-material pass-through lag; FY27 double-digit margin guidance retained.
517206|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue was INR 1,342 crore (+33% y-o-y, +10% q-o-q), with H1 revenue at INR 2,565 crore (+33% y-o-y). Consolidated EBITDA was INR 110 crore (+21% y-o-y) with margin of 8.2% versus 9.0% a year earlier, as West Asia-driven material and electronic component cost increases were only partly recovered from customers. PAT including associates was INR 52 crore (+46% y-o-y), margin 3.9%. Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 25%+ from 20%+ and kept the full-year double-digit EBITDA margin target, which depends on H2 recovery of escalations.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence in double-digit FY27 EBITDA margin given cost pressures and recovery lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 and Q2 escalations are being recovered in H2, no major further price hikes are expected, and operating leverage will help. H2 margin is expected at ~10.5-11%, lower in Q3 and higher in Q4; guidance is conditional on no major West Asia volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Will growth slow after the festive season, and what is the FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 growth will be well below H1's ~35% due to the high base, but q-o-q revenue should keep rising. FY27 growth is now 25%+; about 60% of the order book (~INR 1,500 crore) is due for SOP in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Is export a growth driver?
qa_highlights.answer: Export engagement with OEM international purchasing offices is ongoing, but it takes 2-3 years to convert; the domestic market remains the priority.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company compete with integrated ADAS/lighting players, and what technology roadmap exists?
qa_highlights.answer: ADB has no camera integration today. Management relies on Stanley for localized technology and on the Czech and Taiwan engineering centres for projection, OLED, DLP and laser technologies.

qa_highlights.question: What is the LED and PCB localization status, and does the company have PLI benefits?
qa_highlights.answer: Bare PCB ~60-70% localized, SMT in-house, connectors ~30-35%. Management clarified that auto lighting is not covered under the PLI scheme.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the Hyundai investment, and what is the role of the associate?
qa_highlights.answer: Hyundai business is handled by associate SL Lumax, so no direct impact on Lumax Industries. The company is talking to Hyundai directly about possible supply to them as a de-risking step.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the revenue growth in Q2?

Quarterly momentum was weaker in H2 because of state subsidy timing: management said Q4 gross margin was INR48.6 crore, INR3 crore below Q3. 517300|2026-06.headline: GIPCL guides FY27 EBITDA to Rs950-1,000 crore at full run-rate, anchored by 600 MW Khavda solar at 33% CUF and Rs355 crore EBITDA.

PPAs carry benchmark CUFs; penalties apply to GUVNL below the benchmark. Management says tariffs embed a margin over the CUF.
Management said Khavda CUF would be 29-30%+ annually, Raghanesda 28-29%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue, EBITDA and debt profile for the 600 MW Khavda asset?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue about Rs420 crore at 33% CUF, EBITDA Rs350-360 crore. Debt repayment starts after the one-year moratorium ended June 2026, with step-up repayment over the following years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 500 MW Khavda need more debt, and what is peak debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term borrowing about Rs4,500 crore post 500 MW commissioning; with thermal expansion, peak debt Rs6,000-6,500 crore. Full disbursement pending against contractor milestones.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY26 Q4 other income Rs42 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly insurance claims settled in FY26 plus Rs17 crore income tax refund, plus government grant amortisation and O&M contractor liquidated damages.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company looking at BESS and pump storage?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes: 120 MW BESS at Baroda gas site under GUVNL approval, with 160 MW planned later; pump storage is in the race for government sites.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 750 MW lignite expansion need equity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs4,800 crore would be 80:20 debt and Rs1,200 crore equity, funded via internal accruals over five years, promoter infusion, dilution or market raise; no firm plan yet.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 310 MW gas stations be revived or hived off?
qa_highlights.answer: Revival depends on gas prices and geopolitics. Management said the gas assets exist in the books but are technically idle, and hive-off is being considered over the next couple of years.

risks_watch: Khavda evacuation (CTUIL) dependency for the 500 MW phase; commissioning timing and teething losses could hit PBT.

Debt rising from ~Rs3,250 crore to ~Rs4,500 crore and then Rs6,000-6,500 crore with thermal; floating 7.8% coupon exposure.
Monsoon-season CUF dip in Q2 FY27 and the two-to-three-month lag in publishing PLF data.
Equity funding for the Rs1,200 crore equity component of the lignite project is undecided.

517300|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on operations and the Khavda ramp-up, but evasive and often approximate on numbers, frequently answering with rough ranges and promising follow-up. Caution is shown on evacuation timing, equity funding and gas-station revival.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: H2 FY27 onward, as 500 MW Khavda phase 2 comes online
rows.why: Solar EBITDA was Rs332 crore in FY26 and management guides company EBITDA of Rs950-1,000 crore at full run-rate, but only once the 500 MW phase is operational around end-2026; 600 MW Khavda CUF rose to 33.24% from about 23% in Q4 FY26 and it is guided to deliver Rs350-360 crore EBITDA in FY27.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2-Q3 FY27 (phased 200/200/100 MW, full by end-2026)
rows.why: 500 MW Khavda phase 2 has Rs2,065 crore CWIP and is contingent on CTUIL evacuation, with PGCIL connectivity expected end-July 2026 and mostly commissioned by end-2026; the CTUIL dependency is the main timing risk.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides about Rs450 crore FY27 top-line addition (Rs400-425 crore from 600 MW Khavda plus Rs30-40 crore from RE park), with Khavda CUF at 33.24% and expected 30%+ annual; much of the 500 MW volume lands after FY27 Q2 given evacuation timing.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.when: Next 2-4 quarters (BHEL order expected by end FY27 or Q4)
rows.why: Capex is already committed: Rs6,000 crore for 750 MW lignite (Rs4,800 crore debt, Rs1,200 crore equity), plus Rs250-300 crore BESS at Baroda and a 200 MW Khavda add at Rs800-1,000 crore, with peak debt guided Rs6,000-6,500 crore including thermal.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave FY27 EBITDA only at full 500 MW operation and said it would not appear fully in FY27; FY27 PBT guided only around Rs220 crore while interest rises to Rs250-270 crore and depreciation to Rs425-450 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Khavda 500 MW commissioning depends on CTUIL evacuation readiness (post-monsoon, around end-2026), and interest/depreciation roughly double (interest Rs107-110 crore currently vs Rs250-270 crore FY27) which compresses PBT; FY27 figures were given inconsistently across answers.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.when: Around one year from award for BESS; no date for pump storag
rows.why: 120 MW BESS at Baroda (Rs250-300 crore, GUVNL approved, tender in place) is about one year from operation and a further 160 MW is planned; pump storage sites are still being identified.

rows.label: 750 MW lignite expansion BHEL order
rows.why: Tender with BHEL under evaluation for Rs6,000 crore 750 MW lignite project, phased 2027-2032-33, with GUVNL approval in principle under Section 62 cost-plus.

rows.label: Debt rises before it falls
rows.why: Long-term borrowings Rs3,247-3,250 crore at 31 Mar 2026 rise to about Rs4,500 crore post 500 MW and Rs6,000-6,500 crore with thermal, at 7.8% floating; FY28 interest guided Rs400-450 crore.

rows.label: Khavda PGCIL connectivity and CTUIL evacuation
rows.when: End-July 2026 connectivity, installation from August, full b
rows.why: 500 MW phase 2 installation depends on PGCIL connectivity expected by end-July 2026 and CTUIL evacuation readiness, with Rs2,065 crore CWIP already sitting against it.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Khavda ramp-up (CUF 33.24% vs about 23% in Q4 FY26) and the 750 MW lignite plan, but cautious and approximate on FY27 numbers, CTUIL evacuation timing, lignite equity funding and gas-station revival; analysts pressed on interest, depreciation and peak debt.
